---
name: pi-subagents
description: |
  Technical guidance for operator-requested delegation to builtin or custom
  subagents: bounded handoffs, parallel review, scripted workflows, async work,
  forked context, isolation, and coordinated execution.
---

# Pi Subagents

The parent works directly by default. Invoke subagents only when the operator
requested delegation in the current request or through applicable user/project
instructions. Task size, complexity, risk, tool-call count, recipe fit, or an
available specialist does not independently authorize delegation.

Once authorized, choose the smallest bounded shape that earns its token and
elapsed-time overhead through concrete evidence, independent review,
specialization, useful parallelism, or needed isolation. A single child is
valid; writer, challenge, and review stages must each earn their overhead rather
than becoming default ceremony. The parent keeps user intent, constraints,
routing, arbitration, decisions, final acceptance, and publication authority,
and may perform the work directly where it is the most efficient owner.

Children do not spawn subagents unless the parent explicitly delegated fanout
and their resolved `tools` allow `subagent`.

## Launch shape

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| One bounded task for one child | direct `{ agent, task }` |
| JavaScript control flow or data-dependent branching; sequence, fanout, retry, rolling fanout, or aggregation | a workflow script with `runs.run(...)` / `runs.all(...)` |
| A broad plan split into visible narrow stages per lane | a workflow script with `runs.lanes([{ key, stages: [...] }])` |
| Independent worktree or repository lanes | `references/multi-lane-orchestration.md` |
| Council of advisors | `../council-mode/SKILL.md` |
| Management, status, steering, authoring, or inspection | `action` |

To launch a workflow script, write it as one ```` ```js workflow ```` fenced
block in your reply, then call `subagent({ workflow: true, ... })` in the same
reply. Use `workflow: "./path/to/script.js"` for a script file and
`workflow: "<name>"` for a named resource.

A workflow script is code-driven: `runs.run(...)` for keyed steps,
`runs.all([...])` for fanout, plain JavaScript for branching and aggregation.
Keep scripts portable: use top-level `await`, plain helpers, or explicit Promise
chains, not nested async helpers. Legacy top-level `chain` / `tasks` inputs and
durable `.chain.md` execution are inspection or migration material only, except
that `disabledFeatures: ["workflow-scripts"]` replaces scripts with top-level
`chain` and `tasks` (see [configuration](../../docs/configuration.md#chain-and-tasks-without-workflow-scripts)).

Use `runs.lanes(...)` only inside a workflow script, not as a top-level mode,
when a broad, predeclared plan benefits from visible per-lane stages; otherwise
use ordinary `runs.run(...)` / `runs.all(...)`. See the [canonical staged-lane
example](../../docs/workflows.md#parallel-sequential-lanes). Keep assignments
bounded, but do not add stages or ceremony just to satisfy this skill.

When composing `runs.run(...)`, `runs.all(...)`, or `runs.lanes(...)`, always
supply a short verb + behavior display `label` derived from the task, unless
the user supplied an explicit label; preserve that label. Keep the stable
machine `key` independent (for example, `issue2011-writer` with
`label: "Fix workflow steering"`). For `runs.lanes`, put labels on stage
items, not lane objects. Use stage-appropriate labels for reviews and retained-child
follow-ups too (for example, `Review workflow steering`). Generate labels in
the orchestrator while composing the launch—no extra model call, runtime
generator, or schema change. Native direct `{ agent, task }` calls have no
top-level `label` parameter; do not invent one or wrap a tiny single task in
a workflow just to label it.

Use async/background by default. Set `async:false` only when the parent must
block. Final reviews, validation gates, oracle checks, and publication checks
stay async.

In an ordinary interactive session, yield after launching or triaging useful
async lanes and let Pi wake the parent on completion; ordinary async subagents
already have native completion notifications, so do not call `bg_wait()` merely
because a child is active. Use blocking `bg_wait()` only for provider,
detached, or other background work without a native notification when a
headless/run-to-completion contract or a required same-turn artifact makes the
result necessary before this turn ends. For
“continue/orchestrate/work until done,” keep the lane board moving while a safe
immediate action remains; if only async lanes are running, record the revisit
trigger and yield.

Package agents appear in `subagent({ action: "list" })`. External CLI/job agents
use their own runner contract. Do not pass native Pi child options to them unless
that runner explicitly supports the option.

## Read the reference for the branch

For exact API fields and worked examples, call `subagent({action:"guide",options:{topic:"tool-reference"}})` or `topic:"workflows"`. The compact tool definition is not the recipe catalog; use `topic:"missions"` for mission updates and schedules.

| Branch | Read |
| --- | --- |
| Delegate or choose roles, prompts, models, or slash commands | `references/prompting-and-roles.md` |
| Execute single, scripted, async, scheduled, mission, forked, watchdog, oracle, or intercom workflows | `references/execution-controls.md` |
| Review, validate, triage gate failures, or prepare delivery | `references/review-and-validation.md` |
| Coordinate lanes, worktrees, repositories, or writer waves | `references/multi-lane-orchestration.md` |
| List, create, edit, disable, eject, or expose agents/RPC | `references/management-authoring-rpc.md` |
| Check safety constraints, recipes, or error handling | `references/constraints-and-recipes.md` |

For an authorized complex delegated workflow, read `prompting-and-roles.md` and
`execution-controls.md`, then load `review-and-validation.md` and
`constraints-and-recipes.md` before launch or review.

## Operating rules

- Avoid duplicate scouts, overlapping writers, and vague prompts without a concrete deliverable.
- Call `subagent`, `subagents_enable`, `subagent_supervisor`, `contact_supervisor`, and `structured_output` as ordinary model tool calls. They are model-only, so codemode scripts cannot reach them through `tools.*`, `ALL_TOOLS`, or `searchTools`.
- Keep the parent on the ordinary strong default model. Route workers/scouts to a fast capable tier, serious reviews to a strong tier, and top reasoning to bounded read-only critique.
- Exact model names are deployment policy. Put them in user/project settings or profiles, not package guidance.
- Give every child a compact meta-prompt checklist: objective; repo/cwd/ref; authority/edit boundary; relevant files/contracts and constraints; success/acceptance criteria; validation; expected output/report; and stop/ask conditions. See `references/prompting-and-roles.md`.
- Before launching a writer for substantial mutation work, classify it as single-seam or multi-seam and partition multi-seam work across exclusive component owners, gates, and durable handoffs before an integration-only owner. See `references/multi-lane-orchestration.md`.
- For mutation work, use an isolated lane/worktree when isolation, overlap, or concurrent juggling matters; keep one writer per cwd/worktree. `worktree: true` refuses to launch unless the source checkout is clean (untracked files count; `.pi/subagents/` does not), so commit your own changes first or plan the lane without managed isolation. See `references/multi-lane-orchestration.md` for lane mechanics.
- Keep long/high-output validation out of chat: prefer `interactive_shell` dispatch/background monitors, bounded logs, or subagent-owned reports; return a concise summary plus report path unless same-turn output is required. Do not use `interactive_shell` as an implicit fallback for a failed `subagent` lane; see `references/execution-controls.md`.
- Treat subagent workflow, child launch, prompt runtime, extension load, and child tooling setup failures as lane infrastructure blockers. Stop, report the exact failure and run/worktree state, verify a clean worktree or capture a partial diff, and use only a clear same-protocol retry or an owner-approved execution-mode fallback.
- For cross-codebase work, record the repo, explicit `cwd`, authority boundary, and expected output before launch.
- Make parallel prompts distinct by source seam, evidence, and decision. Do not clone prompts with only item numbers swapped.
- Prefer fresh-context review/validation fanout, then synthesize and apply fixes in the parent.
- For Pi extension repos under `~/.pi/agent/extensions`, put lane worktrees outside extension auto-discovery, such as `~/.pi/agent/worktrees`.
- Preserve capability ceilings, including child tool limits and allowed-agent restrictions.
- Preserve parent authority and escalate unresolved choices.
- Treat receipts, CI, review bots, and external-run records as evidence, not authority.
- For backlog maintenance, releases, merge queues, or other public-repo mutation policy, load the matching user/project skill. This package defines delegation primitives, not private policy.
- As a conservative orchestration policy, do not pass a hard `toolBudget` or tight `usageBudget` to mutation-capable workers. The default tool budget blocks read/search tools rather than mutation tools. If interrupted after a tool call starts, checkpoint after the current tool returns with changed files, build/test state, and commit or PR state.

## P1 rendered-layout regression: bounded row metadata at 1000px

- **Bug.** With Gmail actions enabled, the unbounded `auto`-sized trailing
  metadata (read-state text + date + up to three `white-space: nowrap`
  actions) collapsed the subject/snippet column to **0 CSS px at 1000px** —
  both for an unknown read state alone and for the realistic unknown+pending
  combination (held `setArchived(false)` on an inbox thread; a held read
  setter makes read state known, so it is not a valid repro).
- **Fix.** `.inbox-row` is now a flex row: when the metadata is widest, the
  deficit comes out of the sender column (160→90px floor) while the
  subject/snippet column keeps a 136px floor (≈104px of readable subject, the
  preview yields first), and `.row-meta` stays content-sized (`flex: 0 0
  auto`) so nothing is clipped. Metadata presentation was compacted without
  losing capability: visible state label "Unknown" with
  `aria-label="Read state unknown"`, and row action chips with tighter inline
  padding whose compact labels carry the full accessible names

  explicit archive/read controls, and the contact breakpoint are unchanged.

  1000px; full subject at 1440px), ≥ 120px subject/snippet column and ≥ 100px
  subject box, single-line row height, no horizontal overflow, visible
  pending/read-state disclosures, and
  named, keyboard-reachable, clickable actions. Scenarios: unknown read state
  with actions enabled at 1000px; unknown + held-unarchive pending membership
  at 1000px; 1440px wide sanity. Default `pnpm test` runs skip it (environment
  gate); it was run and is green with
  `/home/exedev/.cache/rod/browser/chromium-1321438/chrome`:

  EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/home/exedev/.cache/rod/browser/chromium-1321438/chrome \
    pnpm vitest run tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts

  green on the working tree and red in an isolated copy with only the pre-fix

  UI run reported 199 passed and this one browser test skipped, followed by the

## Findings

### [P1] Prevent keyboard activation of actions hidden beneath a drawer
**Location:** `src/App.vue:677`

The central surface remains focusable while a fixed utility drawer covers it. In the parent-run synthetic Chrome probe at 1000px, opening Activity and pressing Shift+Tab from its Close button focused `row-archive-conv-18`, entirely behind the drawer: hit-testing the button’s center returned the drawer instead. Native Enter then confirmed an archive of that conversation while Activity remained open. The shortcut guard does not prevent native button activation. **Smallest correction:** make the covered central surface inert while a utility/contact disclosure is open, leaving rail navigation and drawer controls available. Evidence: `/tmp/email-os-post-layout-review-decb6o1j/keyboard-scroll-probes.json` and `keyboard-enter-confirmation.json`.

### [P1] Bound metadata when larger text exhausts the row’s width
**Location:** `src/assets/style.css:327-328`

The subject floor prevents zero-width collapse, but content-sized, nonshrinking metadata trades that failure for horizontal overflow. At 1000px with a 20px root font, an unknown-read row with a held unarchive and the valid date “30 Sept 2001” measured **585px client width versus 695px scroll width**; Archive ended at x814.6 although the visible row ended at x705. The parent’s root-font override emulated larger user text rather than changing browser preferences. The same scenario fits at 16px. **Smallest correction:** introduce an adaptive compact metadata/action presentation when the combined minimum widths exceed available space, retaining accessible action names, and add this larger-font/older-date regression. Evidence: `targeted-review-probes.json`, keys `defaultFontOldDate` and `largerRootFontOldDate`.

### [P2] Preserve a shared sender/subject boundary across rows
**Location:** `src/assets/style.css:292-294`

Shrinking each sender independently according to its row’s metadata breaks column alignment and moves a conversation’s subject when pending state changes. At 1000px/default text size, the parent probe measured the pending unknown row’s sender at **90px** and subject start at **x203.98**, while neighboring read, unread, and nonpending unknown rows retained **160px** senders and subjects starting at **x273.98**. This is a 70px scanning discontinuity, not screenshot calibration, and conflicts with the specification’s stable constrained sender column. **Smallest correction:** choose a shared sender width for all rows at the current available width rather than shrinking only metadata-heavy rows. Evidence: `targeted-review-probes.json`, `defaultFontOldDate.neighbors`.

### [P2] Let drawer Escape reach the protected draft-close lifecycle
**Location:** `src/App.vue:458-464`

Once a draft editor is active, the early return prevents the new Drafts drawer’s Escape handler from running—even when focus is on its outer Close button, not a text field. The parent’s native-key probe confirmed that Escape leaves both drawer and composer open without attempting the save. This contradicts UX-01’s stated utility-disclosure Escape behavior; the existing `closeDrawer()` already preserves the buffer when flushing fails. **Smallest correction:** dispatch eligible drawer Escape through `closeDrawer()` before suppressing mailbox shortcuts for the active editor, retaining IME/modifier/editable-target protections. Evidence: `keyboard-scroll-probes.json`, `draftEscape`.

## Overall verdict

**Needs attention.** The default-font collapse regression is fixed in the supplied Chrome evidence, but covered-action activation and larger-text overflow remain actionable accessibility defects.

No commands were executed by this reviewer. Existing parent-run checks were inspected, and narrowly requested synthetic probes supplied the measurements above. Chrome’s accessibility tree did expose “Read state unknown”; no finding is raised against that accessible name. Native/WKWebView and VoiceOver verification remain pending.

## Human Reviewer Callouts (Non-Blocking)

- (none)

## Findings

### [P2] Cancel pending draft opens when dismissing Drafts
**Location:** `src/App.vue:139–141`

If an existing draft’s `getDraft` is delayed, closing Drafts succeeds because `activeRef` is still null (`releaseDraftsDrawer`, lines 97–99). After the user navigates to another conversation, the response installs the draft and this new watcher reopens Drafts and steals focus. The parent-run synthetic probe reproduced the transition from reader-only to reader plus composer, with focus moving to `utility-drawer` (`targeted-review-probes.json`, `resolveDismissedDraftLoad`). **Smallest correction:** invalidate pending draft-open requests when leaving Drafts, and only route a completed open when its navigation intent remains current. Add a deferred-load dismissal regression.

### [P2] Preserve the Inbox anchor when opening Activity mail from a reader
**Location:** `src/App.vue:330–334`

Activity can be opened while a reader is active, but `captureListOrigin()` then replaces the saved anchor with null because `InboxList` is unmounted. Opening an Activity conversation and returning consequently resets Inbox scrolling and leaves the focused row offscreen. The parent-run Chrome probe confirmed `scrollTop` changing from 170 to 0, with focused `conv-14` moving below the viewport (`keyboard-scroll-probes.json`, `scrollBefore`, `scrollAfterBack`, `scrollAfterDrawerClose`). **Smallest correction:** retain the existing anchor when navigating from an already-open reader; capture a new anchor only from a mounted Inbox list. Add this nested navigation round-trip test.

**Overall verdict: correct — no blocking issues identified; two report-only P2 findings.**

Validation was evidence-only: supplied independent checks report six passing gates, 199 UI tests passing, and the explicit Chrome layout regression passing. I did not execute commands or modify files. Native/WKWebView and assistive-technology verification remain pending.

## Review synthesis

The three fresh-context reviews are complete. **The original zero-width subject bug is fixed at the tested default font**, but two P1 issues remain. No P0 findings.

### Fixes worth doing now

**1. [P1] Hidden mailbox actions remain keyboard-activatable beneath drawers** — [`src/App.vue:677`](src/App.vue#L677)  
With Activity open, Shift+Tab from Close focuses an Archive button completely covered by the drawer. A real Enter keypress then archives that synthetic conversation while Activity remains open.

Make the covered central surface inert while a disclosure is open, while retaining access to rail navigation and drawer controls. Add a native keyboard-input regression.

**2. [P1] Larger text pushes actions outside the row** — [`src/assets/style.css:328–329`](src/assets/style.css#L328)  
At 1000px with a 20px root font, unknown read state, pending membership, and an older date, Chrome measured **585px available width versus 695px content width**. Archive extended roughly **110px beyond the visible row**. The same case fits at 16px.

Use an adaptive metadata/action presentation when the available width is exhausted, preserving readable subjects and accessible actions. Extend the rendered regression to cover larger text and longer dates.

### Optional improvements — P2, report-only

| Finding | Evidence / suggested correction |
|---|---|
| **Sender/subject columns shift between rows** — [`style.css:292`](src/assets/style.css#L292) | The pending row’s subject starts 70px left of neighboring subjects. Use a shared sender width rather than independent per-row shrinking. |
| **Draft drawer Escape is suppressed** — [`App.vue:458–464`](src/App.vue#L458) | Escape from the outer Close button does nothing while a draft is active. Dispatch eligible Escape through protected close handling. |
| **Dismissed draft loads can reopen Drafts** — [`App.vue:139–141`](src/App.vue#L139) | A delayed `getDraft()` response overrides newer reader navigation and steals focus. Fence or cancel the pending navigation intent. |
| **Nested Activity navigation loses the list anchor** — [`App.vue:330–334`](src/App.vue#L330) | Reader → Activity → reader → Back resets scroll from 170 to 0, leaving the focused row offscreen. Preserve the saved anchor when the list is unmounted. |

Use actual Tab traversal and coordinate-based clicks for those claims. This is a test gap, not proof normal buttons are inaccessible. |

- The suspected loss of the **“Read state unknown”** accessible name was **not confirmed**: Chrome exposes it correctly.
- No concrete ambient-type or generated-contract defect was established.
- Native/WKWebView/VoiceOver verification remains pending.
- No reviewed files changed during this review.

# Multi-Lane Orchestration

Use this reference when several independent tasks need coordinated workers, worktrees, or repositories. It defines lane ownership; use the other pi-subagents references for run controls, prompts, and mission details. The parent remains the final decision-maker.

Create lanes only after delegation is operator-authorized and each lane materially improves evidence, independent review, specialization, useful parallelism, or isolated execution. Do not manufacture parallelism: keep dependent work serial, and only split work when each lane has a distinct decision and useful output.

## Mandatory implementation-topology preflight

Before launching a writer for substantial mutation work, classify the implementation as **single-seam** or **multi-seam**. Two or more independently testable contracts or source boundaries make it multi-seam. One PR does not imply one writer, and the one-writer-per-worktree rule prevents concurrent ownership conflicts; it does not authorize an issue-wide commission.

Record the classification and evidence on a lane board before writer launch. For multi-seam work, give each isolated component writer exclusive file or contract ownership and focused validation gates. Require every component to produce a committed or otherwise durable handoff, then start a separate integration-only owner after the component handoffs are ready. Mechanically reject and repartition a writer prompt if it owns all major outcomes across multiple independent boundaries.

A single complete writer remains valid only when the board records evidence that the work is genuinely one seam or that splitting it would create overlapping ownership or artificial handoffs. This preflight must not manufacture parallelism: do not split tightly coupled work merely to increase the lane count.

## Lane board and authority

Before multiple mutation-capable lanes start, record this board in the parent context:

`Lane | repo/cwd | exact decision | claimed files or contract | isolation path | authority | next gate | handoff | why independent`

Record the isolation path before the first mutation. Do not split one source seam or decision into duplicate lanes. Make overlapping work one lane with one source of truth.

For every lane, record the delivery target, allowed actions, required validation, and review rigor. For cross-repository work, name the shared contract and which repository changes first. A blocked decision is a lane state: record the owner, options, recommended default, and evidence needed to continue.

## Partitioned runs

Use one writer per repo/cwd or worktree. Mutation lanes need distinct isolation paths and explicit `cwd` values. Set `worktree: true` when a run needs managed worktree isolation within one repository. Each managed worktree branches from `HEAD` unless `baseRef` names another ref, and launch fails with "worktree isolation requires a clean git working tree" while the source checkout has modified, staged, or untracked files outside `.pi/subagents/`. In a shared or dirty checkout, commit your own changes before launching, give each lane an explicit `cwd` in a worktree you created, or run without isolation. Read-only runs can share a checkout only when they cannot change state or create generated files.

For Pi extension repositories, keep lane worktrees outside auto-discovered extension directories such as `~/.pi/agent/extensions`. A stale extension worktree there can auto-load duplicate tools and shortcuts. Remove or move it only after its handoff is durable, the worktree is clean, and no run owns it.

Partition fanout by repository, source seam, decision, or review angle. Each run needs a stable key, lane-specific task, and a managed output path when a file is needed. Do not launch prompts that differ only by item name or broad file glob.

### Cold-start packets and bounded orchestration audits

Every child packet must stand alone: include the goal, exact repository/cwd/ref, authority and edit boundary, relevant context/evidence, success criteria, validation, expected output, and stop/escalation rules. Do not rely on parent history, an issue number, or a broad glob alone. An orchestration audit by a top-reasoning critic model is read-only and returns at most three cited omissions; use high thinking only as an explicit parent/user escalation, never as an autonomous root or a parallel placeholder.

Use one async workflow script (`subagent({ workflow: true, async: true })` after a ```` ```js workflow ```` block) for a coordinated wave. Use `runs.all` for independent lanes and `runs.run` for dependent lane stages. Give cross-repository runs explicit `cwd` values and lane-qualified outputs. Use `outputMode: "file-only"` when a report must survive the run or feed a later stage. Keep scratch outputs relative so they live under subagent artifacts; use absolute paths only for durable memory, approved docs paths, or final handoff files.

## Keep independent work moving

While one lane waits, run safe independent preparation, validation, or fresh read-only review lanes. Do not block the parent just because a run is active. If no safe lane remains, record the blocker and the event that will reopen work.

In an ordinary interactive session, completion wakes the parent; after useful
async lanes are launched or triaged, yield rather than use
`bg_wait({ all: true })` as a barrier. “Continue/orchestrate/work until
done” means keep the board moving while safe immediate work remains. If only
async lanes are running, record the revisit trigger and yield.

An ordinary coordinated workflow has one mission. Use its durable state, artifacts, run records, and receipts for recovery. Treat a receipt as evidence, not as authority or acceptance.

After a writer produces a candidate, run the required fresh-context, read-only reviewer. The reviewer inspects the exact worktree and returns evidence-backed findings. The parent decides which findings are in scope and whether the lane is ready. Use `review-and-validation.md` for finding disposition, validation, and gate-failure triage. Send accepted fixes to that lane's sole writer, then rerun only the affected gate.

## Handoff, cleanup, and recovery

Use stable lane-qualified artifact paths for reports and review output. A handoff states the lane status, repository and worktree, changed files, validation, open decisions, next action, and artifact or receipt paths. Copy only the final evidence to memory, a mission record, or a PR/comment, then remove scratch files from the active worktree before closing the lane.

For backlog lanes and other subagent-governed workflows, a setup/runtime/tooling failure remains an infrastructure blocker. Preserve the exact failure, run/status, and repository/cwd/worktree/branch/ref state; verify a clean worktree or capture any partial diff before a same-protocol retry or asking the owner. Do not start another writer or switch to an external, foreground, or CLI execution mode without explicit owner approval.

Keep a worktree until its handoff is durable, no run owns it, and no later gate needs it. Clean up only inside the recorded authority boundary. If a run stops or needs attention, preserve its worktree and artifacts, record the last known state and recovery owner, then resume that run or create one replacement lane from the handoff. Do not start another writer while worktree ownership is uncertain.

Before completion, inspect the board. Every lane must be terminal or blocked with a named next action. Confirm one writer per repo/cwd or worktree, required validation, required fresh read-only review, and a durable handoff. The parent reports outcomes, evidence, residual risks, and the next decision.

---
name: pi-subagents
description: |
  Technical guidance for operator-requested delegation to builtin or custom
  subagents: bounded handoffs, parallel review, scripted workflows, async work,
  forked context, isolation, and coordinated execution.
---

# Pi Subagents

The parent works directly by default. Invoke subagents only when the operator
requested delegation in the current request or through applicable user/project
instructions. Task size, complexity, risk, tool-call count, recipe fit, or an
available specialist does not independently authorize delegation.

Once authorized, choose the smallest bounded shape that earns its token and
elapsed-time overhead through concrete evidence, independent review,
specialization, useful parallelism, or needed isolation. A single child is
valid; writer, challenge, and review stages must each earn their overhead rather
than becoming default ceremony. The parent keeps user intent, constraints,
routing, arbitration, decisions, final acceptance, and publication authority,
and may perform the work directly where it is the most efficient owner.

Children do not spawn subagents unless the parent explicitly delegated fanout
and their resolved `tools` allow `subagent`.

## Launch shape

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| One bounded task for one child | direct `{ agent, task }` |
| JavaScript control flow or data-dependent branching; sequence, fanout, retry, rolling fanout, or aggregation | a workflow script with `runs.run(...)` / `runs.all(...)` |
| A broad plan split into visible narrow stages per lane | a workflow script with `runs.lanes([{ key, stages: [...] }])` |
| Independent worktree or repository lanes | `references/multi-lane-orchestration.md` |
| Council of advisors | `../council-mode/SKILL.md` |
| Management, status, steering, authoring, or inspection | `action` |

To launch a workflow script, write it as one ```` ```js workflow ```` fenced
block in your reply, then call `subagent({ workflow: true, ... })` in the same
reply. Use `workflow: "./path/to/script.js"` for a script file and
`workflow: "<name>"` for a named resource.

A workflow script is code-driven: `runs.run(...)` for keyed steps,
`runs.all([...])` for fanout, plain JavaScript for branching and aggregation.
Keep scripts portable: use top-level `await`, plain helpers, or explicit Promise
chains, not nested async helpers. Legacy top-level `chain` / `tasks` inputs and
durable `.chain.md` execution are inspection or migration material only, except
that `disabledFeatures: ["workflow-scripts"]` replaces scripts with top-level
`chain` and `tasks` (see [configuration](../../docs/configuration.md#chain-and-tasks-without-workflow-scripts)).

Use `runs.lanes(...)` only inside a workflow script, not as a top-level mode,
when a broad, predeclared plan benefits from visible per-lane stages; otherwise
use ordinary `runs.run(...)` / `runs.all(...)`. See the [canonical staged-lane
example](../../docs/workflows.md#parallel-sequential-lanes). Keep assignments
bounded, but do not add stages or ceremony just to satisfy this skill.

When composing `runs.run(...)`, `runs.all(...)`, or `runs.lanes(...)`, always
supply a short verb + behavior display `label` derived from the task, unless
the user supplied an explicit label; preserve that label. Keep the stable
machine `key` independent (for example, `issue2011-writer` with
`label: "Fix workflow steering"`). For `runs.lanes`, put labels on stage
items, not lane objects. Use stage-appropriate labels for reviews and retained-child
follow-ups too (for example, `Review workflow steering`). Generate labels in
the orchestrator while composing the launch—no extra model call, runtime
generator, or schema change. Native direct `{ agent, task }` calls have no
top-level `label` parameter; do not invent one or wrap a tiny single task in
a workflow just to label it.

Use async/background by default. Set `async:false` only when the parent must
block. Final reviews, validation gates, oracle checks, and publication checks
stay async.

In an ordinary interactive session, yield after launching or triaging useful
async lanes and let Pi wake the parent on completion; ordinary async subagents
already have native completion notifications, so do not call `bg_wait()` merely
because a child is active. Use blocking `bg_wait()` only for provider,
detached, or other background work without a native notification when a
headless/run-to-completion contract or a required same-turn artifact makes the
result necessary before this turn ends. For
“continue/orchestrate/work until done,” keep the lane board moving while a safe
immediate action remains; if only async lanes are running, record the revisit
trigger and yield.

Package agents appear in `subagent({ action: "list" })`. External CLI/job agents
use their own runner contract. Do not pass native Pi child options to them unless
that runner explicitly supports the option.

## Read the reference for the branch

For exact API fields and worked examples, call `subagent({action:"guide",options:{topic:"tool-reference"}})` or `topic:"workflows"`. The compact tool definition is not the recipe catalog; use `topic:"missions"` for mission updates and schedules.

| Branch | Read |
| --- | --- |
| Delegate or choose roles, prompts, models, or slash commands | `references/prompting-and-roles.md` |
| Execute single, scripted, async, scheduled, mission, forked, watchdog, oracle, or intercom workflows | `references/execution-controls.md` |
| Review, validate, triage gate failures, or prepare delivery | `references/review-and-validation.md` |
| Coordinate lanes, worktrees, repositories, or writer waves | `references/multi-lane-orchestration.md` |
| List, create, edit, disable, eject, or expose agents/RPC | `references/management-authoring-rpc.md` |
| Check safety constraints, recipes, or error handling | `references/constraints-and-recipes.md` |

For an authorized complex delegated workflow, read `prompting-and-roles.md` and
`execution-controls.md`, then load `review-and-validation.md` and
`constraints-and-recipes.md` before launch or review.

## Operating rules

- Avoid duplicate scouts, overlapping writers, and vague prompts without a concrete deliverable.
- Call `subagent`, `subagents_enable`, `subagent_supervisor`, `contact_supervisor`, and `structured_output` as ordinary model tool calls. They are model-only, so codemode scripts cannot reach them through `tools.*`, `ALL_TOOLS`, or `searchTools`.
- Keep the parent on the ordinary strong default model. Route workers/scouts to a fast capable tier, serious reviews to a strong tier, and top reasoning to bounded read-only critique.
- Exact model names are deployment policy. Put them in user/project settings or profiles, not package guidance.
- Give every child a compact meta-prompt checklist: objective; repo/cwd/ref; authority/edit boundary; relevant files/contracts and constraints; success/acceptance criteria; validation; expected output/report; and stop/ask conditions. See `references/prompting-and-roles.md`.
- Before launching a writer for substantial mutation work, classify it as single-seam or multi-seam and partition multi-seam work across exclusive component owners, gates, and durable handoffs before an integration-only owner. See `references/multi-lane-orchestration.md`.
- For mutation work, use an isolated lane/worktree when isolation, overlap, or concurrent juggling matters; keep one writer per cwd/worktree. `worktree: true` refuses to launch unless the source checkout is clean (untracked files count; `.pi/subagents/` does not), so commit your own changes first or plan the lane without managed isolation. See `references/multi-lane-orchestration.md` for lane mechanics.
- Keep long/high-output validation out of chat: prefer `interactive_shell` dispatch/background monitors, bounded logs, or subagent-owned reports; return a concise summary plus report path unless same-turn output is required. Do not use `interactive_shell` as an implicit fallback for a failed `subagent` lane; see `references/execution-controls.md`.
- Treat subagent workflow, child launch, prompt runtime, extension load, and child tooling setup failures as lane infrastructure blockers. Stop, report the exact failure and run/worktree state, verify a clean worktree or capture a partial diff, and use only a clear same-protocol retry or an owner-approved execution-mode fallback.
- For cross-codebase work, record the repo, explicit `cwd`, authority boundary, and expected output before launch.
- Make parallel prompts distinct by source seam, evidence, and decision. Do not clone prompts with only item numbers swapped.
- Prefer fresh-context review/validation fanout, then synthesize and apply fixes in the parent.
- For Pi extension repos under `~/.pi/agent/extensions`, put lane worktrees outside extension auto-discovery, such as `~/.pi/agent/worktrees`.
- Preserve capability ceilings, including child tool limits and allowed-agent restrictions.
- Preserve parent authority and escalate unresolved choices.
- Treat receipts, CI, review bots, and external-run records as evidence, not authority.
- For backlog maintenance, releases, merge queues, or other public-repo mutation policy, load the matching user/project skill. This package defines delegation primitives, not private policy.
- As a conservative orchestration policy, do not pass a hard `toolBudget` or tight `usageBudget` to mutation-capable workers. The default tool budget blocks read/search tools rather than mutation tools. If interrupted after a tool call starts, checkpoint after the current tool returns with changed files, build/test state, and commit or PR state.

## Recommended orchestration pattern

Use orchestration as parent-agent guidance, not as a runtime workflow mode. For implementation work, the recommended loop is:

```text
clarify → scout → worker → fresh reviewers → worker
```

Packaged `worker` defaults to fresh context so implementation starts from its assigned brief instead of the parent's unfinished conversation. Packaged `oracle` and `advisor` default to forked context; if the parent has no persisted session file or current leaf yet, that implicit default falls back to `fresh`. Explicit `context`, `context: "profile"`, and global `defaultSubagentContext` still override these profile defaults.

Launch children in the background (`async` follows `asyncByDefault`, normally true) and consume each result at the point a later step depends on it. Native completion wakes the parent session, so the parent returns control instead of sleeping or polling. Use `async: false` only when the parent must block, not for final reviews or gates. When an oracle or advisor reaches an unknown that needs a decision, it asks through supervisor dialogue; use a one-shot oracle call only when one was requested.

Child-safety boundaries are enforced at runtime:

- Child sessions do not receive the bundled `pi-subagents` skill.
- Child context filtering removes parent-only subagent artifacts (hidden orchestration-instruction messages, slash/status/control messages, and `subagent` tool-call/tool-result history) while preserving ordinary prose and unrelated tool calls/results. A forked child sends the history it inherited exactly as the parent sent it, so its first request can reuse the parent's prompt cache; it still cannot run `subagent`.
- By default, children do not register the `subagent` tool and receive boundary instructions that they are not the parent orchestrator and must not propose or run subagents.
- The explicit exception is an agent whose resolved builtin `tools` includes `subagent`; that child gets a child-safe `subagent` tool for the fanout work the parent assigned, still bounded by `maxSubagentDepth`.

### Failed lane recovery and execution-mode boundaries

A failure in the subagent workflow, child launch, prompt runtime, extension loading, or child tooling setup is a lane infrastructure blocker. It is not permission to silently retry through `interactive_shell`, `pi -ne`, Codex/Claude/Cursor CLI, a foreground agent, or another external execution mode.

Stop and report the exact failure, run/status, and repository/cwd/worktree/branch/ref state. Before a same-protocol retry or asking the owner, verify the worktree is clean or capture the partial diff. Retry or fix the `subagent` path only through a clear same-protocol action. For backlog lanes and other subagent-governed workflows, external/foreground/CLI fallback requires explicit owner approval. `interactive_shell` remains valid when the user explicitly requests visible foreground/CLI work or the task is outside the governed subagent protocol.

Failed workflow details and async `status.json` include `workflow.failureKind` as `validation`, `script`, `child`, `return-serialization`, `timeout`, `detached-child`, or `runtime`. `validation` means the host rejected the script before it ran (syntax or portability) or at completion (unawaited calls); errors thrown into a running script, including rejected `runs.run` parameters and runtime `SyntaxError`s, are `script` because the script could catch them, and failed children are `child`. `runtime` covers host setup and infrastructure failures, such as an unavailable cwd or a crashed worker. A workflow that is stopped or reloaded is not a failure and has no `failureKind`.

When `/reload`, a session resume, or a pi-web project switch replaces the extension runtime, a running async workflow stops with `workflow.stopCause: "runtime-replaced"` in `status.json`, and its awaited async children keep running. Its in-process foreground children are stopped, including ones that detached to ask their supervisor. When the same workflow script is launched again with the same `args` in that session, a `runs.run` with the same key and params returns a child that already finished successfully without launching it, and waits for a child that is still running instead of starting another. Those results carry `reused: true`, their step and trace entry are marked `reused`, and the new run records `workflow.reusedFrom`. Failed and stopped children, and children that ran in-process, launch again. Reuse applies only when the newest run of that script and args in the session was stopped this way; a user stop or a completed run ends it. From another session, such as one that took over after a handoff, relaunch the same script as an async workflow with `options: { reuseFrom: "<stopped run id>" }`; the run must have stopped this way in the same cwd, and `args` may differ, because each child is still reused only when its key and params match.

After `/new`, `/resume`, or a fork in the same Pi process, the new session owns the async runs of the session it replaced, and of the sessions that one replaced. It can list, `bg_wait` on, steer, stop, and resume them, receives their completion notices, and answers their children's pending supervisor requests. Over RPC, a host can steer, interrupt, stop, resume, and inspect them, and sees them in the fleet and `subagent-async` snapshots. Startup and other Pi processes inherit nothing; `/reload` adds nothing new but keeps what the session already inherited. To relaunch a stopped workflow instead of controlling its children one by one, use `options.reuseFrom`.

Pi core may print a generic `pi -ne` extension-load hint; that out-of-repo hint is not protocol-approved fallback. A verified compaction abort may continue the retained child once on its already resolved model; it does not authorize an execution-mode or model switch.

/**
 * Compact conversation list (UX-01).
 *
 * - Focus is an explicit account-scoped conversation reference, never an array
 *   position and never bulk selection: rows use ordinary list/listitem
 *   semantics with roving tabindex and `aria-current` (not `aria-selected`),
 *   so a future selection model can diverge from focus.
 * - Row keys are account+conversation; DOM refs and navigation address
 *   conversations only. Date group headings are non-actionable and never
 *   tabbable, and they never reorder the backend's rows.
 * - Hover changes nothing: no hover handler mutates focus or read state.
 *   Inline actions are row-scoped buttons that stop propagation; focusing one
 *   never opens the row or scrolls it to center.
 * - Anchor capture/restoration supports the reader round trip: a visible-row
 *   reference with its relative offset plus a scrollTop fallback.
 */
import { computed, nextTick, onBeforeUnmount, onBeforeUpdate, onMounted, reactive, ref, watch } from 'vue';
import type { ConversationRef } from '../lib/ipc/client';
import type { ConversationSummaryLike } from '../composables/useMailbox';
import { sameConversation } from '../composables/useMailbox';
import { compactDateLabel, dateGroupCaption, dateGroupFor } from '../lib/browsing-dates';

const props = defineProps<{
  rows: ConversationSummaryLike[];
  focusedRef: ConversationRef | null;
  actionsEnabled?: boolean;
  showReadState?: boolean;
  showReadControls?: boolean;
}>();

const emit = defineEmits<{
  focus: [ref: ConversationRef];
  open: [ref: ConversationRef];
  archive: [ref: ConversationRef];
  setRead: [ref: ConversationRef, read: boolean];
}>();

/** A surviving list row plus the geometry needed to restore it. */
export interface RowAnchor {
  ref: ConversationRef;
  /** Row top relative to the scrollport top at capture time. */
  offsetTop: number;
  /** Scrollport scrollTop at capture time (fallback when geometry is unavailable). */
  scrollTop: number;
}

const listEl = ref<HTMLElement | null>(null);
const rowEls = new Map<string, HTMLElement>();
let lastFocusedKey: string | null = null;
let listHasFocus = false;
/** Guard so preventScroll focus does not trigger the focusin reveal. */
let preventScrollReveal = false;

/*
 * Adaptive compact action presentation: when a row's full inline metadata and
 * actions do not fit its laid-out width (larger user text, longer dates, the
 * 1000px contact breakpoint), the row keeps its one-line scanning rhythm by
 * collapsing the action buttons behind a small disclosure control. Read state,
 * pending, and date stay visible; the collapsed buttons keep their stable
 * data-test ids, accessible names, and event semantics — only their container
 * moves out of flow (measured while hidden, then shown as a row-anchored
 * disclosure panel while the toggle is operated).
 */
const compactRows = reactive(new Set<string>());
const openActionRows = reactive(new Set<string>());
/** Rows whose open disclosure panel opens upward (near the list bottom). */
const upwardPanels = reactive(new Set<string>());
/** Panel flip threshold in row-font em: the tallest disclosed panel plus slack. */
const PANEL_FLIP_EM = 6;
/** Slack for overflow detection: scrollWidth/clientWidth round to integers. */
const ROW_OVERFLOW_SLACK_PX = 1;
let rowLayoutObserver: ResizeObserver | null = null;
const rowKeyByEl = new Map<HTMLElement, string>();

type ComponentPublicInstance = import('vue').ComponentPublicInstance;

onBeforeUpdate(() => {
  rowEls.clear();
});

function rowKey(target: ConversationRef): string {
  return `${target.accountId}:${target.conversationId}`;
}

function setRowRef(el: Element | ComponentPublicInstance | null, key: string): void {
  if (el instanceof HTMLElement) {
    rowEls.set(key, el);
    rowKeyByEl.set(el, key);
  }
}

interface GroupItem { kind: 'group'; key: string; caption: string; id: number }
interface RowItem { kind: 'row'; row: ConversationSummaryLike; index: number }
type ListItem = GroupItem | RowItem;

/**
 * Backend order is preserved; a heading is emitted wherever the calendar
 * bucket changes between consecutive rows (never re-sorted here).
 */
const items = computed<ListItem[]>(() => {
  const result: ListItem[] = [];
  let previousKey: string | null = null;
  let groupId = 0;
  props.rows.forEach((row, index) => {
    const key = dateGroupFor(row.lastMessageAt);
    if (key !== previousKey) {
      previousKey = key;
      groupId += 1;
      result.push({ kind: 'group', key, caption: dateGroupCaption(key), id: groupId });
    }
    result.push({ kind: 'row', row, index });
  });
  return result;
});

function isFocused(row: ConversationSummaryLike): boolean {
  return sameConversation(row.ref, props.focusedRef);
}

/** Roving tabindex: the focused row, else the first row, is the tab stop. */
function tabIndexFor(row: ConversationSummaryLike, index: number): 0 | -1 {
  if (isFocused(row)) return 0;
  if (props.focusedRef === null && index === 0) return 0;
  return -1;
}

function senderLabel(row: ConversationSummaryLike): string {
  const primary = row.primaryCorrespondent;
  // Absent primaryCorrespondent never becomes a guessed contact.
  if (!primary) return 'Unknown sender';
  return primary.displayName ?? primary.mailbox;
}

/*
 * Compact visible labels; the full disclosure lives in the accessible name so
 * the bounded metadata region never starves the subject column at the 1000px
 * contact breakpoint (rows render "Unknown" + Read/Unread, AT reads the
 * complete "Read state unknown" / "Mark read" / "Mark unread" semantics).
 */
function readStateLabel(row: ConversationSummaryLike): string {
  if (row.isRead === undefined) return 'Unknown';
  return row.isRead ? 'Read' : 'Unread';
}

function hasRowActions(): boolean {
  return Boolean(props.showReadControls || props.actionsEnabled);
}

/** DOM id of the row's action disclosure panel (for aria-controls). */
function actionsPanelId(row: ConversationSummaryLike): string {
  return `row-actions-${row.ref.accountId}-${row.ref.conversationId}`.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/g, '-');
}

function isCompactRow(row: ConversationSummaryLike): boolean {
  return compactRows.has(rowKey(row.ref));
}

function isActionsOpen(row: ConversationSummaryLike): boolean {
  // Open state is tracked independently of the measured compact presentation;
  // CSS only reveals the panel when the row is both compact and open.
  return openActionRows.has(rowKey(row.ref));
}

function isPanelUpward(row: ConversationSummaryLike): boolean {
  return upwardPanels.has(rowKey(row.ref));
}

function toggleActions(row: ConversationSummaryLike): void {
  const key = rowKey(row.ref);
  if (openActionRows.has(key)) {
    openActionRows.delete(key);
    return;
  }
  openActionRows.add(key);
  // Open away from the nearer list edge so the panel never extends past the
  // list scroller's visible box when the row sits near its bottom.
  upwardPanels.delete(key);
  const el = rowEls.get(key);
  const scroller = listEl.value;
  if (!el || !scroller || scroller.clientHeight === 0 || el.clientHeight === 0) return;
  const em = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).fontSize) || 16;
  const below = scroller.getBoundingClientRect().bottom - el.getBoundingClientRect().bottom;
  if (below < PANEL_FLIP_EM * em) upwardPanels.add(key);
}

function closeActions(row: ConversationSummaryLike, refocusToggle: boolean): void {
  const key = rowKey(row.ref);
  if (!openActionRows.delete(key) || !refocusToggle) return;
  rowEls.get(key)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.row-actions-toggle')?.focus();
}

/**
 * Decide per row whether the full inline presentation fits the laid-out row.
 * Measured, not assumed: in the compact presentation the actions span stays in
 * the DOM out of flow (absolute, hidden, max-content width), so the expanded
 * width is exactly the current overflow measurement plus the toggle/action
 * width swap — no threshold guessing, no layout flip-flop. Runs synchronously
 * from the ResizeObserver callback, so a row never paints an overflowing
 * expanded layout.
 */
function evaluateRowLayout(el: HTMLElement, key: string): void {
  if (!el.isConnected || el.clientWidth === 0) return;
  const actions = el.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.row-actions');
  // Rows without actions never overflow into the disclosure.
  if (!actions) return;
  const toggle = el.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.row-actions-toggle');
  let fitsExpanded: boolean;
  if (compactRows.has(key)) {
    const actionsWidth = actions.getBoundingClientRect().width;
    const toggleWidth = toggle ? toggle.getBoundingClientRect().width : 0;
    // Strict margin: only leave the compact presentation when the expanded
    // layout measurably fits, so integer-rounded overflow cannot oscillate.
    fitsExpanded =
      el.scrollWidth + (actionsWidth - toggleWidth) <= el.clientWidth - ROW_OVERFLOW_SLACK_PX;
  } else {
    fitsExpanded = el.scrollWidth <= el.clientWidth + ROW_OVERFLOW_SLACK_PX;
  }
  if (fitsExpanded) compactRows.delete(key);
  else compactRows.add(key);
}

function observeRowLayouts(): void {
  if (!rowLayoutObserver) return;
  rowLayoutObserver.disconnect();
  rowKeyByEl.clear();
  for (const [key, el] of rowEls) {
    rowKeyByEl.set(el, key);
    rowLayoutObserver.observe(el);
  }
}

onMounted(() => {
  // Non-layout environments (jsdom component tests) keep the expanded
  // presentation; the rendered-layout regression covers the compact one.
  if (typeof ResizeObserver !== 'function') return;
  rowLayoutObserver = new ResizeObserver((entries) => {
    for (const entry of entries) {
      const el = entry.target;
      if (!(el instanceof HTMLElement)) continue;

      if (key) evaluateRowLayout(el, key);
    }
  });
  observeRowLayouts();
});

onBeforeUnmount(() => {
  rowLayoutObserver?.disconnect();
  rowLayoutObserver = null;
});

watch(
  () => props.rows.map((row) => rowKey(row.ref)),
  () => observeRowLayouts(),
  { flush: 'post' },
);

edits.newText:
## Follow-up P1 fixes: covered actions and larger text

- **Covered actions.** The central list/reader surface is `inert` while a
  utility drawer or the narrow Contact disclosure is open. Rail and active
  disclosure controls remain available; closing the disclosure restores
  central interaction. This prevents Tab/Shift+Tab from reaching covered mail
  actions and Enter from activating them behind a drawer.
- **Larger text.** A row-local `ResizeObserver` detects when inline actions no
  longer fit. Compact rows offer a named “More actions” disclosure containing
  the same explicit read/unread/archive controls and stable IDs. Its local
  Escape handling returns focus to the toggle; a panel near the list bottom
  opens upward. This fixes the reproduced 1000px/20px-root-font overflow with
  unknown read facts, pending membership, and an old date without shrinking
  the user's root font or clipping actions.
- **Durable browser coverage.** `tests/disclosure-focus.rendered.test.ts`
  exercises real Chrome Tab/Shift+Tab, Enter and pointer input with Activity
  and narrow Contact, including restored interaction after dismissal.
  `tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts` also exercises the 16px/20px,
  old-date, unknown-plus-pending cases and operable compact actions. These
  tests use isolated synthetic previews and caller-supplied Chrome, not real
  accounts or native IPC.
- **Independent combined validation.** After importing only the two workers'
  owned deltas, the parent ran both rendered test files successfully (three
  browser tests total) and all six configured checks. The normal UI suite
  reported **205 passed, three opt-in browser tests skipped**; those three
  were explicitly run with Chrome separately. This evidence note was added
  after validation without changing application or test code. P2 follow-ups
  and native/WKWebView/VoiceOver verification remain pending.

Run the browser gates separately with the appropriate environment variable:

```sh
EMAIL_OS_DISCLOSURE_FOCUS_CHROME=/path/to/chrome \
  pnpm exec vitest run tests/disclosure-focus.rendered.test.ts
EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/path/to/chrome \
  pnpm exec vitest run tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts
```

---
name: pi-subagents
description: |
  Technical guidance for operator-requested delegation to builtin or custom
  subagents: bounded handoffs, parallel review, scripted workflows, async work,
  forked context, isolation, and coordinated execution.
---

# Pi Subagents

The parent works directly by default. Invoke subagents only when the operator
requested delegation in the current request or through applicable user/project
instructions. Task size, complexity, risk, tool-call count, recipe fit, or an
available specialist does not independently authorize delegation.

Once authorized, choose the smallest bounded shape that earns its token and
elapsed-time overhead through concrete evidence, independent review,
specialization, useful parallelism, or needed isolation. A single child is
valid; writer, challenge, and review stages must each earn their overhead rather
than becoming default ceremony. The parent keeps user intent, constraints,
routing, arbitration, decisions, final acceptance, and publication authority,
and may perform the work directly where it is the most efficient owner.

Children do not spawn subagents unless the parent explicitly delegated fanout
and their resolved `tools` allow `subagent`.

## Launch shape

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| One bounded task for one child | direct `{ agent, task }` |
| JavaScript control flow or data-dependent branching; sequence, fanout, retry, rolling fanout, or aggregation | a workflow script with `runs.run(...)` / `runs.all(...)` |
| A broad plan split into visible narrow stages per lane | a workflow script with `runs.lanes([{ key, stages: [...] }])` |
| Independent worktree or repository lanes | `references/multi-lane-orchestration.md` |
| Council of advisors | `../council-mode/SKILL.md` |
| Management, status, steering, authoring, or inspection | `action` |

To launch a workflow script, write it as one ```` ```js workflow ```` fenced
block in your reply, then call `subagent({ workflow: true, ... })` in the same
reply. Use `workflow: "./path/to/script.js"` for a script file and
`workflow: "<name>"` for a named resource.

A workflow script is code-driven: `runs.run(...)` for keyed steps,
`runs.all([...])` for fanout, plain JavaScript for branching and aggregation.
Keep scripts portable: use top-level `await`, plain helpers, or explicit Promise
chains, not nested async helpers. Legacy top-level `chain` / `tasks` inputs and
durable `.chain.md` execution are inspection or migration material only, except
that `disabledFeatures: ["workflow-scripts"]` replaces scripts with top-level
`chain` and `tasks` (see [configuration](../../docs/configuration.md#chain-and-tasks-without-workflow-scripts)).

Use `runs.lanes(...)` only inside a workflow script, not as a top-level mode,
when a broad, predeclared plan benefits from visible per-lane stages; otherwise
use ordinary `runs.run(...)` / `runs.all(...)`. See the [canonical staged-lane
example](../../docs/workflows.md#parallel-sequential-lanes). Keep assignments
bounded, but do not add stages or ceremony just to satisfy this skill.

When composing `runs.run(...)`, `runs.all(...)`, or `runs.lanes(...)`, always
supply a short verb + behavior display `label` derived from the task, unless
the user supplied an explicit label; preserve that label. Keep the stable
machine `key` independent (for example, `issue2011-writer` with
`label: "Fix workflow steering"`). For `runs.lanes`, put labels on stage
items, not lane objects. Use stage-appropriate labels for reviews and retained-child
follow-ups too (for example, `Review workflow steering`). Generate labels in
the orchestrator while composing the launch—no extra model call, runtime
generator, or schema change. Native direct `{ agent, task }` calls have no
top-level `label` parameter; do not invent one or wrap a tiny single task in
a workflow just to label it.

Use async/background by default. Set `async:false` only when the parent must
block. Final reviews, validation gates, oracle checks, and publication checks
stay async.

In an ordinary interactive session, yield after launching or triaging useful
async lanes and let Pi wake the parent on completion; ordinary async subagents
already have native completion notifications, so do not call `bg_wait()` merely
because a child is active. Use blocking `bg_wait()` only for provider,
detached, or other background work without a native notification when a
headless/run-to-completion contract or a required same-turn artifact makes the
result necessary before this turn ends. For
“continue/orchestrate/work until done,” keep the lane board moving while a safe
immediate action remains; if only async lanes are running, record the revisit
trigger and yield.

Package agents appear in `subagent({ action: "list" })`. External CLI/job agents
use their own runner contract. Do not pass native Pi child options to them unless
that runner explicitly supports the option.

## Read the reference for the branch

For exact API fields and worked examples, call `subagent({action:"guide",options:{topic:"tool-reference"}})` or `topic:"workflows"`. The compact tool definition is not the recipe catalog; use `topic:"missions"` for mission updates and schedules.

| Branch | Read |
| --- | --- |
| Delegate or choose roles, prompts, models, or slash commands | `references/prompting-and-roles.md` |
| Execute single, scripted, async, scheduled, mission, forked, watchdog, oracle, or intercom workflows | `references/execution-controls.md` |
| Review, validate, triage gate failures, or prepare delivery | `references/review-and-validation.md` |
| Coordinate lanes, worktrees, repositories, or writer waves | `references/multi-lane-orchestration.md` |
| List, create, edit, disable, eject, or expose agents/RPC | `references/management-authoring-rpc.md` |
| Check safety constraints, recipes, or error handling | `references/constraints-and-recipes.md` |

For an authorized complex delegated workflow, read `prompting-and-roles.md` and
`execution-controls.md`, then load `review-and-validation.md` and
`constraints-and-recipes.md` before launch or review.

## Operating rules

- Avoid duplicate scouts, overlapping writers, and vague prompts without a concrete deliverable.
- Call `subagent`, `subagents_enable`, `subagent_supervisor`, `contact_supervisor`, and `structured_output` as ordinary model tool calls. They are model-only, so codemode scripts cannot reach them through `tools.*`, `ALL_TOOLS`, or `searchTools`.
- Keep the parent on the ordinary strong default model. Route workers/scouts to a fast capable tier, serious reviews to a strong tier, and top reasoning to bounded read-only critique.
- Exact model names are deployment policy. Put them in user/project settings or profiles, not package guidance.
- Give every child a compact meta-prompt checklist: objective; repo/cwd/ref; authority/edit boundary; relevant files/contracts and constraints; success/acceptance criteria; validation; expected output/report; and stop/ask conditions. See `references/prompting-and-roles.md`.
- Before launching a writer for substantial mutation work, classify it as single-seam or multi-seam and partition multi-seam work across exclusive component owners, gates, and durable handoffs before an integration-only owner. See `references/multi-lane-orchestration.md`.
- For mutation work, use an isolated lane/worktree when isolation, overlap, or concurrent juggling matters; keep one writer per cwd/worktree. `worktree: true` refuses to launch unless the source checkout is clean (untracked files count; `.pi/subagents/` does not), so commit your own changes first or plan the lane without managed isolation. See `references/multi-lane-orchestration.md` for lane mechanics.
- Keep long/high-output validation out of chat: prefer `interactive_shell` dispatch/background monitors, bounded logs, or subagent-owned reports; return a concise summary plus report path unless same-turn output is required. Do not use `interactive_shell` as an implicit fallback for a failed `subagent` lane; see `references/execution-controls.md`.
- Treat subagent workflow, child launch, prompt runtime, extension load, and child tooling setup failures as lane infrastructure blockers. Stop, report the exact failure and run/worktree state, verify a clean worktree or capture a partial diff, and use only a clear same-protocol retry or an owner-approved execution-mode fallback.
- For cross-codebase work, record the repo, explicit `cwd`, authority boundary, and expected output before launch.
- Make parallel prompts distinct by source seam, evidence, and decision. Do not clone prompts with only item numbers swapped.
- Prefer fresh-context review/validation fanout, then synthesize and apply fixes in the parent.
- For Pi extension repos under `~/.pi/agent/extensions`, put lane worktrees outside extension auto-discovery, such as `~/.pi/agent/worktrees`.
- Preserve capability ceilings, including child tool limits and allowed-agent restrictions.
- Preserve parent authority and escalate unresolved choices.
- Treat receipts, CI, review bots, and external-run records as evidence, not authority.
- For backlog maintenance, releases, merge queues, or other public-repo mutation policy, load the matching user/project skill. This package defines delegation primitives, not private policy.
- As a conservative orchestration policy, do not pass a hard `toolBudget` or tight `usageBudget` to mutation-capable workers. The default tool budget blocks read/search tools rather than mutation tools. If interrupted after a tool call starts, checkpoint after the current tool returns with changed files, build/test state, and commit or PR state.

# Pi Subagents: Review And Validation

Generic review and delivery guidance for operator-authorized delegated work. This file does not encode private backlog, merge, or release policy.

## Delivery loop

Use the smallest loop that proves the change:

1. Inspect the source, diff, issue, or plan directly.
2. Keep one writer for each cwd or worktree.
3. Run focused validation that can fail for the changed behavior.
4. When the operator/project delegation contract calls for independent review, use a fresh-context read-only reviewer; otherwise parent inspection is valid.
5. Apply only accepted findings inside the same writer boundary.
6. Re-run affected validation and review only the changed blast radius.
7. Inspect the final diff and evidence before parent acceptance.

Skip review ceremony for trivial wording, renames, or local-only probes when direct parent inspection is enough.

## Review shape

| Situation | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| One coherent diff or one risk | one reviewer |
| Independent risks, such as correctness, tests, security, or UI | parallel reviewers with distinct contracts |
| Possible over-scope or needless complexity | same-writer challenge before fresh review |
| Material design tradeoff | council mode |

Reviewers are fresh-context by default. Use the ordinary `reviewer` role for routine code review. Forked oracle/advisor runs are escalation-only for parent-history, drift, root-cause, model-routing, or hard tradeoff evidence.

## Finding disposition

The parent classifies each finding against current HEAD:

- **Valid blocker:** concrete failure, repro, security issue, contract mismatch, or source-proven regression. Fix now.
- **Valid non-blocker:** real but outside the delivery slice. Record or defer.
- **Stale:** fixed or absent at the reviewed head. Cite current evidence.
- **Invalid:** contradicted by source, tests, docs, or user-approved scope. Cite the contradiction.
- **Out of policy/scope:** needs unapproved product, architecture, authority, release, or public-repo action. Escalate.
- **Speculative:** no contract, repro, or reachable failure. Do not block.

A clean reviewer result is evidence, not publication authority.

## Gate-failure triage

When validation fails:

1. Confirm the run belongs to the exact head/ref under judgment.
2. Read the focused failing logs first.
3. Name the failing test, assertion, contract, or thread.
4. Classify cause: current diff, stale test, environment/setup, or existing flake.
5. Reproduce locally when practical with the narrowest command.
6. Patch forward when the current diff caused it.
7. For stale/flaky failures, collect proof before one rerun or residual-risk note.
8. Re-run the affected command or exact-head gate after every fix.

For bot comments, classify each thread as valid, stale, invalid, or out of policy before assigning severity.

## Final checklist

Before reporting delegated work as done, verify the relevant subset:

- final diff contains only intended files
- focused validation covers changed behavior
- required independent review has fresh-review evidence
- accepted findings are fixed and revalidated
- publication authority exists before push, comment, close, merge, deploy, or release
- external checks are exact-head when used as evidence
- handoff is durable before cleanup
- residual risks, skipped validation, and blocked decisions are explicit

## Public/private boundary

For issue/PR backlogs, releases, merge queues, contributor credit, or repo-specific policy, load the matching user/project skill when available. Keep those rules out of this public package until intentionally released.

## Findings

1. **[P2] Compact actions never return inline when space becomes available** — `src/components/InboxList.vue:214–215`  
   Once a row becomes compact, `scrollWidth` is at least `clientWidth`; adding the positive actions-minus-toggle width therefore cannot satisfy this inequality, even after widening the viewport. The supplied current-source probe confirms that the same mount remains compact at 1440px, while a fresh mount renders inline actions. The rendered test misses this because its wide scenario remounts the app. Measure the expanded content’s required width rather than adding to the filled row’s `scrollWidth`, and test widening the existing compact mount.

2. **[P2] Clicking action-panel padding opens the conversation** — `src/components/InboxList.vue:459–465`  
   The new disclosure panel stops propagation only on its buttons, not its container. Clicking the panel’s padding or gaps consequently reaches the row’s open handler and replaces the list with the reader. This is reproduced in the fingerprint-matched `compact-followup-probes.json` (`panelGapClick.reader: true`). Stop click propagation on the action-panel container and cover a background/padding click alongside the existing button-center probes.

3. **[P2] New date assertions depend on the runner’s locale and timezone** — `tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts:440–442`; `tests/inbox-list.component.test.ts:60–65`  
   Chrome is launched without pinning its locale/timezone, but the rendered test requires the exact British label `30 Sept 2001`; an `en-US` browser formats that date differently. Separately, freezing `Date.now()` does not freeze the calendar zone: under `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati`, the component fixture’s first three dates group as Yesterday/Today/Yesterday rather than the expected Today/Yesterday. Control locale and timezone in these test environments, or make expectations explicitly follow the selected environment; retain the separate timezone-specific date-helper tests.

4. **[P2] Decode file URLs before using them as Vite filesystem roots** — `tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts:76`; `tests/disclosure-focus.rendered.test.ts:64`  
   `new URL('..', import.meta.url).pathname` remains URL-encoded. In a checkout such as `/tmp/email os`, both browser tests therefore start Vite against `/tmp/email%20os/`, not the repository, and fail while waiting for the preview. Windows drive paths are also not converted correctly. Use Node’s `fileURLToPath` to obtain the filesystem root in both tests.

5. **[P2] Reply tests now activate central content while it is inert** — `tests/drafts.component.test.ts:25–28,73–79`  
   The changed mount helper opens Drafts for every test, after which the reply scenarios programmatically click the covered conversation row and reader controls without dismissing that drawer. These activations bypass the new `inert` interaction boundary and leave Drafts pre-opened, so the existing reply gates no longer exercise the real Inbox → Reader → Reply → Drafts transition or its new automatic drawer routing. Close the utility drawer before entering each reader/reply scenario, then assert that Reply opens the drafts surface itself.

**Overall verdict: correct — no blocking findings within this review angle.** All findings above are report-only P2 issues under the requested priority policy.

## Findings

1. **[P2] Compact rows never expand again when space returns** — `src/components/InboxList.vue:214–215`  
   Once compact, `scrollWidth` is at least `clientWidth`; adding the positive action-minus-toggle width therefore cannot satisfy this condition, even when flex children have ample spare room. The current-source `compact-followup-probes.json` confirms that resizing the same mounted app from 1000px to 1440px leaves only “More actions” visible, while a fresh 1440px mount displays all actions. Measure the minimum required expanded width rather than adding to the already stretched row’s `scrollWidth`, and cover compact→expanded resizing without remounting.

2. **[P2] Collapsing actions drops keyboard focus instead of handing it to More** — `src/components/InboxList.vue:219–220`  
   When resizing hides a focused inline action, changing `compactRows` provides no focus handoff. The requested narrow current-source Chrome probe (`focus-resize-probe.json`) reproduces this: focus Archive on conv-01 at 1440px/20px, then shrink the same app to 1000px; focus becomes `BODY`, and the next native Tab lands on conv-02’s read control, changing the conversation context. Before collapsing, record whether the action group owns focus; afterward, move that focus to the same row’s disclosure toggle without scrolling.

3. **[P2] Clicking disclosure-panel padding opens the conversation** — `src/components/InboxList.vue:459–465`  
   The disclosed action container does not stop click propagation; only its buttons do. Its newly added padding and gaps therefore bubble clicks to the row’s open handler. The current-source `compact-followup-probes.json` records a hit on `SPAN.row-actions` inside the panel followed by the reader opening and the list disappearing. Stop propagation on the action-group container so the entire disclosed surface remains row-action context rather than an accidental conversation-open target.

4. **[P2] An empty display name hides a known contact mailbox** — `src/components/ContactPane.vue:29–30`  
   For `{ displayName: '', mailbox: 'anon@example.test' }`, `nameLabel()` returns an empty string, while the mailbox’s truthiness check suppresses its separate rendering. The pane consequently displays neither the known identity nor the unavailable-information disclosure. This input is reachable from a valid `From: "" <anon@example.test>`: mailparse preserves the empty quoted display name and `gmail/provider.rs:1764–1767` copies it unchanged. Use a consistent nonempty-name predicate for the fallback and secondary mailbox, and add an empty-display-name component case.

content.text:
## Findings

1. **[P2] Preserve the Inbox anchor when Activity opens another reader** — `src/App.vue:271–272`  
   Opening Activity while already reading leaves `InboxList` unmounted. Activity’s Open handler calls `captureListOrigin()` again, replacing the saved anchor with `null`; Back therefore loses the original scroll position. The current-source Chrome probe recorded scrollTop **170 → 0** after Back, with the focused row offscreen; explicit Inbox navigation subsequently revealed it at **236**, not the original position. Preserve the existing anchor when no list is mounted. Evidence: `interaction-probes.json`, `inboxBefore` / `inboxAfterBack` / `inboxAfterRailInbox`.

2. **[P2] Fence deferred editor activation against later rail navigation** — `src/App.vue:139–140`  
   With draft A dirty and its save ACK held, clicking **New draft**, then **Activity**, creates competing protected transitions. After the ACK, the delayed editor activation invokes this unconditional watcher and leaves **Local drafts** visible instead of the later Activity destination. The current-source probe confirmed draft B was created and both backend drafts survived; this is navigation ownership failure, **not demonstrated data loss**. Serialize these transitions or associate them with navigation generations so the latest destination wins after safely releasing the correct editor. Evidence: `interaction-probes.json`, `raceAfterActivityPending` / `raceAfterSaveAck`.

3. **[P2] Let Escape reach the protected Drafts drawer-close path** — `src/App.vue:470–472`  
   Once any draft is active, this early return suppresses Escape before disclosure handling—even with a clean draft and focus on the drawer’s Close button. The current-source native-key probe confirmed Escape left both drawer and composer open. That contradicts the new utility-disclosure Escape contract. Handle disclosure Escape before the composer’s mailbox-shortcut guard, retaining the IME/native-control exclusions and existing flush-and-close protection. Evidence: `interaction-probes.json`, `cleanDraftBeforeEscape` / `cleanDraftAfterEscape`.

**Overall verdict: correct, with three report-only P2 findings; no P0/P1 findings in this angle.**

Evidence above is parent-run synthetic confirmation, not reviewer-executed commands. Native/WKWebView and assistive-technology behavior remain unverified.
