All three fresh-context reviews are complete. **No P0 or P1 findings.** The two previously fixed P1s remain resolved in the reviewed state.

**Merge verdict: OK with notes.**

### Fixes worth doing now

None under the requested P0/P1 threshold. No code changes were made during this review.

### Optional improvements — 10 distinct P2 findings

| Finding | Location | Suggested correction |
|---|---|---|
| **Compact rows never restore inline actions after widening** | [`InboxList.vue:214`](src/components/InboxList.vue#L214) | Measure required expanded content width rather than adding to the already-filled row’s `scrollWidth`. Test resizing the same mount. |
| **Compaction drops keyboard focus** | [`InboxList.vue:219`](src/components/InboxList.vue#L219) | Before hiding a focused action, capture focus ownership and transfer it to that row’s More toggle. Chrome confirmed focus currently falls to `BODY`. |
| **Panel-padding clicks open the conversation** | [`InboxList.vue:459`](src/components/InboxList.vue#L459) | Stop propagation on the action-panel container, not just its buttons. |
| **Empty display names hide known contact addresses** | [`ContactPane.vue:29–30`](src/components/ContactPane.vue#L29) | Use a consistent nonempty-name check and fall back to the mailbox. |
| **Nested Activity navigation loses the Inbox anchor** | [`App.vue:271`](src/App.vue#L271) | Preserve the saved anchor when the list is unmounted. The probe reproduced scroll changing from 170 to 0. |
| **Deferred editor activation overrides later navigation** | [`App.vue:139`](src/App.vue#L139) | Fence or serialize navigation intents. New draft → Activity during a held save ends on Drafts after the ACK. |
| **Escape cannot close an active Drafts drawer** | [`App.vue:470`](src/App.vue#L470) | Route eligible disclosure Escape through protected close handling before suppressing composer shortcuts. |
| **Date tests assume particular locale/timezone settings** | [`rendered-layout.test.ts:440`](tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts#L440), [`component test:63`](tests/inbox-list.component.test.ts#L63) | Control those environments or derive expectations from the explicitly selected locale/calendar zone. |
| **Browser-test roots use URL-encoded filesystem paths** | [`rendered-layout.test.ts:76`](tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts#L76), [`disclosure test:64`](tests/disclosure-focus.rendered.test.ts#L64) | Use `fileURLToPath`; `.pathname` breaks checkouts containing spaces. |
| **Reply tests bypass the new inert boundary** | [`drafts.component.test.ts:25`](tests/drafts.component.test.ts#L25), [`73`](tests/drafts.component.test.ts#L73) | Close Drafts before entering the reader, then assert Reply opens Drafts itself. Current programmatic clicks bypass realistic interaction ownership. |

- Duplicate reports were consolidated.
- The suspected loss of **“Read state unknown”** from Chrome’s accessibility tree was disproven.
- The draft race demonstrated navigation override, **not data loss or a hidden new editor**.
- Native/WKWebView/VoiceOver verification remains a separate pending gate.
- The reviewed diff remained unchanged throughout.

---
name: github-cli
description: Use this skill when the user wants to interact with GitHub via the `gh` CLI — cloning repositories, inspecting dependencies or third-party projects, checking GitHub Actions pipeline logs or statuses, viewing workflow runs, and ad-hoc GitHub API calls. Triggers on tasks like "clone this repo", "check the pipeline", "view CI logs", "what's the status of the workflow", "find a dependency repo", or "inspect a GitHub project".
compatibility: Requires the `gh` CLI installed, on PATH, and authenticated. Verify with `gh auth status`; run `gh auth login` if not logged in.
---

# GitHub CLI (`gh`) Skill

Use this skill to interact with GitHub from the terminal using the `gh` CLI. Covers cloning repos for inspection/learning, checking GitHub Actions pipeline logs and statuses, and ad-hoc GitHub API/GraphQL calls.

## Setup

Ensure `gh` is installed and authenticated before running any commands.

```bash
gh --version         # current gh version
gh auth status       # show logged-in account, active status, token scopes
gh auth login        # interactive login flow (browser/device code)
gh auth refresh      # refresh token / request additional scopes
```

Auth state is stored in the OS keyring. `gh` also configures `git` to use the authenticated account for HTTPS pushes (`gh auth setup-git`).

## Global conventions

These flags apply to most commands and make `gh` scriptable/agent-safe:

| Flag | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `-R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO` | Run a command against a different repo than the cwd. Use instead of `cd`-ing into a clone. |
| `--json fields` | Output JSON with the specified fields (best for parsing). |
| `-q, --jq expression` | Filter JSON output with a jq expression. |
| `-t, --template string` | Format JSON output with a Go template (see `gh help formatting`). |
| `--web` / `-w` | Open the relevant page in the browser instead of printing. |
| `--help` | Show help for a command. |

**Automation pattern:** prefer `--json` (optionally with `-q`) for parsing, plain output for grepping. When targeting a repo you don't have checked out locally, use `-R owner/repo` instead of cloning just to inspect.

**Discovery:** every command supports `--help`. For a full reference run `gh help` or `gh help reference`.

## Cloning repositories (inspecting dependencies / learning)

`gh repo clone` resolves `OWNER/REPO` (or a full URL, or a bare repo name = your own account), uses your configured git protocol, and automatically wires up an `upstream` remote when the repo is a fork.

```bash
# Clone a dependency / third-party project to inspect
gh repo clone cli/cli                       # OWNER/REPO -> ./cli
gh repo clone cli/cli workspace/cli         # clone into a specific directory
gh repo clone https://github.com/cli/cli    # explicit URL (overrides git_protocol config)
gh repo clone git@github.com:cli/cli.git    # SSH URL

# Shallow / partial clones (faster for read-only inspection) — pass git flags after --
gh repo clone cli/cli -- --depth=1
gh repo clone cli/cli -- --depth=1 --filter=blob:none   # blobless clone

# When the repo is a fork, the parent is added as `upstream` (configurable)
gh repo clone octocat/Hello-World --upstream-remote-name=octocat
```

When you only want to *read* a repo without cloning, prefer `gh repo view` / `gh repo view --web` / `gh api` instead of cloning.

```bash
gh repo view cli/cli                    # README + metadata, no clone
gh repo view cli/cli --web             # open in browser
gh repo view cli/cli --json name,description,defaultBranchRef
```

## Finding repositories to inspect

```bash
# Search across GitHub (repos, code, issues, prs, commits)
gh search repos "cli github" --language go --sort stars --limit 20
gh search repos --owner cli            # repos owned by a user/org
gh search code "fn main" --repo cli/cli
gh search issues "panic on nil" --repo cli/cli --state open

# List repos you own / an org owns
gh repo list                           # your repos
gh repo list cli --limit 50           # an org's repos
gh repo list --fork --source          # filter forks/sources
```

## GitHub Actions: pipeline statuses and logs

Two command groups: `gh run` (individual workflow runs) and `gh workflow` (workflow definitions).

### Listing and viewing runs

```bash
gh run list                            # recent runs in the cwd repo
gh run list --limit 20                 # more runs
gh run list -R owner/repo              # runs in a different repo (no clone needed)
gh run list --workflow build.yml       # filter by workflow file
gh run list --branch main --status failure
gh run list --json databaseId,status,conclusion,headBranch,workflowName --limit 10

gh run view                            # interactively pick a run to view
gh run view 12345                      # view a specific run (summary + jobs)
gh run view 12345 -v                   # verbose: show job steps
gh run view 12345 -R owner/repo        # view a run in another repo
```

### Reading logs

```bash
gh run view 12345 --log                # full log for the run (all jobs)
gh run view 12345 --log-failed         # only failed steps (best for debugging CI)
gh run view --job 67890 --log          # log for a specific job
gh run view 12345 --web                # open the run in the browser
```

### Watching, rerunning, cancelling, downloading artifacts

```bash
gh run watch                          # interactively watch the latest run until it finishes
gh run watch 12345                    # watch a specific run (exit non-zero if it fails with --exit-status)
gh run watch 12345 --exit-status

gh run rerun 12345                    # rerun all failed jobs (or --failed)
gh run rerun 12345 --failed
gh run cancel 12345
gh run delete 12345
gh run download 12345                 # download artifacts to ./ by default
gh run download 12345 -D ./artifacts --name build-output
```

### Workflows

```bash
gh run list --workflow build.yml
gh workflow list                      # workflows defined in the repo
gh workflow view build.yml
gh workflow view build.yml --web
gh workflow run build.yml             # trigger a workflow_dispatch
gh workflow run build.yml --ref main -f environment=staging
gh workflow enable / disable build.yml
```

`gh run list` / `gh run view` accept `-R owner/repo`, so you can check pipeline status of a dependency or upstream repo **without cloning it** — useful for "is upstream CI green?" checks.

## Cross-cutting tips

- **No-clone inspection:** for read-only checks (status, README, releases, CI state), use `-R owner/repo` with `gh run list` / `gh repo view` / `gh release list` rather than cloning.
- **JSON + jq:** `--json` + `-q '.[] | .name'` is the most reliable way to extract specific fields.
- **Pipeline debugging flow:** `gh run list --status failure` → pick run id → `gh run view <id> --log-failed` to jump straight to failing step logs.
- **Branch context:** most `gh run` commands support `--branch`, `--event`, `--status`, `--workflow` filters.
- **Default repo:** `gh repo set-default` marks a repo as default for the cwd, so `gh pr` / `gh issue` / `gh run` resolve without `-R`. Useful when working inside a clone.

## Other commonly used commands (summary)

- **`gh pr`** — list/view/checkout/diff/merge/review PRs (`gh pr checkout 123`, `gh pr view --web`, `gh pr diff`, `gh pr checks`).
- **`gh issue`** — list/view/create/close issues.
- **`gh release`** — list/view/create/download releases (`gh release download`).
- **`gh gist`** — create/list/view gists (paste snippets).
- **`gh browse`** — open the current repo / a PR / an issue / a file in the browser.
- **`gh status`** — overview of relevant issues/PRs/notifications across your repos.
- **`gh api`** — make an authenticated REST v3 or GraphQL v4 request directly (escape hatch for anything not exposed by a subcommand).
- **`gh search`** — search repos, code, issues, PRs, commits across all of GitHub.

### `gh api` escape hatch

```bash
gh api repos/cli/cli                       # GET a REST endpoint
gh api repos/cli/cli/releases/latest --jq .tag_name
gh api graphql -f query='query { viewer { login } }'
gh api repos/cli/cli/contents/README.md    # fetch a file's metadata/content
gh api -X POST repos/cli/cli/labels -f name=foo -f color=ff0000
```

Placeholders `{owner}`, `{repo}`, `{branch}` are filled from the cwd repo (or `GH_REPO`). Prefer the dedicated subcommands when they exist; reach for `gh api` only for endpoints `gh` doesn't wrap.

## Reference

- Built-in help: `gh --help`, `gh <command> --help`, or `gh help <command>` for prose.
- Full reference: `gh help reference`.
- Formatting/JSON: `gh help formatting`.
- Exit codes: `gh help exit-codes`.
- Manual: https://cli.github.com/manual

# exe.dev

Use exe.dev to run small services on persistent Linux VMs with automatic HTTPS at `https://<vm>.exe.xyz/`. It is SSH-native: there is no dedicated CLI binary. For current syntax and capabilities, consult the [docs index](https://exe.dev/docs.md), [agent skill](https://exe.dev/docs/agent-skill.md), or [all docs](https://exe.dev/docs/all.md) rather than relying on remembered flags.

## The critical SSH distinction

There are two different destinations:

- **The lobby (`ssh exe.dev`)** is a restricted command interface for VM and account operations. It is not a shell and does not support arbitrary commands, `scp`, or `sftp`.
- **A VM (`ssh <vm>.exe.xyz`)** is a normal Linux host. Use it for shells, copying files, port forwarding, building, and running services.

Targeting the lobby when you meant the VM is the most common source of SSH, copy, and remote-command failures. In scripts and CI, use `StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new` on the first connection so host-key prompts do not block unattended work. Pin the intended identity for both host patterns in SSH config when multiple keys are available.

## Authentication and account model

Authentication uses the registered SSH key; there is no separate exe.dev password. Confirm access before making changes. Accounts are pinned to one VM region, and VMs share underlying capacity, so choose resource sizes based on the service rather than creating large machines by default.

For automation, the HTTPS API mirrors lobby operations through `POST https://exe.dev/exec` with a bearer token. Generate tokens with an explicit short expiry, restrict their allowed commands, and never put secrets in token payloads, logs, images, or committed files. The API has no interactive stdin/PTY and has request and timeout limits, so use direct VM SSH for work that needs a shell or long-running process.

## Durable deployment guidance

A typical deployment has these decisions, in this order:

1. **Discover before mutating.** Check whether a suitable VM already exists and inspect its status, image, region, and current sharing configuration. Use machine-readable output in scripts.
2. **Choose the customization path.** SSH in and build for a one-off or actively developed service; use a reproducible OCI image for repeatable deployments; use a bounded first-boot setup script for small bootstrap tasks. Treat setup scripts as one-time operations and keep them reviewable.
3. **Run and expose deliberately.** Make the service listen on the expected port, configure the proxy for that port, and verify the HTTPS endpoint. Keep the default authenticated/private visibility unless public access is explicitly required. Dev servers may need their host allow-list configured for `*.exe.xyz`.
4. **Share the minimum access.** Prefer named users or teams when access should be controlled. Public sharing removes authentication; links and team access still need explicit revocation planning.
5. **Operate and clean up.** Inspect resource metrics and service health before resizing. Persistent disks survive sessions, but disk growth is one-way. Deleting a VM is destructive; confirm the target and preserve data before teardown.

The lobby supports VM creation, inspection, sharing, domains, integrations, resource changes, and deletion; use its built-in help or the official docs for exact commands and flags. Integrations include HTTP proxies (including header injection), GitHub access, and a managed LLM gateway. Keep provider credentials in integrations or environment management rather than baking them into images.

## HTTPS, domains, and integrations

Every VM receives TLS termination and a hostname. A single selected port can be made public; alternate proxied ports remain authenticated. Reverse-proxy headers identify the original request and should be handled by the application appropriately.

A custom domain requires a correctly configured CNAME before registering it with exe.dev. Verify DNS and certificate status after the change. Integrations can attach to one VM, a tag, or all current and future VMs; review scope carefully, especially for integrations carrying credentials or disabling authentication.

The default LLM integration may provide provider access without storing API keys on the VM. Treat the VM identity and monthly allocation as the authorization boundary, and consult the [LLM gateway docs](https://exe.dev/docs/shelley/llm-gateway.md) for endpoint details.

## Safety checklist

- Separate lobby operations from commands inside the VM.
- Inspect names and machine-readable state before destructive or paid changes.
- Keep SSH/API credentials and application secrets out of transcripts, repos, images, and setup scripts where possible.
- Use private visibility by default and grant the narrowest sharing scope.
- Verify the live HTTPS endpoint after deployment or proxy changes.
- Use official help/docs when an option or behavior is uncertain; do not infer flags from another CLI.

# GitHub Integration


Instead of [setting up a GitHub personal access token](faq/github-token),
the GitHub integration connects your GitHub account to exe.dev so that you
can work on private repos without managing tokens, and without having
tokens on the VM itself.

## Linking your GitHub account

Link your GitHub account from the [Integrations page](/integrations).

The exe.dev GitHub App will need to be installed into your account or into
your organization. If someone else has already installed it, you may need
to sign into your account instead of clicking the install button.

## Creating repo integrations

Once connected, create per-repo integrations:

```
exe.dev ▶ integrations add github --name blog --repository ghuser/blog --attach vm:my-vm
Added integration blog

Usage from a VM:
  ssh my-vm.exe.xyz 'cd $(mktemp -d) && git clone https://github.int.exe.xyz/ghuser/blog.git'
```

Then, from inside the VM:

```
git clone https://github.int.exe.xyz/ghuser/blog.git
```

## Acting as your user (`--act-as-user`)

By default the integration acts as the exe.dev GitHub App, so pushes
show up as `exe-dev-github-integration[bot]`. Pass `--act-as-user` on
`integrations add github` or `integrations edit` (or use the toggle in
the web UI) to authenticate as your GitHub user instead, attributing
activity to your account. Not available on team integrations.

## Read-only integrations (`--readonly`)

Pass `--readonly` on `integrations add github` or `integrations edit`
(or check "Read-only" in the web UI) to allow reads but not writes, for
both the API and git.

## Using the `gh` CLI

The integration also supports the GitHub CLI (`gh`). Set `GH_HOST` to the
aggregate integration hostname:

```
export GH_HOST=github.int.exe.xyz
gh repo view ghuser/blog
gh issue list -R ghuser/blog
gh pr list -R ghuser/blog
```

arguments.content:
## Summary

Implement the first Superhuman-inspired browsing slice on the existing Vue/Tauri/Rust mail foundation, plus the committed browsing roadmap and shared factory validation configuration.

- Replace the competing list/reader columns with a compact warm-dark browsing shell: persistent rail, chronological one-line conversation rows, central list-or-reader mode, and correspondent context.
- Use account-scoped conversation identity for focus and action targeting, preserving surviving focus and list scroll anchors through ordinary reader round trips and incoming-mail updates.
- Add optional Rust-owned/generated `primaryCorrespondent` metadata from the newest cached message's exact From address; moving list focus does not fetch message bodies or mutate read state.
- Rehouse Account, Activity, and local Drafts in explicit disclosures while retaining permission, draft-save, normal-close, and recovery entry points.
- Make the covered central surface inert while utility/Contact disclosures are open, preventing native keyboard activation of hidden mailbox actions.
- Adapt overflowing row actions to a named “More actions” disclosure, retaining readable subjects, pending/read/date information, and keyboard/pointer routes at the tested larger-text breakpoint.
- Add component/core/transport coverage and opt-in real-Chrome regression tests. No new dependencies, provider permissions, database migrations, or automatic mark-as-read behavior.

The PR also includes `.pi/factory.json`, its narrow Git ignore exception, the incremental implementation roadmap, and the UX-01 contract/evidence notes. It does not implement later search, bulk selection, Undo, additional splits, attachments, reminders, AI, calendar, or multi-account functionality.

## Validation

Independently passed locally on the reviewed application/test content:

- `mise run test:core`
- `mise run check:contract`
- `mise run lint:core`
- `mise run test:ui` — **205 passed**; three opt-in browser tests skipped in the default run
- `mise run typecheck`
- `mise run build:web`

The three opt-in tests also passed separately in real headless Chrome:

```sh
EMAIL_OS_DISCLOSURE_FOCUS_CHROME=/path/to/chrome \
  pnpm exec vitest run tests/disclosure-focus.rendered.test.ts
EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/path/to/chrome \
  pnpm exec vitest run tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts
```

They exercise native Tab/Shift+Tab, Enter and pointer input for covered-action protection/restored interaction, and rendered layout/action access at 1000px with 16px/20px root fonts, an older date, unknown read state, and pending membership. All mail/account data was synthetic; no real Gmail account, Google network, or mailbox mutations were used for VM validation.

The latest three fresh-context adversarial reviews found no P0/P1 issues; the P2 follow-ups below remain intentionally deferred. Local results are not a claim that GitHub CI, native packaging, or the macOS runtime passed.

## Platform gates still pending

- Native compile/test in this VM is blocked by missing GTK/WebKit development prerequisites.
- macOS native fixture/WKWebView, VoiceOver, full visual calibration, and broader browser/accessibility verification remain pending.
- This is not a certification for primary-mailbox dogfooding or behavioral equivalence to Superhuman.

## Deferred P2 review notes

These are report-only follow-ups, not claimed fixed by this PR:

1. A compact row does not return to inline actions when the same mounted app gains space.
2. Compaction can drop focus from an inline action instead of handing it to the same row's More toggle.
3. Clicking action-panel padding/gaps can bubble to the row and open the conversation.
4. An empty display name can hide a known contact mailbox.
5. Reader → Activity → another reader can overwrite the saved Inbox anchor.
6. A deferred draft activation can override a later rail navigation request; the tested case did not demonstrate data loss.
7. Active-draft shortcut suppression prevents Escape from reaching protected drawer-close handling.
8. Some date assertions depend on the runner's locale/timezone.
9. Browser-test Vite roots use URL `.pathname` rather than decoded filesystem paths, affecting checkouts with spaces.
10. Some reply component tests programmatically activate central content while the Drafts disclosure makes it inert, weakening real-flow coverage.

See `docs/superhuman-browsing-implementation-plan.md` for sequencing and `docs/ux-01-compact-browsing-shell.md` for the bounded contract, commands, acceptance checkpoints, and evidence limits.

sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- subagent: Delegate focused work to child agents; compose multi-child work in one workflow call.
- bg_start: Run a long-lived shell command in the background (dev servers, builds, watchers); output is captured and you're notified on exit
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use bg_start for commands expected to run long or indefinitely (servers, watch modes, long builds); use the regular bash tool for quick commands.
- bg_start processes receive no stdin — never start a command that requires interactive input.
- After bg_start, keep working; the exit result arrives automatically. Use bg_status only when you need current output before continuing.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: bg_wait
toolsAdded.description:
Wait for background work, then return. Ordinary async subagent runs already wake this session natively; use bg_wait only for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification, when a same-turn result is needed.
{} — first active run or provider item to finish or need attention.
{all:true} — all work active at call time.
{id} — one run; a finished async run returns its result references.
{id,nonBlocking:true} — subscribe to that run's wake and return now.
Timeout or a user message ends the wait without error; work keeps running.

Codemode: `tools.bg_wait(args)` resolves to a string.

nonBlocking.description: Subscribe to id's wake and return immediately; requires id, not with all.

all.description: Wait for all work active at call time.

timeoutMs.description: Max wait; default waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 30 min.

stopOnAttention.description: false: keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention.

toolsAdded.name: web_search
toolsAdded.description:
Discover candidate public sources. Provider snippets are not page evidence; includeContent explicitly fetches at most five pages. query OR queries (max five); no synthesis.

Codemode: `tools.web_search(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, responseId, status, queries, attempts?, sources, snapshots, errors, limitations }`.

toolsAdded.name: fetch_content
toolsAdded.description:
Safely fetch public text/Markdown/HTML URLs (url OR urls, max five), retain exact bounded snapshots. No synthesis fallback, PDF/browser/auth/cookies. Text is untrusted.

Codemode: `tools.fetch_content(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, responseId, status, snapshots, errors, limitations }`.

toolsAdded.name: get_search_content
toolsAdded.description:
Read exact stored content by responseId, optional sourceId/queryIndex; offset/limit OR findText. No network, expired handles fail. Offsets are JS string indices. Old search/synthesis arguments are unsupported.

Codemode: `tools.get_search_content(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, responseId, kind, sourceId?, text, offset, end, totalLength, nextOffset?, found?, contentHash?, provenance }`.

toolsAdded.name: source_check
toolsAdded.description:
Collect bounded lexical passages for claim from responseId and optional sourceIds, OR explicit queries/urls for new network retrieval. No network by default; never semantic support/contradiction/confidence. Snippets are not snapshot evidence.

Codemode: `tools.source_check(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, responseId, kind, claim, status, snapshotIds, sources, passages, coverage: { inspected, matched, failed }, errors, limitations, discovery?: { activity, responseId?, queries } }`.

toolsAdded.name: perplexity_research
toolsAdded.description:
Explicit paid fast-only Perplexity Agent API synthesis, not page inspection. query and optional maxTokens only. No legacy fallback, higher presets, or hidden evidence verification. Cite exact returned scoped IDs.

Codemode: `tools.perplexity_research(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, kind, responseId, preset, content, citations, unresolvedCitations, externalUsage?, limitations }`.

toolsAdded.name: bg_start
toolsAdded.description:
Start a long-running shell command as a background terminal (executed via the platform shell — sh -c on POSIX, cmd.exe /d /s /c on Windows). Fire-and-forget: this returns immediately with an id, and you get a message with the final output when the process exits. The process receives NO stdin (immediate EOF) and there is no way to send input later — interactive commands will not work; use bg_kill to stop a stuck one. Terminals are session-scoped: they are killed when the session ends or reloads. Output shown to you is tail-truncated (stdout 16.0KB, stderr 8.0KB); the full logs are captured to files and in the /ps viewer. Max 8 background terminals can run at once.

Codemode: `tools.bg_start(args)` resolves to a string.

command.description: Shell command line to run in the background (sh -c on POSIX, cmd.exe /d /s /c on Windows). It receives no stdin (EOF immediately); interactive commands will not work.

title.description: Short human-readable name shown in listings and the UI

toolsAdded.name: bg_status
toolsAdded.description:
Peek at a background terminal's status and current output (tail-truncated) without blocking. If the terminal already exited, this returns its final state.

Codemode: `tools.bg_status(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: bg_list
toolsAdded.description:
List all background terminals (running and settled) with pid, elapsed time, exit status, and output sizes.

Codemode: `tools.bg_list(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: bg_kill
toolsAdded.description:
Stop one or more running background terminals (SIGTERM to the whole process tree, escalating to SIGKILL). Returns each terminal's final state; already-settled ids are reported as such.

Codemode: `tools.bg_kill(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. A tool whose declaration returns an object resolves on failure too when it returned that object; check its fields. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /home/exedev/.local/share/mise/installs/pi/1.4.0/pi/docs/codemode.md first.

---
name: github-cli
description: Use this skill when the user wants to interact with GitHub via the `gh` CLI — cloning repositories, inspecting dependencies or third-party projects, checking GitHub Actions pipeline logs or statuses, viewing workflow runs, and ad-hoc GitHub API calls. Triggers on tasks like "clone this repo", "check the pipeline", "view CI logs", "what's the status of the workflow", "find a dependency repo", or "inspect a GitHub project".
compatibility: Requires the `gh` CLI installed, on PATH, and authenticated. Verify with `gh auth status`; run `gh auth login` if not logged in.
---

# GitHub CLI (`gh`) Skill

Use this skill to interact with GitHub from the terminal using the `gh` CLI. Covers cloning repos for inspection/learning, checking GitHub Actions pipeline logs and statuses, and ad-hoc GitHub API/GraphQL calls.

## Setup

Ensure `gh` is installed and authenticated before running any commands.

```bash
gh --version         # current gh version
gh auth status       # show logged-in account, active status, token scopes
gh auth login        # interactive login flow (browser/device code)
gh auth refresh      # refresh token / request additional scopes
```

Auth state is stored in the OS keyring. `gh` also configures `git` to use the authenticated account for HTTPS pushes (`gh auth setup-git`).

## Global conventions

These flags apply to most commands and make `gh` scriptable/agent-safe:

| Flag | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `-R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO` | Run a command against a different repo than the cwd. Use instead of `cd`-ing into a clone. |
| `--json fields` | Output JSON with the specified fields (best for parsing). |
| `-q, --jq expression` | Filter JSON output with a jq expression. |
| `-t, --template string` | Format JSON output with a Go template (see `gh help formatting`). |
| `--web` / `-w` | Open the relevant page in the browser instead of printing. |
| `--help` | Show help for a command. |

**Automation pattern:** prefer `--json` (optionally with `-q`) for parsing, plain output for grepping. When targeting a repo you don't have checked out locally, use `-R owner/repo` instead of cloning just to inspect.

**Discovery:** every command supports `--help`. For a full reference run `gh help` or `gh help reference`.

## Cloning repositories (inspecting dependencies / learning)

`gh repo clone` resolves `OWNER/REPO` (or a full URL, or a bare repo name = your own account), uses your configured git protocol, and automatically wires up an `upstream` remote when the repo is a fork.

```bash
# Clone a dependency / third-party project to inspect
gh repo clone cli/cli                       # OWNER/REPO -> ./cli
gh repo clone cli/cli workspace/cli         # clone into a specific directory
gh repo clone https://github.com/cli/cli    # explicit URL (overrides git_protocol config)
gh repo clone git@github.com:cli/cli.git    # SSH URL

# Shallow / partial clones (faster for read-only inspection) — pass git flags after --
gh repo clone cli/cli -- --depth=1
gh repo clone cli/cli -- --depth=1 --filter=blob:none   # blobless clone

# When the repo is a fork, the parent is added as `upstream` (configurable)
gh repo clone octocat/Hello-World --upstream-remote-name=octocat
```

When you only want to *read* a repo without cloning, prefer `gh repo view` / `gh repo view --web` / `gh api` instead of cloning.

```bash
gh repo view cli/cli                    # README + metadata, no clone
gh repo view cli/cli --web             # open in browser
gh repo view cli/cli --json name,description,defaultBranchRef
```

## Finding repositories to inspect

```bash
# Search across GitHub (repos, code, issues, prs, commits)
gh search repos "cli github" --language go --sort stars --limit 20
gh search repos --owner cli            # repos owned by a user/org
gh search code "fn main" --repo cli/cli
gh search issues "panic on nil" --repo cli/cli --state open

# List repos you own / an org owns
gh repo list                           # your repos
gh repo list cli --limit 50           # an org's repos
gh repo list --fork --source          # filter forks/sources
```

## GitHub Actions: pipeline statuses and logs

Two command groups: `gh run` (individual workflow runs) and `gh workflow` (workflow definitions).

### Listing and viewing runs

```bash
gh run list                            # recent runs in the cwd repo
gh run list --limit 20                 # more runs
gh run list -R owner/repo              # runs in a different repo (no clone needed)
gh run list --workflow build.yml       # filter by workflow file
gh run list --branch main --status failure
gh run list --json databaseId,status,conclusion,headBranch,workflowName --limit 10

gh run view                            # interactively pick a run to view
gh run view 12345                      # view a specific run (summary + jobs)
gh run view 12345 -v                   # verbose: show job steps
gh run view 12345 -R owner/repo        # view a run in another repo
```

### Reading logs

```bash
gh run view 12345 --log                # full log for the run (all jobs)
gh run view 12345 --log-failed         # only failed steps (best for debugging CI)
gh run view --job 67890 --log          # log for a specific job
gh run view 12345 --web                # open the run in the browser
```

### Watching, rerunning, cancelling, downloading artifacts

```bash
gh run watch                          # interactively watch the latest run until it finishes
gh run watch 12345                    # watch a specific run (exit non-zero if it fails with --exit-status)
gh run watch 12345 --exit-status

gh run rerun 12345                    # rerun all failed jobs (or --failed)
gh run rerun 12345 --failed
gh run cancel 12345
gh run delete 12345
gh run download 12345                 # download artifacts to ./ by default
gh run download 12345 -D ./artifacts --name build-output
```

### Workflows

```bash
gh run list --workflow build.yml
gh workflow list                      # workflows defined in the repo
gh workflow view build.yml
gh workflow view build.yml --web
gh workflow run build.yml             # trigger a workflow_dispatch
gh workflow run build.yml --ref main -f environment=staging
gh workflow enable / disable build.yml
```

`gh run list` / `gh run view` accept `-R owner/repo`, so you can check pipeline status of a dependency or upstream repo **without cloning it** — useful for "is upstream CI green?" checks.

## Cross-cutting tips

- **No-clone inspection:** for read-only checks (status, README, releases, CI state), use `-R owner/repo` with `gh run list` / `gh repo view` / `gh release list` rather than cloning.
- **JSON + jq:** `--json` + `-q '.[] | .name'` is the most reliable way to extract specific fields.
- **Pipeline debugging flow:** `gh run list --status failure` → pick run id → `gh run view <id> --log-failed` to jump straight to failing step logs.
- **Branch context:** most `gh run` commands support `--branch`, `--event`, `--status`, `--workflow` filters.
- **Default repo:** `gh repo set-default` marks a repo as default for the cwd, so `gh pr` / `gh issue` / `gh run` resolve without `-R`. Useful when working inside a clone.

## Other commonly used commands (summary)

- **`gh pr`** — list/view/checkout/diff/merge/review PRs (`gh pr checkout 123`, `gh pr view --web`, `gh pr diff`, `gh pr checks`).
- **`gh issue`** — list/view/create/close issues.
- **`gh release`** — list/view/create/download releases (`gh release download`).
- **`gh gist`** — create/list/view gists (paste snippets).
- **`gh browse`** — open the current repo / a PR / an issue / a file in the browser.
- **`gh status`** — overview of relevant issues/PRs/notifications across your repos.
- **`gh api`** — make an authenticated REST v3 or GraphQL v4 request directly (escape hatch for anything not exposed by a subcommand).
- **`gh search`** — search repos, code, issues, PRs, commits across all of GitHub.

### `gh api` escape hatch

```bash
gh api repos/cli/cli                       # GET a REST endpoint
gh api repos/cli/cli/releases/latest --jq .tag_name
gh api graphql -f query='query { viewer { login } }'
gh api repos/cli/cli/contents/README.md    # fetch a file's metadata/content
gh api -X POST repos/cli/cli/labels -f name=foo -f color=ff0000
```

Placeholders `{owner}`, `{repo}`, `{branch}` are filled from the cwd repo (or `GH_REPO`). Prefer the dedicated subcommands when they exist; reach for `gh api` only for endpoints `gh` doesn't wrap.

## Reference

- Built-in help: `gh --help`, `gh <command> --help`, or `gh help <command>` for prose.
- Full reference: `gh help reference`.
- Formatting/JSON: `gh help formatting`.
- Exit codes: `gh help exit-codes`.
- Manual: https://cli.github.com/manual

content.text:
## 4. Delivery sequence

### UX-01 — A compact inbox that can actually be browsed

**Journey:** Launch → move focus with J/K → see the correspondent → Enter/click → read → Escape/back to the same row and scroll position.

- Build the rail, compact top navigation and warm-dark tokens from the spec. Use constrained sender width, a one-line subject/snippet, trailing date/actions, lavender focus bar, nonselectable date groups and generous unused space below short lists.
- List mode shows contact context, not a message preview. Reader mode replaces the central list surface; rail and contact context remain. Account/Activity/drafts become explicit accessible surfaces instead of permanent competing columns. Keep freshness, pending/error indicators and recovery discoverable.
- Convert `selectedIndex` into explicit focused identity. Hover must not change focus/read state; inline actions stop propagation. Preserve existing archive/recovery controls and permission gates during the layout change.
- Render only known contact fields. Add a minimal backend-derived primary correspondent to the summary if needed; do not fetch an entire body on every J/K movement or guess the latest sender from the unordered participant list. No external enrichment.
- Use real cached/core data through existing list/detail IPC. Additive DTO changes require generator and transport tests. No new provider writes.

**E2E checkpoint:** Use a six-conversation synthetic scenario with long names, mixed read states and missing profile fields. Focus the fourth row, open it, return, and verify row identity, list scroll and contact context. Insert a newer row while focused: an action must still target the original ID. Test empty/loading/error states and narrow-desktop contact disclosure.

**Acceptance:** BROWSE-01, 05 (conversation portion), 17, 20. Screenshot measurements are image coordinates, not established CSS pixels; calibrate on the Mac rather than asserting pixel parity.

### UX-02 — Read a multi-message conversation without losing your place

**Journey:** Open a conversation → N/P between messages → O/Shift+O expand → inspect participant details → J/K to another conversation → return to the originating list.

- Add message focus, expansion and a purple focus cue; newest relevant message initially expanded. Use the existing cached message stack and safe text rendering.
- Keep reader scrolling separate from rail/header. Preserve expansion and scroll during background refresh and within the current visit; prune IDs removed remotely.
- Provide full known From/To/timestamps via disclosure. Hover/focus participant context temporarily, restore on exit; contact copy controls must not trigger navigation or drafting.
- J/K in the reader follows its originating list/context, not all cached mail. Loading a different thread disables stale destructive targets.
- Reply still targets the explicitly displayed latest source under Slice 04's checks; focusing an older message must not silently change the reply contract. Unknown Cc/Bcc/header data is absent, not fabricated.

**E2E checkpoint:** A three-message conversation with a long body, hostile literal markup and multiple participants. Exercise message versus conversation navigation, expansion, participant context, copy, reply exit and Back. Reorder/update the source list while reading; stable IDs and a surviving anchor must win.

**Acceptance:** Complete BROWSE-05; copy portion of 15. HTML-only/incomplete/retained snapshots keep their current disclosures and restrictions.

### UX-03 — Discover actions and navigate to recoverable mail

**Journey:** Cmd+K → “go to Done” → open a cached archived conversation → Back to the exact prior inbox context.

- Introduce the shared action catalog and context-aware keyboard dispatcher. Start with implemented actions only: open/back, Done/Not Done, explicit read controls, account/Activity/drafts destinations, and Inbox/cached Done.
- Palette has an input, keyboard-highlighted results, Enter execution, Escape/focus restoration and shortcut labels/tooltips. Editable controls and IME cannot invoke mailbox shortcuts.
- Left opens a small destination navigator; support `G`, then `E` with a documented proposed timeout. Inbox and cached Done reuse rows/reader and a context history stack.
- Add a Rust read query for known locally archived/recovery conversations, including retained snapshots. Label this coverage honestly: it is not provider-complete Done/All Mail. Do not define Done as every thread lacking INBOX; future Sent/Spam/Trash membership must stay distinct.
- Keep activity history independently retrievable as contexts expand; a filtered list must not accidentally filter out operation failures.

**E2E checkpoint:** Archive a fixture thread, navigate to cached Done through palette and pointer, open it and return. Deny capabilities, delay destination responses and type `e/s/h` in the palette: no wrong-thread mutation. Preserve local drafts and normal-close protection after moving their entry points.

**Acceptance:** BROWSE-10, 20 and folder return/keyboard precedence contracts. Cmd+K must be exercised in WKWebView, not just synthetic key events.

### UX-04 — Process one conversation with trustworthy Undo

**Journey:** E marks Done → row/count/focus update → Z within 10 seconds restores the exact prior target state; explicit read/unread has the same recovery discipline.

- Reuse existing durable setters and authoritative pending overlays. Add a concise notification with Undo and visible pending/confirmed/failed/unknown distinctions; accepted locally is not confirmed remotely.
- Add narrow Rust Undo eligibility/query and command contracts. Persist the original target IDs, prior **per-message** values for the affected dimension, expiry and linkage to the original operation. A UI timer or `setArchived(false)` against the thread's latest inventory is not sufficient.
- Undo atomically cancels still-unclaimed intent where safe, or stages an ordered compensating operation against the immutable targets. It must not touch a new incoming message or independent labels/star/read state.
- Initially support the latest eligible action only. Mixed read facts require restoring each prior value; unknown prior facts are not exactly undoable. Expiry and same-target newer actions are checked in Rust. Uncertain dispatched outcomes remain explicitly uncertain/reconciled, not falsely reported as undone.
- Use `Z`, not native text-editing Cmd+Z. Preserve Activity-based recovery after expiry and on restart.

**E2E checkpoint:** Archive → undo at 9 seconds; reject at expiry; archive last/only row; failure rollback; offline accept → restart → restore/reconcile; a new reply between action and Undo remains untouched. Check mixed read values and an older Undo after a newer same-target action.

**Acceptance:** BROWSE-07, 08. Fake clock/provider tests prove durable semantics; approved disposable-Mac tests prove remote convergence.

### UX-05 — Select and process several conversations safely

**Journey:** X / Shift+J/K / Cmd- or Shift-click select three rows → archive → inspect per-item results → recover failures or Undo the eligible group.

- Add selected-ID set/range anchor and explicit count; focus is not selection. Plain J/K never expands selection. Escape clears selection before leaving the list; changing context clears cross-context selection.
- Actions resolve exactly the selected set, otherwise the current conversation. Inline row actions remain explicitly row-scoped. Bulk read controls use a visible desired state rather than ambiguous mixed-state toggling.
- Add durable bounded group acceptance with member receipts/status, idempotent group request and immutable per-thread message targets. Do not treat frontend `Promise.all` as durable or atomic bulk execution.
- Reuse serial execution/reconciliation. Report accepted, succeeded, failed and unknown members separately; failed IDs remain actionable. Group Undo reuses UX-04's preimages and excludes unsafe/superseded members explicitly.
- “Select all loaded” means loaded rows only. Do not promise cross-page/all-matching selection.

**E2E checkpoint:** Select noncontiguous IDs, insert/reorder mail, archive, fail one member and lose another response. Verify precise targets, separate statuses and recovery after restart; returning from a reader must not widen selection.

**Acceptance:** BROWSE-06 (archive), 18; later star actions reuse the same selection mechanism.

### UX-06 — One real saved split, not a classification engine

**Journey:** Define a sender/domain view → switch Inbox/saved split by pointer or Tab → open/read/archive → see both memberships/counts update → disable the view without deleting mail.

- Implement the ADR's one local saved definition, initially bounded sender/domain criteria, stable ordering and optional hide-when-empty. Persist it in Rust/SQLite; add a small editor, no natural-language authoring.
- Reuse browsing contexts, reader, bulk actions, commands and Undo. Views derive membership and never mutate mail. Overlap with Inbox is intentional, not a duplicate-storage error.
- Define counts as total matching conversations, not unread. Render badges only for exact known totals 1…999; cached-only views disclose that scope, and unavailable mailbox totals are not presented as exact.
- Add single-active unread filter first, with unknown read facts not treated as unread. Choose/document nonwrapping split navigation until live evidence says otherwise. Hidden views remain reachable through the palette.
- Do not invent Important/Other classification from Gmail IMPORTANT or make those mutually exclusive storage folders. Existing-label criteria become available after UX-09.

**E2E checkpoint:** Save → restart → switch → open → archive → undo; verify overlapping views, focus/selection isolation, hiding and disabling. Synthetic exact counts 0/1/999/1000 exercise badge rules; timezone-boundary fixtures exercise date groups.

**Acceptance:** BROWSE-02, 03, 04 plus split membership/configuration contracts. Ship Inbox + one named saved split before broader split configuration.

### UX-07 — Find older mail and return without losing the query

**Journey:** / → enter query → Enter → result → reader → Back to query/results/focus → Back to previous split.

- Add search input/operator guidance and reuse the normal list/reader/action surfaces. Contact-name click becomes sender search; add up to four real recent-email links from a bounded query, not invented history.
- Add account-scoped Rust search and a bounded provider read path for older mail. Online search reaches beyond the 100-conversation inbox window; offline search uses cached content with an incompleteness disclosure. A failed search is not an empty result.
- Define a supported parser/AST for AND, OR, quoted phrases, exclusions and initial From/To/Subject criteria. Reject unsupported syntax visibly; do not silently give cached and provider modes different meanings. Add Cc/Bcc/label operators only when the requisite facts are available. Document fields, date/time and Spam/Trash defaults.
- Page/cancel provider work, guard account/context/query generations, deduplicate by conversation ID, and retain the query while loading details. Respect existing rate pacing and auth/cancellation.
- Bound search cache retention separately from inbox discovery; persist/pin any operation targets/recovery context before evicting results. Opening an uncached result is a visible load, never a substitute thread.

**E2E checkpoint:** Find an archived conversation absent from inbox discovery, page results, inspect it, return and edit the query. Force stale responses, offline incomplete coverage, expired auth, rate limits and a missing result body. Contact copy stays independent of search/draft exits.

**Acceptance:** BROWSE-09, 10, 15, 19 and archive-searchability from 07. This completes the initial browsing milestone; it does not complete the ADR's sending/dogfooding scope.

### UX-08 — Star a conversation and find it in Starred

**Journey:** S (or bulk Star) → indicator → go to Starred → unstar → correct neighbor/Back/Undo.

- Add observed per-message star facts, conversation aggregation, a narrow durable setter and reconciliation. Keep star independent of inbox/read state and feed the same group/Undo/catalog machinery.
- Starred becomes a real browsing destination. Add the starred filter once the facts exist, not before. Unknown/partial star facts must remain distinguishable where they affect correctness.

**E2E checkpoint:** Star archived mail, find it in Starred, unstar while browsing that view, fail/restart/reconcile and verify independent read/inbox facts and bulk scope.


[137 more lines in file. Use offset=205 to continue.]

The source fingerprint was unchanged throughout the checks; this evidence
  summary was added afterwards without changing application or test code.
- Eight targeted checks in real headless Chrome passed against the explicitly
  labelled synthetic, in-memory browser preview: contact growth and shrink
  focus handoffs, no focus theft from the list, Contact-to-Inbox dismissal,
  opening archived fixture mail from Activity, explicit Inbox overriding that
  origin, ordinary Escape preserving it, and a reader round trip preserving
  the focused ID, nonzero list scrollTop, and viewport offset.
- Browser dimensions were changed via Chrome's actual device-metrics API at
  999/1000 CSS px. The scroll round trip used real layout, not jsdom geometry.
  These were ad hoc parent validation probes, not a newly installed E2E runner;
  no real mailbox, native IPC, or provider behavior was exercised.

## Pending verification (not claimed as done)

- `mise run check:native` / `mise run test:native` — **blocked** in this
  environment: GTK/WebKit development prerequisites (`glib-sys`/`gobject-sys`
  via pkg-config) are absent, matching `docs/development.md`. Not reported as
  passed.
- `mise run dev:native` operator follow-up: actual WKWebView/native-fixture
  scroll/focus restoration, resize behavior, keyboard/VoiceOver walk-through,
  and the six-conversation journey. Targeted Chrome success does not satisfy
  those platform gates or prove native IPC persistence.
- Full visual calibration (~36px rhythm, warm-dark tokens), broader browser
  interaction/accessibility coverage, and exact Superhuman fidelity remain
  unverified. Neither synthetic Chrome nor native fixture success is evidence
  of real Gmail behavior.
- No-auto-read remains mandatory in every mode; any future change to that
  invariant requires its own approval.

**Next is UX-02: a polished, keyboard-first conversation reader.** The inbox now has the new browsing shell, but `ReaderView.vue` still displays every message expanded in a basic plain-text stack.

I’d sequence the UI work like this:

## 1. Small row-menu polish PR

Close the three rough edges directly introduced by the adaptive actions:
- Restore inline actions when space returns.
- Move focus to “More” when resizing hides the focused action.
- Stop panel-padding clicks from opening the conversation.

Keep this separate and small—not a sweep of the entire P2 backlog.

## 2. UX-02: conversation reading

| Area | User-visible result |
|---|---|
| **Reading layout** | Clear subject/header, quieter toolbar, readable typography and sensible text width |
| **Message stack** | Latest message expanded; older history collapsed into compact headers |
| **Message navigation** | `N`/`P` moves between messages, with a visible focus cue |
| **Expansion** | `O` expands the focused message; `Shift+O` expands all |
| **Conversation navigation** | `J`/`K` moves through the originating inbox list without returning to it |
| **Participant details** | Full known addresses/timestamps, temporary contact context, separate copy controls |
| **Return behavior** | Back restores the original row, context and scroll position |

Keep plain-text rendering, explicit read-state changes, and existing reply-safety checks. Focusing an older message must **not** silently change the reply recipient/source.

### Vertical-slice acceptance journey

```text
Open a three-message conversation
→ expand older history
→ navigate messages with N/P
→ inspect/copy a participant address
→ move to the next conversation with J
→ return to the original inbox position
```

Validate that journey in real Chrome, including a background refresh and a removed conversation. Then run the native fixture checkpoint on macOS/WKWebView; that remains unverified today.

## 3. After the reader: command discovery

Then build **UX-03: Cmd+K and destination navigation**. It will expose existing actions and recovery paths without requiring new mailbox capabilities.

**Recommendation:** one small menu-polish PR, then the reader slice from the [implementation plan](docs/superhuman-browsing-implementation-plan.md). That’s the biggest next improvement to the daily browse/read loop.

content.text:
---
name: pi-subagents
description: |
  Delegate work to Pi subagents after the operator asks for it: one child,
  parallel or scripted workflows, async runs, resume/steer/stop, review fanout,
  and multi-lane or worktree orchestration.
---

# Pi Subagents

The parent works directly by default. Invoke subagents only when the operator
requested delegation in the current request or through applicable user/project
instructions. Task size, complexity, risk, tool-call count, recipe fit, or an
available specialist does not independently authorize delegation.

Once authorized, choose the smallest bounded shape that earns its token and
elapsed-time overhead through evidence, independent review, specialization,
useful parallelism, or isolation. A single child is valid. The parent keeps
intent, routing, decisions, final acceptance, and publication authority, and
does the work itself where that is cheaper.

## Calls

```typescript
subagent({ agent: "worker", task: "<brief>" })                    // one child; async by default
subagent({ workflow: "parallel", args: { tasks: [{ agent, task, cwd?, model? }] } })  // independent children
subagent({ workflow: true })              // runs the one ```js workflow block in this same reply
subagent({ workflow: "./lane.js", args }) // script file, path relative to the request cwd
subagent({ action: "validate", workflow: "./lane.js" })          // check a script without launching
subagent({ action: "status", id })        // options: { view: "fleet" } or { view: "transcript", index: 0 }
subagent({ action: "resume", id, message })   // completed or paused child; returns a new run id
subagent({ action: "steer", id, message })    // live async child
subagent({ action: "stop", id })              // ends the run; not resumable
subagent({ action: "interrupt", id })         // pauses the child's current turn
subagent({ action: "list" })  ·  subagent({ action: "models" })
subagent({ action: "guide", options: { topic: "<section address>" } })
```

Launches are async by default. Set `async: false` only when the parent must
block; final reviews and gates stay async. After launching, keep doing safe
independent work, or yield: native completion wakes this session. Do not sleep,
poll, or call `bg_wait` for ordinary children. Use `bg_wait` only for provider
or detached work that has no native notification and whose result this turn
needs.

## Workflow scripts

Use a script when later steps depend on earlier results, or for keyed,
retried, aggregated, or resumed children. Write one ```` ```js workflow ````
block in the reply and call `subagent({ workflow: true })` in the same reply.
For a long script, write it to a file and pass `workflow: "./path.js"`; calls in
one reply run at the same time, so write the file in one reply and `validate` or
launch it in the next. When a `workflow: true` call reports the block missing,
pass the source as `options: { script: "..." }` in place of `workflow: true` for
the rest of the turn: on some hosts, text after a tool call reaches the session
as a summary without the block.

```js workflow
const scan = await runs.run("scan", { label: "Map auth flow", agent: "scout", task: "..." });
const reviews = await runs.all([
  { key: "correctness", label: "Review auth correctness", agent: "reviewer", task: "... " + scan.output },
  { key: "tests", label: "Review auth tests", agent: "reviewer", task: "..." },
]);
return reviews.map((review) => review.output);
```

- Scripts are statement bodies with an explicit `return`, top-level `await`,
  and plain helpers. Nested async functions, arrows, and methods are rejected.
- Every `runs.run` / `runs.all` item needs a stable `key`. Add a short
  verb + behavior `label` unless the user gave one.
- Bind files with `output: "plans/x.md"` (relative paths land in run
  artifacts) and return `outputReference` or `artifactPaths`. A filename in
  task text does not route output. Never send reports to the repo root.
- `runs.lanes([{ key, stages: [...] }])` runs a predeclared plan: first stages
  together, later stages in order per lane.

Resuming a retained child:

```js workflow
let child = await runs.run("fix-1", { agent: "worker", task: "..." });
child = await runs.run("fix-2", { resume: child.runId, task: "Apply these accepted findings: ..." });
return child.output;
```

- Always resume the latest returned run id; every resume returns a new one.
- Use a new stable key for every resume pass.
- `resume` excludes `agent` and `gate`; the child keeps its agent, model, and tools.
- Resume a completed child; steer a live one. Top-level `{ action: "resume" }` is detached.

## Briefs

Every child starts cold. Its task states: goal; repo, explicit `cwd`, and
ref; authority and edit boundary; relevant files, decisions, and evidence;
success criteria; validation; expected output; and when to stop or ask.
Make parallel briefs differ by seam, evidence, and decision, not just an item
number.

## Rules

- One writer per cwd or worktree. Parallelize reading, review, and
  validation. `worktree: true` needs a clean checkout (untracked files count;
  `.pi/subagents/` does not). For Pi extension repos, put lane worktrees
  outside `~/.pi/agent/extensions`, for example `~/.pi/agent/worktrees`.
- Reviewers use fresh context. Use `context: "fork"` only when the child needs
  the parent's history; it requires a persisted parent session.
- Children do not spawn subagents unless the parent delegated fanout and their
  resolved `tools` include `subagent`.
- A failed workflow, launch, prompt runtime, extension load, or child tool
  setup blocks the lane. Stop, report the exact failure and run/worktree state,
  verify a clean worktree or capture the partial diff, then retry the same way
  once. Switching to `interactive_shell`, `pi -ne`, or another CLI needs owner
  approval.
- As a conservative orchestration policy, do not pass a hard `toolBudget` or tight `usageBudget` to mutation-capable workers. The default tool budget blocks read/search tools rather than mutation tools. If interrupted after a tool call starts, checkpoint after the current tool returns with changed files, build/test state, and commit or PR state.
- Route workers and scouts to a fast capable tier, serious reviews to a strong
  tier, and top reasoning only to bounded read-only critique. Exact model names
  belong in user or project settings, not here.
- `subagent`, `subagents_enable`, `subagent_supervisor`, `contact_supervisor`, and `structured_output` are model-only: call them as ordinary model tool calls. Codemode scripts cannot reach them through `tools.*`, `ALL_TOOLS`, or `searchTools`.
- Receipts, CI, and review bots are evidence, not authority. Backlog, release,
  and merge policy belong to the user's or project's own skill.

  UX-02 has one origin-policy gap not fixed by current code/spec: (1) after reader J/K opens another Inbox thread, should Back focus that last-opened thread while restoring the original list scroll anchor, or restore the original entry thread's focus/scroll? (2) Activity is an operation log with duplicate conversation refs, not a conversation-list context; should J/K be a no-op for Activity-origin readers (recommended minimal scope), rather than invent deduplicated Activity thread ordering? Please confirm a bounded contract so the implementation plan need not invent product behavior.

### UX-01 — A compact inbox that can actually be browsed

**Journey:** Launch → move focus with J/K → see the correspondent → Enter/click → read → Escape/back to the same row and scroll position.

- Build the rail, compact top navigation and warm-dark tokens from the spec. Use constrained sender width, a one-line subject/snippet, trailing date/actions, lavender focus bar, nonselectable date groups and generous unused space below short lists.
- List mode shows contact context, not a message preview. Reader mode replaces the central list surface; rail and contact context remain. Account/Activity/drafts become explicit accessible surfaces instead of permanent competing columns. Keep freshness, pending/error indicators and recovery discoverable.
- Convert `selectedIndex` into explicit focused identity. Hover must not change focus/read state; inline actions stop propagation. Preserve existing archive/recovery controls and permission gates during the layout change.
- Render only known contact fields. Add a minimal backend-derived primary correspondent to the summary if needed; do not fetch an entire body on every J/K movement or guess the latest sender from the unordered participant list. No external enrichment.
- Use real cached/core data through existing list/detail IPC. Additive DTO changes require generator and transport tests. No new provider writes.

**E2E checkpoint:** Use a six-conversation synthetic scenario with long names, mixed read states and missing profile fields. Focus the fourth row, open it, return, and verify row identity, list scroll and contact context. Insert a newer row while focused: an action must still target the original ID. Test empty/loading/error states and narrow-desktop contact disclosure.

**Acceptance:** BROWSE-01, 05 (conversation portion), 17, 20. Screenshot measurements are image coordinates, not established CSS pixels; calibrate on the Mac rather than asserting pixel parity.

### UX-02 — Read a multi-message conversation without losing your place

**Journey:** Open a conversation → N/P between messages → O/Shift+O expand → inspect participant details → J/K to another conversation → return to the originating list.

- Add message focus, expansion and a purple focus cue; newest relevant message initially expanded. Use the existing cached message stack and safe text rendering.
- Keep reader scrolling separate from rail/header. Preserve expansion and scroll during background refresh and within the current visit; prune IDs removed remotely.
- Provide full known From/To/timestamps via disclosure. Hover/focus participant context temporarily, restore on exit; contact copy controls must not trigger navigation or drafting.
- J/K in the reader follows its originating list/context, not all cached mail. Loading a different thread disables stale destructive targets.
- Reply still targets the explicitly displayed latest source under Slice 04's checks; focusing an older message must not silently change the reply contract. Unknown Cc/Bcc/header data is absent, not fabricated.

**E2E checkpoint:** A three-message conversation with a long body, hostile literal markup and multiple participants. Exercise message versus conversation navigation, expansion, participant context, copy, reply exit and Back. Reorder/update the source list while reading; stable IDs and a surviving anchor must win.

**Acceptance:** Complete BROWSE-05; copy portion of 15. HTML-only/incomplete/retained snapshots keep their current disclosures and restrictions.

### UX-03 — Discover actions and navigate to recoverable mail

**Journey:** Cmd+K → “go to Done” → open a cached archived conversation → Back to the exact prior inbox context.

- Introduce the shared action catalog and context-aware keyboard dispatcher. Start with implemented actions only: open/back, Done/Not Done, explicit read controls, account/Activity/drafts destinations, and Inbox/cached Done.
- Palette has an input, keyboard-highlighted results, Enter execution, Escape/focus restoration and shortcut labels/tooltips. Editable controls and IME cannot invoke mailbox shortcuts.
- Left opens a small destination navigator; support `G`, then `E` with a documented proposed timeout. Inbox and cached Done reuse rows/reader and a context history stack.
- Add a Rust read query for known locally archived/recovery conversations, including retained snapshots. Label this coverage honestly: it is not provider-complete Done/All Mail. Do not define Done as every thread lacking INBOX; future Sent/Spam/Trash membership must stay distinct.
- Keep activity history independently retrievable as contexts expand; a filtered list must not accidentally filter out operation failures.

**E2E checkpoint:** Archive a fixture thread, navigate to cached Done through palette and pointer, open it and return. Deny capabilities, delay destination responses and type `e/s/h` in the palette: no wrong-thread mutation. Preserve local drafts and normal-close protection after moving their entry points.

**Acceptance:** BROWSE-10, 20 and folder return/keyboard precedence contracts. Cmd+K must be exercised in WKWebView, not just synthetic key events.

### UX-04 — Process one conversation with trustworthy Undo

**Journey:** E marks Done → row/count/focus update → Z within 10 seconds restores the exact prior target state; explicit read/unread has the same recovery discipline.

arguments.message:
Approve these bounded UX-02 defaults, consistent with the existing 'return to the original inbox position' contract, not claims of verified Superhuman fidelity:
(1) Back/Escape restores the ORIGINAL ENTRY thread's focus and captured list anchor/approximate scroll, not a mixed state of last-opened thread plus old scroll. Freeze that reader-session origin on initial list->reader entry; J/K changes the current open conversation/cursor only, and must not overwrite the saved origin. If the entry thread/anchor disappears, resolve by stable account-scoped IDs using the established next surviving old neighbor, then previous, then valid first/empty fallback. Incoming rows must not redirect the restore target. IMPORTANT: saved origin is navigation state only—archive/read/reply still target the CURRENT loaded open conversation, never the original entry ref. Existing stale-detail/action guards remain required.
(2) J/K is a NO-OP for Activity-origin readers in UX-02. Do not deduplicate/sort the operation log into a conversation list, substitute Inbox ordering, move hidden list focus, or fetch another thread. Message-level N/P/O and implemented explicit actions remain available normally. Back returns to Activity and preserves the existing underlying Inbox anchor; do not overwrite an anchor with null while the list is unmounted.
Record both policies as proposed implementation contracts in the UX-02 plan/doc. Acceptance tests: enter thread A at nonzero scroll, J to B (and K/J roundtrip), Back restores A+origin anchor; removal of A has a deterministic surviving fallback; an action while B is open affects B not A; duplicate Activity refs do not give J/K any effect or extra getConversation calls; ordinary Activity Back restores its surface. No new IPC, provider writes/scopes, automatic read, sending, or wider UX feature authority is introduced. Continue the existing UX-02 planning scope.

<script setup lang="ts">
/**
 * Plain-text reader. Opening is read-only — never marks read.
 *
 * Archive/read controls are shown only when the authoritative capability permits them, and
 * Gmail-supplied plain-text limitations are disclosed explicitly (`unsupportedReason`,
 * `contextComplete === false`) instead of silently dropping content.
 *
 * Safety: message content is rendered exclusively through text interpolation
 * ({{ }}). No v-html, no markdown/HTML processing, no remote assets anywhere in
 * this slice — hostile markup stays literal text.
 */
import { computed, nextTick, ref, watch } from 'vue';
import type { Conversation, DraftSource, MailError } from '../lib/ipc/client';
import type { DetailState } from '../composables/useMailbox';
const props = defineProps<{
  conversation: Conversation | null;
  state: DetailState;
  error: MailError | null;
  commandInFlight: boolean;
  /** Gmail mode: archive/unarchive controls are hidden, not just disabled. */
  readOnly?: boolean;
  showReadControls?: boolean;
}>();
const emit = defineEmits<{
  close: [];
  archive: [];
  unarchive: [];
  setRead: [read: boolean];
  prepareReply: [source: DraftSource];
}>();
const container = ref<HTMLElement | null>(null);
const latestMessage = computed(() => props.conversation?.messages.at(-1) ?? null);
const replyBlockedReason = computed(() => {
  if (!props.conversation || !latestMessage.value) return 'No displayed latest message is available as a reply source.';
  if (props.conversation.retainedSnapshotAt) return 'Reply preparation is blocked for a retained snapshot; current message headers cannot be verified.';
  if (props.conversation.contextComplete === false) return 'Reply preparation is blocked because this cached conversation is incomplete.';
  if (props.conversation.replyContext && props.conversation.replyContext.sourceMessageId !== latestMessage.value.id) return 'Reply preparation is blocked because cached reply headers do not match the displayed latest message.';
  return null;
});
function prepareReply(): void {
  const conversation = props.conversation;
  const source = latestMessage.value;
  if (!conversation || !source || replyBlockedReason.value) return;
  emit('prepareReply', {
    kind: 'reply',
    conversation: { ...conversation.ref },
    sourceMessageId: source.id,
  });
}
function describeError(error: MailError): string {
  switch (error.kind) {
    case 'not_found':
      return 'That conversation is no longer available.';
    case 'invalid_request':
      return `The request was rejected (invalid field: ${error.field}).`;
    case 'request_id_conflict':
      return 'The request conflicted with an earlier request ID.';
    case 'storage_unavailable':
      return 'Local storage is unavailable. The operation was not confirmed.';
    case 'profile_in_use':
      return 'Another window is using this profile.';
    case 'read_only':
      return 'Gmail is read-only; archiving is unavailable.';
    case 'not_configured':
      return 'Gmail is not configured on this device.';
    case 'auth_required':
      return 'Sign-in is required; cached conversations stay readable.';
    case 'auth_cancelled':
      return 'Sign-in was cancelled.';
    case 'auth_failed':
      return 'Sign-in failed. Cached conversations stay readable.';
    case 'secrets_unavailable':
      return 'Secure credential storage is unavailable.';
    case 'network_unavailable':
      return 'The network is unavailable; cached conversations stay readable.';
    case 'rate_limited':
      return 'The provider is rate limiting. Cached conversations stay readable.';
    case 'provider_unavailable':
      return 'The mail provider is temporarily unavailable.';
    case 'invalid_provider_response':
      return 'The provider returned an unexpected response.';
    case 'busy':
      return 'A sync is already in progress. Try again shortly.';
    case 'permission_required':
      return 'Google mailbox-action permission is not enabled.';
    case 'provider_rejected':
      return 'The provider rejected this action.';
    case 'outcome_unknown':
      return 'The remote result is uncertain. Review Activity before retrying.';
    default:
      return 'Could not load the conversation.';
  }
}
watch(
  () => props.conversation?.ref.conversationId,
  async (id, previousId) => {
    // A background status refresh must not steal focus from the toolbar/activity.
    if (id && id !== previousId && props.state === 'ready') {
      await nextTick();
      container.value?.focus();
    }
  },
);
</script>
