<script setup lang="ts">
/**
 * Plain-text, keyboard-first conversation reader (UX-02). Opening is read-only —
 * never marks read.
 *
 * Visit-scoped message state (active message, expansion, details disclosure,
 * scroll anchor) lives inside this mounted reader instance, keyed by
 * account+conversation reference and message ID — never by array position. It
 * survives J/K round trips and same-reference background replacements within
 * the reader session and is released when the reader closes (component
 * unmount) or the account changes.
 *
 * Archive/read controls are shown only when the authoritative capability permits them, and
 * Gmail-supplied plain-text limitations are disclosed explicitly (`unsupportedReason`,
 * `contextComplete === false`) instead of silently dropping content.
 *
 * Safety: message content is rendered exclusively through text interpolation
 * ({{ }}). No v-html, no markdown/HTML processing, no remote assets anywhere in
 * this slice — hostile markup stays literal text. Reply preparation always
 * targets the explicitly displayed latest message, never the focused message.
 *
 * Message commands (N/P/O/Shift+O, details dismissal) are exposed as narrow
 * methods for App's single keyboard dispatcher — this component never adds its
 * own window listener.
 */
import { computed, nextTick, ref, watch } from 'vue';
import type { Address, Conversation, ConversationRef, DraftSource, MailError, Message } from '../lib/ipc/client';
import type { DetailState } from '../composables/useMailbox';

const props = defineProps<{
  conversation: Conversation | null;
  state: DetailState;
  error: MailError | null;
  commandInFlight: boolean;
  /** The conversation reference the shell currently wants displayed. */
  openRef: ConversationRef | null;
  /** Gmail mode: archive/unarchive controls are hidden, not just disabled. */
  readOnly?: boolean;
  showReadControls?: boolean;
}>();

const emit = defineEmits<{
  close: [];
  archive: [];
  unarchive: [];
  setRead: [read: boolean];
  prepareReply: [source: DraftSource];
  /** Identity of the message that currently owns reader focus. */
  activeMessage: [messageId: string | null];
  /** Hover/focus participant context override; `null` restores the baseline. */
  contactOverride: [
    override:
      | { ref: ConversationRef; messageId: string; displayName: string | null; mailbox: string }
      | null,
  ];
}>();

const container = ref<HTMLElement | null>(null);
const scrollerEl = ref<HTMLElement | null>(null);
const messageEls = new Map<string, HTMLElement>();

const latestMessage = computed(() => props.conversation?.messages.at(-1) ?? null);
const replyBlockedReason = computed(() => {
  if (!props.conversation || !latestMessage.value) return 'No displayed latest message is available as a reply source.';
  if (props.conversation.retainedSnapshotAt) return 'Reply preparation is blocked for a retained snapshot; current message headers cannot be verified.';
  if (props.conversation.contextComplete === false) return 'Reply preparation is blocked because this cached conversation is incomplete.';
  if (props.conversation.replyContext && props.conversation.replyContext.sourceMessageId !== latestMessage.value.id) return 'Reply preparation is blocked because cached reply headers do not match the displayed latest message.';
  return null;
});

function prepareReply(): void {
  // Reply always targets the explicitly displayed latest message; focusing an
  // older message never changes the reply contract.
  const conversation = props.conversation;
  const source = latestMessage.value;
  if (!conversation || !source || replyBlockedReason.value) return;
  emit('prepareReply', {
    kind: 'reply',
    conversation: { ...conversation.ref },
    sourceMessageId: source.id,
  });
}

function describeError(error: MailError): string {
  switch (error.kind) {
    case 'not_found':
      return 'That conversation is no longer available.';
    case 'invalid_request':
      return `The request was rejected (invalid field: ${error.field}).`;
    case 'request_id_conflict':
      return 'The request conflicted with an earlier request ID.';
    case 'storage_unavailable':
      return 'Local storage is unavailable. The operation was not confirmed.';
    case 'profile_in_use':
      return 'Another window is using this profile.';
    case 'read_only':
      return 'Gmail is read-only; archiving is unavailable.';
    case 'not_configured':
      return 'Gmail is not configured on this device.';
    case 'auth_required':
      return 'Sign-in is required; cached conversations stay readable.';
    case 'auth_cancelled':
      return 'Sign-in was cancelled.';
    case 'auth_failed':
      return 'Sign-in failed. Cached conversations stay readable.';
    case 'secrets_unavailable':
      return 'Secure credential storage is unavailable.';
    case 'network_unavailable':
      return 'The network is unavailable; cached conversations stay readable.';
    case 'rate_limited':
      return 'The provider is rate limiting. Cached conversations stay readable.';
    case 'provider_unavailable':
      return 'The mail provider is temporarily unavailable.';
    case 'invalid_provider_response':
      return 'The provider returned an unexpected response.';
    case 'busy':
      return 'A sync is already in progress. Try again shortly.';
    case 'permission_required':
      return 'Google mailbox-action permission is not enabled.';
    case 'provider_rejected':
      return 'The provider rejected this action.';
    case 'outcome_unknown':
      return 'The remote result is uncertain. Review Activity before retrying.';
    default:
      return 'Could not load the conversation.';
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Visit-scoped message state, keyed by account+conversation
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Viewport-relative scroll anchor: a message top plus a scrollTop fallback. */
interface MessageAnchor { messageId: string; offsetTop: number; scrollTop: number }

interface VisitState {
  activeMessageId: string | null;
  expandedIds: Set<string>;
  detailsOpenId: string | null;
  anchor: MessageAnchor | null;
  /** Message ordering this state was built against (for removed-ID resolution). */
  order: string[];
}

const visits = new Map<string, VisitState>();
/** Reactive holder for the currently displayed visit. */
const visitRef = ref<VisitState | null>(null);
let lastDataKey: string | null = null;

function visitKey(ref: ConversationRef): string {
  return `${ref.accountId}:${ref.conversationId}`;
}

function keyOfDisplayed(): string | null {
  const conversation = props.conversation;
  const open = props.openRef;
  if (!conversation || !open) return null;
  if (conversation.ref.accountId !== open.accountId || conversation.ref.conversationId !== open.conversationId) return null;
  return visitKey(conversation.ref);
}

/**
 * Prune removed message IDs and resolve removed active/anchor IDs by the
 * surviving old neighbors (next surviving old neighbor, then previous), so a
 * background replacement can never leave a stale message target.
 */
function pruneVisit(visit: VisitState, nextIds: string[]): void {
  const present = new Set(nextIds);
  const resolve = (id: string | null): string | null => {
    if (id === null || present.has(id)) return id;
    const oldIndex = visit.order.indexOf(id);
    if (oldIndex >= 0) {
      for (let i = oldIndex + 1; i < visit.order.length; i += 1) {
        const candidate = visit.order[i]!;
        if (present.has(candidate)) return candidate;
      }
      for (let i = oldIndex - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
        const candidate = visit.order[i]!;
        if (present.has(candidate)) return candidate;
      }
    }
    return null;
  };
  visit.activeMessageId = resolve(visit.activeMessageId);
  visit.detailsOpenId = visit.detailsOpenId !== null && present.has(visit.detailsOpenId) ? visit.detailsOpenId : null;
  if (visit.anchor && !present.has(visit.anchor.messageId)) {
    const resolved = resolve(visit.anchor.messageId);
    visit.anchor = resolved
      ? { ...visit.anchor, messageId: resolved }
      : { messageId: '', offsetTop: 0, scrollTop: visit.anchor.scrollTop };
  }
  visit.expandedIds = new Set([...visit.expandedIds].filter((id) => present.has(id)));
  visit.order = [...nextIds];
}

function captureScrollAnchor(visit: VisitState): MessageAnchor | null {
  const scroller = scrollerEl.value;
  if (!scroller || visit.order.length === 0) return null;
  const scrollerTop = scroller.getBoundingClientRect().top;
  for (const id of visit.order) {
    const el = messageEls.get(id);
    if (!el) continue;
    const top = el.getBoundingClientRect().top;
    if (top >= scrollerTop - 1 || id === visit.order[visit.order.length - 1]) {
      return { messageId: id, offsetTop: top - scrollerTop, scrollTop: scroller.scrollTop };
    }
  }
  return null;
}

function restoreScroll(visit: VisitState, scroller: HTMLElement): void {
  const anchor = visit.anchor;
  if (!anchor) return;
  const el = messageEls.get(anchor.messageId);
  if (!el || scroller.clientHeight === 0 || !anchor.messageId) {
    // Fallback: the anchored message no longer exists; restore the raw offset.
    scroller.scrollTop = anchor.scrollTop;
    return;
  }
  const relative = el.getBoundingClientRect().top - scroller.getBoundingClientRect().top;
  scroller.scrollTop = scroller.scrollTop + (relative - anchor.offsetTop);
}

function focusElement(el: HTMLElement | null | undefined, reveal: boolean): void {
  if (!el || !el.isConnected) return;
  // Never move focus into an inert ancestor (e.g. a drawer covering the reader).
  if (el.closest('[inert]')) return;
  el.focus({ preventScroll: true });
  if (reveal && typeof el.scrollIntoView === 'function') el.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' });
}

# UX-02 — Conversation reader: implemented contract and evidence

Status: implemented at the component/shell level and validated with the
repository's automated gates plus the opt-in real-Chrome suites. Real-Chrome
runs cover the reader journey, scroll/anchor behavior, and covered-surface
focus safety in the synthetic browser preview only. Native fixture/WKWebView,
VoiceOver/assistive-technology, and platform clipboard verification remain
**explicitly pending**. Browser passes do not establish native IPC/provider
correctness or Superhuman fidelity.

Grounding: `docs/superhuman-browsing-implementation-plan.md` (UX-02; acceptance
complete BROWSE-05 and the copy portion of BROWSE-15) and the UX-02 section of
`superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md` (message focus/expansion, participant
details, copy-only contact controls, reader scrolling).

## Bounded UX-02 contract

What shipped:

- **Visit-scoped message state** inside the mounted reader
  (`src/components/ReaderView.vue`), keyed by account+conversation reference and
  message ID — never array position. Per visit: active message ID, expanded IDs,
  details-disclosure state, and a viewport-relative scroll anchor with a
  `scrollTop` fallback. State survives J/K round trips and same-reference
  background replacements for the life of the mounted reader session and is
  released when the reader unmounts (close) or the account changes. Removed
  message IDs are pruned; a removed active/anchor ID resolves to the next
  surviving old neighbor, then the previous one; empty/loading/error states fall
  back to the reader article and never hold a stale target.
- **Initial focus/expansion:** opening a conversation focuses the newest cached
  message's toggle (not the article) with that message expanded; only as much of
  its header as needed is revealed. Ordinary `ol/li` semantics with a roving
  primary message-toggle button carrying `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`;
  focusing any control of a message updates its message identity.
- **Message movement (nonwrapping):** `N`/`P` move message focus one step
  without auto-expanding (clamped at both ends, no wrap). `O` toggles expansion
  of the focused message; `Shift+O` idempotently expands all messages. These are
  narrow methods exposed to App's single keyboard dispatcher — the reader adds
  no window listener — dispatched after the existing editor/IME/modifier/
  editable/overlay guards. Native Enter/Space button activation is preserved,
  as are the existing `e`/`Shift+U` action contracts.
- **Conversation movement:** Inbox-origin reader `J/K` moves the reader cursor
  through the originating Inbox's current ready snapshot resolved against the
  current `openRef` (previous context ordering for a removed cursor, no wrap),
  without moving hidden list focus and without recapturing the entry origin.
  Activity-origin reader `J/K` is a strict no-op: no navigation, no hidden-focus
  mutation, no invented ordering of duplicate operation references, and no extra
  `getConversation` calls; `N/P/O` still work there.
- **Back/Escape restoration:** the original entry focus, account-scoped
  ordering, and non-null list anchor are captured only at the initial
  list-to-reader entry. Back (Escape/Close) restores the ORIGINAL entry thread
  and best anchor with the fallback chain: surviving entry reference → next
  surviving neighbor from the entry ordering → previous → first valid row →
  empty state. An Activity-origin Back reopens Activity without erasing the
  saved underlying Inbox anchor; explicit Inbox navigation keeps the list's own
  current focus instead.
- **Actions target the current open thread only.** Archive/read/reply use the
  CURRENT loaded open conversation; the saved origin is never an action target.
  Existing stale-request/late-receipt guards and request tokens are retained.
  Inbox archive auto-advance selects a surviving neighbor of the currently
  actioned conversation (`mailbox.focusedSummary` deliberately remains the
  original entry focus); an Activity-origin reader never advances into
  unrelated Inbox mail.
- **Participant details and context.** Each message exposes a native
  `<details>` disclosure with the complete known From/To addresses and sent
  timestamp; unknown Cc/Bcc and other headers are omitted, never fabricated.
  Participant names/addresses are keyboard-focusable context controls separate
  from the expansion toggle (no nested buttons). The active message's sender is
  the baseline reader contact; participant hover and keyboard focus each
  temporarily override it, keyboard focus wins, and exit (leave/blur, disclosure
  dismissal, message change, close) restores the baseline. Overrides are
  identity-qualified by conversation reference + message ID in App, so late
  blur/leave events, loading, removals, and account changes cannot leak a stale
  contact. A visible "Reply targets the latest message from …" label sits near
  Prepare reply so focusing an older message cannot imply a different reply
  target.
- **Copy controls (copy-only BROWSE-15 portion):** separately labelled
  copy-name (only when a display name is known) and copy-email buttons in
  `ContactPane.vue`, reachable by hover and keyboard. Activation uses
  `navigator.clipboard.writeText` only on explicit activation and reports
  success, failure, or unavailable-clipboard honestly via `role="status"`, with
  the text staying selectable for manual copy. Copying never triggers a draft,
  navigation, or any mailbox write, and adds no native permission.
- **Safety unchanged:** bodies render exclusively through text interpolation —
  no `v-html`, no HTML/Markdown processing, no remote assets; hostile markup
  stays literal text (asserted in real Chrome). Retained/incomplete/header
  checks, `unsupportedReason`/`contextComplete` disclosures, draft lifecycle and
  close protection, permission gates, no-auto-read, and overlay inertness are
  preserved.
- **Reader surface:** the reader is a bounded flex surface with its own content
  scroller and a persistent toolbar/Back affordance; the toolbar stays fixed
  while content scrolls beneath it (asserted with real layout geometry in
  Chrome). The 1000px Contact breakpoint and covered-surface inertness are
  preserved, including the wide contact column being inert while a utility
  drawer overlays it.

## Reconstruction choices (marked, not verified Superhuman fidelity)

- Escape precedence inside the reader: an open message-details disclosure is
  dismissed before the reader closes; utility drawers and the narrow Contact
  disclosure keep their existing earlier precedence.
- The participant context displays the participant's display name when present
  and the bare mailbox otherwise — the same known-fields rule as the rest of
  the contact pane.
- Newest message = last entry of the cached message stack (backend order is
  authoritative); no independent relevance ordering is invented.

## Executed validation

- `pnpm vitest run tests/reader.component.test.ts` — visit-scoped state,
  N/P/O/Shift+O semantics, ID-based pruning/removal resolution, same-reference
  replacements, account isolation with equal message IDs, empty/error fallback:
  **10 passed**.
- `pnpm vitest run tests/app.component.test.ts` — 62 tests including the new
  reader-message keyboard contracts (initial newest-message focus, N/P vs J/K,
  original-entry Back at nonzero scroll, removed-entry fallback, J/K round-trip
  state, action-on-current-not-origin, stale/late-receipt safety, Activity
  no-op/call counts, keyboard precedence, participant restoration, copy
  success/unavailability with no writes) and the retained draft/permission/
  inertness/no-auto-read regressions: **62 passed**.
- `pnpm test` (default, Chrome gates skipped) — **235 passed, 7 skipped (14
  files)**.
- Real-Chrome opt-in suites, executed with
  `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME` and `EMAIL_OS_DISCLOSURE_FOCUS_CHROME`
  pointing at `/home/exedev/.cache/rod/browser/chromium-1321438/chrome`:
  - `tests/reader.rendered.test.ts` — **4 passed**: real keyboard/pointer
    open → N/P → O/Shift+O (incl. idempotence) → details Escape precedence →
    participant hover/focus context with baseline restore → explicit copy with
    no draft/navigation/mailbox writes; literal hostile text with zero
    created `script`/`img`/`a`/remote-stylesheet nodes; viewport-stable message
    anchor across a background replacement; original entry restored after
    source reorder and removed-entry neighbor fallback; self-scrolled reader
    with fixed toolbar geometry; contact disclosure below and column at/above
    1000px; reply exit targeting the displayed latest source (`read-03-m1`)
    with zero archive/read commands.
  - `tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts` — **2 passed** (existing layout
    gate, unaffected).
  - `tests/disclosure-focus.rendered.test.ts` — **1 passed** (covered-surface
    focus safety under Activity and narrow-Contact disclosures).
  - `pnpm test` with both Chrome gates set — **242 passed, 0 skipped (14
    files)**.
- `mise run typecheck` — **passing** (vue-tsc, includes the new
  fixture/component/rendered test types).
- `mise run build:web` — **passing** (production Vite build).
- `mise run check` — **passing** (core tests, generated-contract drift, core
  lint, frontend tests, typecheck; no generated/wire/backend changes in this
  slice).

## Pending verification (not claimed as done)

- `mise run dev:native` on a prepared native host: the same keyboard/scroll/
  Back/disclosure/copy/reply journey, IME and native reserved-key behavior, and
  accessibility focus in the actual WKWebView shell. Not run here; recorded as
  **pending**, not passed.
- Native platform clipboard behavior (macOS pasteboard permissions and the
  unavailable-clipboard manual-copy path) is unverified; only the Chromium
  clipboard path of the synthetic preview was exercised.
- VoiceOver/assistive-technology walkthrough of the roving toggle, details
  disclosure, and copy status announcements: pending.
- No real accounts, credentials, mail, or provider behavior were exercised;
  synthetic Chrome success is not evidence of Gmail behavior. Screenshot pixel
  parity was not asserted anywhere.

content.text:
## Findings

### [P1] Preserve reader actions at the new default message focus
**Location:** `src/components/ReaderView.vue:270–276`

Opening now focuses a message-toggle **button**, whereas HEAD focused the reader article. Consequently, App’s existing `buttonOwns()` guards reject `e` and, in Gmail mode, Shift+U at the new default focus and after N/P movement. Parent-run `reader-action-probe.json` confirms native E performs no archive on `message-toggle-conv-01-m3`, while focusing the article and sending E archives conv-01. This breaks the declared reader action journey; window-dispatched component tests bypass the actual focused target. Distinguish message toggles from action buttons when guarding these shortcuts, while preserving native Enter/Space activation and toolbar exclusions.

### [P1] Capture outgoing scroll before clearing the conversation
**Location:** `src/components/ReaderView.vue:280–289`

The watcher returns on `conversation === null` before capturing the outgoing anchor. Actual J/K navigation calls `loadDetail()`, which clears the conversation and renders loading before the next detail arrives; by then the old message elements and scroll geometry are gone. The requested synthetic probe confirms scrollTop **376 → 0** after J/K back to read-01, despite expansion surviving; m3 moves from viewport top **−46.94 → 329.06**. Capture the outgoing anchor before the null-return/DOM teardown, and restore revisit focus without allowing header-reveal scrolling to overwrite the saved viewport. The component roundtrip test directly swaps non-null props and does not cover this loading transition.

### [P2] Publish the resolved active message after pruning
**Location:** `src/components/ReaderView.vue:304–307`

`visits.get(key)` returns the raw stored object, so `pruneVisit()` mutates `activeMessageId` outside Vue’s reactive proxy; assigning that same object back to `visitRef` does not trigger the active-message watcher. The synthetic probe removes active read-01-m1: DOM focus and `.message-active` correctly move to m2, but App retains `readerActiveMessageId = read-01-m1` and displays/copies Ada’s address instead of m2’s `anon@example.test`. Store/prune reactive visit objects, or explicitly publish the resolved active identity after pruning. Add an assertion for the emitted identity/contact, not only visual focus.

Evidence files are under `/tmp/email-os-ux02-timeout-49fem8dc/`: `reader-action-probe.json`/`.mjs` and `reader-scroll-state-probes.json`/`.mjs` (`oldestActive400`).

**Validation:** Parent-provided evidence records six passing configured checks, 235 default UI passes with seven browser skips, and seven separately passing Chrome tests. No reviewer commands were run. These are implementation defects despite those passes, not incorrect intentional focus expectations. Native/WKWebView, VoiceOver, and native clipboard validation remain unavailable—not additional proven defects.

**Overall verdict:** needs attention.  
**Merge verdict: BLOCK** — address the P1 findings before release; P2 is report-only.

## Human Reviewer Callouts (Non-Blocking)

- (none)

## Findings

1. **[P1] Keep reader action shortcuts usable from the new message-toggle focus** — `src/components/ReaderView.vue:276`  
   Initial opening and N/P now focus a message-toggle **button**, so the unchanged `buttonOwns()` guards in App reject `e` and Gmail `Shift+U` throughout the normal reading path. HEAD initially focused the article, where these actions worked. The supplied `reader-action-probe.json` confirms real Chrome input produces no archive on the initial toggle, but archives `conv-01` after explicitly focusing the article. Preserve the approved toggle focus and toolbar/editor exclusions, but allow these conversation shortcuts from message toggles. Add target-bubbling key tests; current `window.dispatchEvent()` action tests bypass this failure.

2. **[P1] Capture the outgoing viewport before the loading transition removes messages** — `src/components/ReaderView.vue:280–289`  
   The watcher returns on `conversation === null` before saving the outgoing anchor. Actual J/K navigation calls unchanged `useMailbox.loadDetail()`, which clears the conversation first; by the next non-null update, the outgoing message elements are gone. The requested parent-run Chrome probe (`reader-scroll-state-probes.json`, `latestBody400`) records read-01 scrolling **353 → 0** after J/K, with focus and expansion otherwise preserved; `expandAll200` independently records **200 → 0**. Capture the anchor during the pre-flush transition to null without discarding visit state, and test the actual loading roundtrip rather than direct non-null component prop swaps.

3. **[P2] Preserve native arrow scrolling inside the reader** — `src/App.vue:679–686`  
   These added aliases turn ArrowDown/ArrowUp into conversation navigation and always cancel their native behavior. HEAD left reader arrows unhandled; the approved reader bindings specify J/K. Consequently, a user reading the long expanded body now changes threads instead of scrolling, while an Activity-origin reader cancels the arrows without doing anything. Keep arrow aliases in the list branch only and retain J/K for reader conversation movement.

4. **[P2] Resolve archive advancement from the pre-action ordering, not the frozen Back ordering** — `src/App.vue:533–535`  
   Source trace: enter A with Inbox `[A,B,C,D]`, refresh its order to `[A,C,B,D]`, then click Archive on A. After `setArchived()` refreshes the list and removes A, `resolveReaderNeighbor()` falls back to the entry ordering and opens B, skipping the actual next survivor C. HEAD’s advancement used the focus resolved by `useMailbox` against the latest pre-removal snapshot and opened C. Capture the current ordering before submitting the archive and resolve advancement against it; keep the frozen entry ordering unchanged for Back and its approved removal fallback.

5. **[P2] Publish the resolved active message after pruning raw visit state** — `src/components/ReaderView.vue:303–307`  
   Existing visits are stored as raw objects in the ordinary Map. Pruning mutates that raw object, then assigns the same object back to `visitRef`, so the active-ID watcher does not emit the change. The parent probe’s `oldestActive400.afterActiveRemoval` demonstrates the consequence: after removing active m1, DOM focus/current styling correctly move to m2, but App still holds m1 and shows **Ada/ada@example.test**, not m2’s **anon@example.test**. Contact copy therefore targets the wrong baseline correspondent. Store reactive visit objects or prune through their reactive proxy so App receives the resolved active ID.

6. **[P2] Scope clipboard outcomes to the displayed contact** — `src/components/ContactPane.vue:44–49`  
   `copyOutcome` persists across contact changes in the mounted wide pane, and pending writes publish outcomes without checking which contact or activation still owns the status. Copy Ada’s address, then move focus to the nameless message: “Email address copied” remains beneath the newly displayed anonymous address although that address was not copied. A delayed completion can introduce the same misleading status after navigation. Clear outcomes when displayed identity changes and guard asynchronous completion with an identity/activation token.

## Validation and verdict

These are implementation defects, not objections to the approved initial focus, Back-origin policy, Activity no-op policy, or latest-source reply contract. The action tests’ window-targeted events and the component test’s non-null roundtrip explain coverage gaps; their passing results do not refute the reproductions.

Parent-run evidence reports all six configured checks passing, **235 UI tests passing / 7 skipped**, and all **7 opt-in Chrome tests passing separately**. I ran no shell, Git, or test commands and made no edits. Native/WKWebView, VoiceOver, and platform clipboard validation remain unavailable—not failed or established by Chrome.

**Overall verdict: needs attention.** P1 findings require correction before release; P2 findings are report-only.

**Merge verdict: BLOCK**

## Human Reviewer Callouts (Non-Blocking)

## Findings

### [P1] Preserve outgoing scroll state before clearing the message DOM
**`src/components/ReaderView.vue:280–289`**

The watcher returns on `conversation === null` before capturing the outgoing anchor, but real J/K navigation clears the detail while loading. When the next detail arrives, the old message elements are already gone. The requested synthetic Chrome probe (`reader-scroll-state-probes.json`, `expandAll200`) confirms read-01 → J → K resets `scrollTop` from **200 to 0**, shifting the same message by **200px**, while expansion and active identity survive. Capture the outgoing anchor before the null return without erasing visit state. The component round-trip test directly swaps ready conversations, and the rendered suite never presses J/K, so neither covers this transition.

### [P1] Keep conversation actions usable from the new default message focus
**`src/components/ReaderView.vue:269–276`**

HEAD focused the reader article; this change focuses a message-toggle **button**, including after N/P. App’s unchanged `buttonOwns()` exclusion therefore suppresses `e` and Shift+U during normal message-focused reading. `reader-action-probe.json` confirms native E produces no operation at initial toggle focus, while focusing the article and pressing E archives conv-01. The new archive test at `tests/app.component.test.ts:1427–1437` passes because `window.dispatchEvent()` targets Window instead of the focused button. Allow the reader’s message toggles through the conversation-action guard while retaining native Enter/Space behavior and unrelated button exclusions; test bubbling keys from actual message focus.

### [P2] Notify App when pruning changes the active message
**`src/components/ReaderView.vue:304–307`**

`visits.get()` returns the raw stored object, so `pruneVisit()` changes `activeMessageId` outside its reactive proxy; assigning the same object back does not trigger the active-message watcher. The supplied probe’s `oldestActive400.afterActiveRemoval` confirms that removing focused m1 moves actual focus/current treatment to nameless-sender **m2**, but App retains **m1** and displays **Ada Fixture / ada@example.test** instead of m2’s sender. Consequently the contact copy controls offer the wrong correspondent. Mutate through reactive visit state or explicitly emit the resolved active ID after pruning; assert contact identity as well as DOM focus in the removal regression.

### [P2] Derive synthetic reply threading from the requested source
**`tests/reader.fixture.ts:318–323`**

Every synthetic reply receives read-01-m3’s RFC Message-ID and references, regardless of its source. The rendered reply test explicitly creates a reply to **read-03-m1**, so its returned draft combines read-03’s source with read-01’s threading metadata and still passes because it only checks the outgoing command. This is a fixture/expectation defect, not evidence of a production reply regression. Build the link from the requested conversation’s valid source metadata, reject mismatched/unavailable sources, and assert the returned draft link in the browser reply checkpoint.

### [P2] Remove cross-test state dependence from the rendered suite
**`tests/reader.rendered.test.ts:346–350`**

This test requires the preceding test to leave read-01 open and expanded, while fixture mounting occurs only in `beforeAll`. Selecting just this test starts in the Inbox and fails its initial reader-subject assertion; changing execution order likewise invalidates the journey setup. Mount/reset the fixture and establish the required reader state for each test, or combine the deliberately sequential journey into one test. This preserves useful focused reruns and prevents unrelated earlier failures from cascading into misleading browser failures.

### [P2] Assert script-node absence instead of checking anchors twice
**`tests/reader.rendered.test.ts:289–293`**

The hostile-content check collects `scripts` but never asserts it, checking `anchors` twice instead. Thus the claimed real-Chrome verification of zero created script nodes in `docs/ux-02-conversation-reader.md` is not performed. Collect script nodes within the reader—not the whole Vite page, which legitimately contains scripts—and assert zero alongside the existing literal-text/image/link checks. This is an assertion/evidence defect; current production rendering remains interpolation-only.

---
name: pi-subagents
description: |
  Delegate work to Pi subagents after the operator asks for it: one child,
  parallel or scripted workflows, async runs, resume/steer/stop, review fanout,
  and multi-lane or worktree orchestration.
---

# Pi Subagents

The parent works directly by default. Invoke subagents only when the operator
requested delegation in the current request or through applicable user/project
instructions. Task size, complexity, risk, tool-call count, recipe fit, or an
available specialist does not independently authorize delegation.

Once authorized, choose the smallest bounded shape that earns its token and
elapsed-time overhead through evidence, independent review, specialization,
useful parallelism, or isolation. A single child is valid. The parent keeps
intent, routing, decisions, final acceptance, and publication authority, and
does the work itself where that is cheaper.

## Calls

```typescript
subagent({ agent: "worker", task: "<brief>" })                    // one child; async by default
subagent({ workflow: "parallel", args: { tasks: [{ agent, task, cwd?, model? }] } })  // independent children
subagent({ workflow: true })              // runs the one ```js workflow block in this same reply
subagent({ workflow: "./lane.js", args }) // script file, path relative to the request cwd
subagent({ action: "validate", workflow: "./lane.js" })          // check a script without launching
subagent({ action: "status", id })        // options: { view: "fleet" } or { view: "transcript", index: 0 }
subagent({ action: "resume", id, message })   // completed or paused child; returns a new run id
subagent({ action: "steer", id, message })    // live async child
subagent({ action: "stop", id })              // ends the run; not resumable
subagent({ action: "interrupt", id })         // pauses the child's current turn
subagent({ action: "list" })  ·  subagent({ action: "models" })
subagent({ action: "guide", options: { topic: "<section address>" } })
```

Launches are async by default. Set `async: false` only when the parent must
block; final reviews and gates stay async. After launching, keep doing safe
independent work, or yield: native completion wakes this session. Do not sleep,
poll, or call `bg_wait` for ordinary children. Use `bg_wait` only for provider
or detached work that has no native notification and whose result this turn
needs.

## Workflow scripts

Use a script when later steps depend on earlier results, or for keyed,
retried, aggregated, or resumed children. Write one ```` ```js workflow ````
block in the reply and call `subagent({ workflow: true })` in the same reply.
For a long script, write it to a file and pass `workflow: "./path.js"`; calls in
one reply run at the same time, so write the file in one reply and `validate` or
launch it in the next. When a `workflow: true` call reports the block missing,
pass the source as `options: { script: "..." }` in place of `workflow: true` for
the rest of the turn: on some hosts, text after a tool call reaches the session
as a summary without the block.

```js workflow
const scan = await runs.run("scan", { label: "Map auth flow", agent: "scout", task: "..." });
const reviews = await runs.all([
  { key: "correctness", label: "Review auth correctness", agent: "reviewer", task: "... " + scan.output },
  { key: "tests", label: "Review auth tests", agent: "reviewer", task: "..." },
]);
return reviews.map((review) => review.output);
```

- Scripts are statement bodies with an explicit `return`, top-level `await`,
  and plain helpers. Nested async functions, arrows, and methods are rejected.
- Every `runs.run` / `runs.all` item needs a stable `key`. Add a short
  verb + behavior `label` unless the user gave one.
- Bind files with `output: "plans/x.md"` (relative paths land in run
  artifacts) and return `outputReference` or `artifactPaths`. A filename in
  task text does not route output. Never send reports to the repo root.
- `runs.lanes([{ key, stages: [...] }])` runs a predeclared plan: first stages
  together, later stages in order per lane.

Resuming a retained child:

```js workflow
let child = await runs.run("fix-1", { agent: "worker", task: "..." });
child = await runs.run("fix-2", { resume: child.runId, task: "Apply these accepted findings: ..." });
return child.output;
```

- Always resume the latest returned run id; every resume returns a new one.
- Use a new stable key for every resume pass.
- `resume` excludes `agent` and `gate`; the child keeps its agent, model, and tools.
- Resume a completed child; steer a live one. Top-level `{ action: "resume" }` is detached.

## Briefs

Every child starts cold. Its task states: goal; repo, explicit `cwd`, and
ref; authority and edit boundary; relevant files, decisions, and evidence;
success criteria; validation; expected output; and when to stop or ask.
Make parallel briefs differ by seam, evidence, and decision, not just an item
number.

## Rules

- One writer per cwd or worktree. Parallelize reading, review, and
  validation. `worktree: true` needs a clean checkout (untracked files count;
  `.pi/subagents/` does not). For Pi extension repos, put lane worktrees
  outside `~/.pi/agent/extensions`, for example `~/.pi/agent/worktrees`.
- Reviewers use fresh context. Use `context: "fork"` only when the child needs
  the parent's history; it requires a persisted parent session.
- Children do not spawn subagents unless the parent delegated fanout and their
  resolved `tools` include `subagent`.
- A failed workflow, launch, prompt runtime, extension load, or child tool
  setup blocks the lane. Stop, report the exact failure and run/worktree state,
  verify a clean worktree or capture the partial diff, then retry the same way
  once. Switching to `interactive_shell`, `pi -ne`, or another CLI needs owner
  approval.
- As a conservative orchestration policy, do not pass a hard `toolBudget` or tight `usageBudget` to mutation-capable workers. The default tool budget blocks read/search tools rather than mutation tools. If interrupted after a tool call starts, checkpoint after the current tool returns with changed files, build/test state, and commit or PR state.
- Route workers and scouts to a fast capable tier, serious reviews to a strong
  tier, and top reasoning only to bounded read-only critique. Exact model names
  belong in user or project settings, not here.
- `subagent`, `subagents_enable`, `subagent_supervisor`, `contact_supervisor`, and `structured_output` are model-only: call them as ordinary model tool calls. Codemode scripts cannot reach them through `tools.*`, `ALL_TOOLS`, or `searchTools`.
- Receipts, CI, and review bots are evidence, not authority. Backlog, release,
  and merge policy belong to the user's or project's own skill.

## Look up the rest

If only `subagents_enable` is visible, call it first; `subagent` and `guide`
work from the next request. Read one section, not a whole topic:

| --- | --- |
| Script API: `runs.*`, `state`, limits | `workflows/scripted-workflows` |

# UX-02 — Conversation reader: implemented contract and evidence

Status: implemented at the component/shell level and validated with the
repository's automated gates plus the opt-in real-Chrome suites. Real-Chrome
runs cover the reader journey, scroll/anchor behavior, and covered-surface
focus safety in the synthetic browser preview only. Native fixture/WKWebView,
VoiceOver/assistive-technology, and platform clipboard verification remain
**explicitly pending**. Browser passes do not establish native IPC/provider
correctness or Superhuman fidelity.

Grounding: `docs/superhuman-browsing-implementation-plan.md` (UX-02; acceptance
complete BROWSE-05 and the copy portion of BROWSE-15) and the UX-02 section of
`superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md` (message focus/expansion, participant
details, copy-only contact controls, reader scrolling).

## Bounded UX-02 contract

What shipped:

- **Visit-scoped message state** inside the mounted reader
  (`src/components/ReaderView.vue`), keyed by account+conversation reference and
  message ID — never array position. Per visit: active message ID, expanded IDs,
  details-disclosure state, and a viewport-relative scroll anchor with a
  `scrollTop` fallback. State survives J/K round trips and same-reference
  background replacements for the life of the mounted reader session and is
  released when the reader unmounts (close) or the account changes. Removed
  message IDs are pruned; a removed active/anchor ID resolves to the next
  surviving old neighbor, then the previous one; empty/loading/error states fall
  back to the reader article and never hold a stale target.
- **Initial focus/expansion:** opening a conversation focuses the newest cached
  message's toggle (not the article) with that message expanded; only as much of
  its header as needed is revealed. Ordinary `ol/li` semantics with a roving
  primary message-toggle button carrying `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`;
  focusing any control of a message updates its message identity.
- **Message movement (nonwrapping):** `N`/`P` move message focus one step
  without auto-expanding (clamped at both ends, no wrap). `O` toggles expansion
  of the focused message; `Shift+O` idempotently expands all messages. These are
  narrow methods exposed to App's single keyboard dispatcher — the reader adds
  no window listener — dispatched after the existing editor/IME/modifier/
  editable/overlay guards. Native Enter/Space button activation is preserved
  (one activation toggles expansion once, never a mailbox action), and the
  existing `e`/`Shift+U` action contracts work from the new message-toggle
  focus: a message toggle is the reader's navigation context, not a toolbar
  action button, so the conversation-level shortcuts remain usable there while
  every other focused button/link keeps the generic exclusion. Toolbar,
  editor/IME, overlay, capability, read-only, and stale-target guards are
  unchanged.
- **Reading progress across foreground loading:** the outgoing visit's
  viewport-relative scroll anchor is captured before any DOM teardown —
  including the foreground null/loading transition where the conversation is
  cleared before the next detail arrives — and retained through loading/error
  without being overwritten by the empty/loading DOM. Returning to a visit
  restores the exact scroll offset and viewport-relative message geometry, and
  revisit focus does not reveal-scroll over the restored offset (initial entry
  and explicit N/P still reveal the focused header as needed).
- **Conversation movement:** Inbox-origin reader `J/K` moves the reader cursor
  through the originating Inbox's current ready snapshot resolved against the
  current `openRef` (previous context ordering for a removed cursor, no wrap),
  without moving hidden list focus and without recapturing the entry origin.
  Activity-origin reader `J/K` is a strict no-op: no navigation, no hidden-focus
  mutation, no invented ordering of duplicate operation references, and no extra
  `getConversation` calls; `N/P/O` still work there.
- **Back/Escape restoration:** the original entry focus, account-scoped
  ordering, and non-null list anchor are captured only at the initial
  list-to-reader entry. Back (Escape/Close) restores the ORIGINAL entry thread
  and best anchor with the fallback chain: surviving entry reference → next
  surviving neighbor from the entry ordering → previous → first valid row →
  empty state. An Activity-origin Back reopens Activity without erasing the
  saved underlying Inbox anchor; explicit Inbox navigation keeps the list's own
  current focus instead.
- **Actions target the current open thread only.** Archive/read/reply use the
  CURRENT loaded open conversation; the saved origin is never an action target.
  Existing stale-request/late-receipt guards and request tokens are retained.
  Inbox archive auto-advance selects a surviving neighbor of the currently
  actioned conversation (`mailbox.focusedSummary` deliberately remains the
  original entry focus); an Activity-origin reader never advances into
  unrelated Inbox mail.
- **Participant details and context.** Each message exposes a native
  `<details>` disclosure with the complete known From/To addresses and sent
  timestamp; unknown Cc/Bcc and other headers are omitted, never fabricated.
  Participant names/addresses are keyboard-focusable context controls separate
  from the expansion toggle (no nested buttons). The active message's sender is
  the baseline reader contact; participant hover and keyboard focus each
  temporarily override it, keyboard focus wins, and exit (leave/blur, disclosure
  dismissal, message change, close) restores the baseline. Overrides are
  identity-qualified by conversation reference + message ID in App, so late
  blur/leave events, loading, removals, and account changes cannot leak a stale
  contact. A visible "Reply targets the latest message from …" label sits near
  Prepare reply so focusing an older message cannot imply a different reply
  target.
- **Copy controls (copy-only BROWSE-15 portion):** separately labelled
  copy-name (only when a display name is known) and copy-email buttons in
  `ContactPane.vue`, reachable by hover and keyboard. Activation uses
  `navigator.clipboard.writeText` only on explicit activation and reports
  success, failure, or unavailable-clipboard honestly via `role="status"`, with
  the text staying selectable for manual copy. Copying never triggers a draft,
  navigation, or any mailbox write, and adds no native permission.
- **Safety unchanged:** bodies render exclusively through text interpolation —
  no `v-html`, no HTML/Markdown processing, no remote assets; hostile markup
  stays literal text (asserted in real Chrome). Retained/incomplete/header
  checks, `unsupportedReason`/`contextComplete` disclosures, draft lifecycle and
  close protection, permission gates, no-auto-read, and overlay inertness are
  preserved.
- **Reader surface:** the reader is a bounded flex surface with its own content
  scroller and a persistent toolbar/Back affordance; the toolbar stays fixed
  while content scrolls beneath it (asserted with real layout geometry in
  Chrome). The 1000px Contact breakpoint and covered-surface inertness are
  preserved, including the wide contact column being inert while a utility
  drawer overlays it.

## Reconstruction choices (marked, not verified Superhuman fidelity)

- Escape precedence inside the reader: an open message-details disclosure is
  dismissed before the reader closes; utility drawers and the narrow Contact
  disclosure keep their existing earlier precedence.

# Orchestration

Use this when several tasks need coordinated children, worktrees, or
repositories, or when a change goes through write, review, and fix rounds.
Create lanes only after delegation is operator-authorized and each lane
materially improves evidence, independent review, specialization, useful
parallelism, or isolated execution. Keep dependent work serial.

## Recipes

Recipes select a shape; they do not authorize delegation. Pick the smallest:

- **Recon then implement:** one focused `scout`, then one `worker` that gets its findings.
- **Implementation:** settle scope and acceptance first, then use a scout, writer, or fresh reviewer only where that stage earns its overhead. Split large work into serial milestones, not a writer swarm.
- **Parallel analysis:** fan out only independent read, review, or validation work, or give each writer its own worktree.

## Seams before writers

Before launching a writer for substantial mutation work, classify it as
**single-seam** or **multi-seam**. Two or more independently testable
contracts or source boundaries make it multi-seam. One PR does not imply one
writer.

- **Multi-seam:** give each component writer exclusive file or contract
  ownership, a focused gate, and a committed or otherwise durable handoff.
  Start one integration-only owner after those handoffs are ready. Repartition
  any writer brief that owns all major outcomes across independent boundaries.
- **Single-seam:** one writer is right when the work is one coupled seam, or
  when splitting would create overlapping ownership or artificial handoffs.
  Record that evidence. Do not split coupled work to raise the lane count.

## Lane board

Before more than one mutation-capable lane starts, record in the parent:

`Lane | repo/cwd | decision | owned files or contract | isolation path | authority | next gate | handoff | why independent`

One source seam or decision is one lane. Record each lane's delivery target,
allowed actions, validation, and review rigor. For cross-repository work,
name the shared contract and which repository changes first. A blocked
decision is a lane state: owner, options, recommended default, and the
evidence needed to continue.

Mutation lanes need distinct isolation paths and explicit `cwd` values.
`worktree: true` branches from `HEAD` (or `baseRef`) and refuses a dirty
checkout; in a shared or dirty checkout, commit first or give each lane a
worktree you created. Use one async workflow for a coordinated wave:
`runs.all` for independent lanes, `runs.run` for dependent stages, repo slug
or lane key in every child key and output path.

While one lane waits, run safe independent preparation, validation, or
read-only review. When only async lanes remain, record what reopens work and
yield; completion wakes the parent.

## Review loop

1. Inspect the source, diff, issue, or plan directly.
2. One writer implements inside its boundary and runs focused validation that can fail for the changed behavior.
3. When the delegation contract calls for independent review, fresh-context read-only reviewers inspect the actual worktree. Otherwise parent inspection is enough; skip review for trivial wording, renames, or local probes.
4. The parent classifies findings (below) and sends accepted fixes to one writer: resume the original worker with its latest run id, or launch one forked `worker` as `/review-loop` does.
5. Re-run affected validation and review only the changed blast radius.
6. Stop when no blocker or fix worth doing now remains, an unapproved product, scope, or architecture decision appears, or the round cap is reached (default 3). Do not loop for polish. Children never decide the loop outcome.

An async writer's handoff is an intermediate state, not completion, unless the
user asked for writer-only work.

| Situation | Review shape |
| --- | --- |
| One coherent diff or risk | one reviewer |
| Independent risks (correctness, tests, security, UI) | parallel reviewers with distinct contracts |
| Possible over-scope | same-writer challenge before fresh review |
| Material design tradeoff | council mode |

### Staged fixes

When reviews have produced findings across several clusters:

1. Run a read-only planning fanout, one reviewer per cluster or angle, each returning exact files, lines, fixes, and validation.
2. Classify the accepted fixes as single-seam or multi-seam (above) on the lane board before any writer starts.
3. Give a writer only its assigned stage. Pass each earlier result into the later task by variable or by its declared `output` path, not as a whole aggregate blob. With `runs.lanes`, keep stages narrow: red test, helper change, one render seam, validation, review.
4. Validate the integrated result with fresh read-only reviewers on distinct angles.

When a child returns a target list, validate it in JavaScript and map bounded
entries into `runs.all`.

## Finding disposition

Classify each finding against the current head:

- **Valid blocker:** concrete failure, repro, security issue, contract mismatch, or source-proven regression. Fix now.
- **Valid non-blocker:** real but outside the slice. Record or defer.
- **Stale:** already fixed or absent. Cite current evidence.
- **Invalid:** contradicted by source, tests, docs, or approved scope. Cite it.
- **Out of scope or policy:** needs an unapproved product, architecture, authority, or release decision. Escalate.
- **Speculative:** no contract, repro, or reachable failure. Do not block.

Classify bot comments the same way before assigning severity.

## Gate failures

1. Confirm the run belongs to the exact head under judgment.
2. Read the focused failing log; name the failing test, assertion, or contract.
3. Classify: current diff, stale test, environment, or existing flake.
4. Reproduce with the narrowest command when practical.
5. Patch forward when the diff caused it. For a stale or flaky failure, collect proof before one rerun.
6. Re-run the affected command or exact-head gate after every fix.

## Handoff and cleanup

A handoff states lane status, repository and worktree, changed files,
validation, open decisions, next action, and artifact or receipt paths. Copy
only final evidence to memory, a mission, a PR, or an approved docs path, then
remove scratch reports from the worktree.

Keep a worktree until its handoff is durable, no run owns it, and no later
gate needs it. If a run stops or needs attention, preserve its worktree and
artifacts, then resume that run or start one replacement lane from the
handoff. Never start a second writer while worktree ownership is unclear.

Before reporting done, check the board: every lane terminal or blocked with a
named next action; one writer per worktree; required validation and fresh
review done; accepted findings fixed and revalidated; publication authority
present before any push, comment, merge, or release; residual risks and
skipped checks stated.

Executable agents:
Package agents
- evidence-auditor (sof-pi@0.0.0, context: fresh): Independent public-source audit with sof-pi snapshots; never treats synthesis as proof
- planner (sof-pi@0.0.0): Read-only implementation planner that turns a validated task and scout findings into a concrete, bounded implementation plan with explicit non-goals and human-approval decisions
- researcher (sof-pi@0.0.0): Evidence-first public web researcher using sof-pi snapshots and explicit evidence gaps
- reviewer (sof-pi@0.0.0): Versatile review specialist for code diffs, plans, proposed solutions, codebase health, and PR/issue validation. Enforces the sof-pi Review Rubric (priority tags, fail-fast error handling, required Human Reviewer Callouts).

Builtin agents
- claude-code (builtin, external-cli:claude): Read-only Claude Code CLI analysis; requires local authentication and trusted user settings/hooks
- claude-code-writer (builtin, external-cli:claude): Explicit file-writing Claude Code CLI mode; requires local authentication and trusted user settings/hooks
- codex-exec (builtin, external-cli:codex): Read-only one-shot analysis through the installed Codex CLI
- codex-exec-writer (builtin, external-cli:codex): Explicit workspace-writing one-shot execution through the installed Codex CLI
- cursor-agent (builtin, external-cli:cursor-agent): Read-only one-shot analysis through the installed Cursor CLI
- cursor-agent-writer (builtin, external-cli:cursor-agent): Explicit workspace-writing one-shot execution through the installed Cursor CLI
- delegate (builtin): Lightweight subagent that inherits the parent model with no default reads
- oracle (builtin, context: fork, aliases: advisor): High-context decision-consistency oracle that protects inherited state and prevents drift
- scout (builtin): Fast codebase recon that returns compressed context for handoff
- worker (builtin, context: fresh, aliases: developer, coder, implementer, develop): Implementation agent for normal tasks and approved oracle handoffs

content.text:
## Findings

1. **[P2] Publish active-message changes after pruning** — `src/components/ReaderView.vue:314–316`  
   `visits` stores raw objects, so pruning mutates the raw visit and reassigns the same object to `visitRef`; the `activeMessage` watcher is not notified. Focus `read-01-m1`, then remove it: the reader resolves focus to nameless `m2`, but App retains `m1` and falls back to latest sender Ada for contact context and copying. Existing removal tests check DOM focus, not this differing-sender baseline. **Smallest correction:** prune through a reactive visit or explicitly publish the resolved active ID.

2. **[P2] Preserve reader focus during foreground loading** — `src/components/ReaderView.vue:325–329`  
   The documented loading/error focus fallback only handles `error`. J/K removes the focused message toggle during loading and leaves focus on `<body>`, losing the reader’s keyboard position. This is confirmed by the fingerprint-matched parent scroll probe: both `duringLoading` records show `activeTag: "BODY"` and no active test target. Current loading tests assert the loading notice and restored geometry, not interim focus. **Smallest correction:** move focus to the persistent reader article when loading removes reader-owned message focus, preserving toolbar/overlay ownership.

3. **[P2] Derive synthetic reply metadata from the requested source** — `tests/reader.fixture.ts:318–323`  
   Every reply receives `read-01-m3` threading metadata, including the rendered reply journey targeting `read-03-m1`. Consequently, that passing test opens a draft whose source and immutable reply link identify different messages. Reply content also remains blank rather than using the source’s recipient/subject defaults. This contradicts Slice04’s source-derived reply contract. **Smallest correction:** derive reply metadata and defaults from the requested stored conversation, and assert the returned draft matches that source.

4. **[P2] Remove dependencies between rendered test cases** — `tests/reader.rendered.test.ts:368–370`  
   This case requires the preceding test to leave `read-01` open with its expansion state; subsequent cases likewise consume prior navigation and Inbox mutations. Running this case alone by test-name filter starts on the Inbox and immediately fails its subject assertion. Failures also cascade into unrelated cases. **Smallest correction:** establish a fresh fixture and explicit scenario setup per case, or combine the intentionally ordered journey into one test.

5. **[P2] Make the stale-response assertion distinguish stale data** — `tests/app.component.test.ts:1525–1533`  
   Before the delayed `read-02` response arrives, the test navigates back to `read-02` and obtains an identical snapshot. Accepting the stale response would therefore leave every final assertion unchanged; this does not establish the stale-request protection claimed by the test and documentation. **Smallest correction:** use distinguishable old/new snapshots with a deferred response and assert the newer content survives, or remain on `read-03` while releasing the old response.

6. **[P2] Assert the collected script-node count** — `tests/reader.rendered.test.ts:311–315`  
   The hostile-content check asserts `anchors` twice and never asserts `scripts`. A reader containing literal hostile text plus an injected script node can pass this browser safety check. The current global script count also includes Vite’s legitimate bootstrap scripts. **Smallest correction:** collect script nodes within the reader and replace the duplicate anchor assertion with a zero-script assertion.

**Overall verdict: correct — no merge-blocking findings; the findings above are report-only P2s.** Parent-run passing checks were reviewed as supplied evidence, not reviewer-executed validation.

name: pi-subagents
description: |
  Delegate work to Pi subagents after the operator asks for it: one child,
  parallel or scripted workflows, async runs, resume/steer/stop, review fanout,
  and multi-lane or worktree orchestration.
---

# Pi Subagents

The parent works directly by default. Invoke subagents only when the operator
requested delegation in the current request or through applicable user/project
instructions. Task size, complexity, risk, tool-call count, recipe fit, or an
available specialist does not independently authorize delegation.

Once authorized, choose the smallest bounded shape that earns its token and
elapsed-time overhead through evidence, independent review, specialization,
useful parallelism, or isolation. A single child is valid. The parent keeps
intent, routing, decisions, final acceptance, and publication authority, and
does the work itself where that is cheaper.

## Calls

```typescript
subagent({ agent: "worker", task: "<brief>" })                    // one child; async by default
subagent({ workflow: "parallel", args: { tasks: [{ agent, task, cwd?, model? }] } })  // independent children
subagent({ workflow: true })              // runs the one ```js workflow block in this same reply
subagent({ workflow: "./lane.js", args }) // script file, path relative to the request cwd
subagent({ action: "validate", workflow: "./lane.js" })          // check a script without launching
subagent({ action: "status", id })        // options: { view: "fleet" } or { view: "transcript", index: 0 }
subagent({ action: "resume", id, message })   // completed or paused child; returns a new run id
subagent({ action: "steer", id, message })    // live async child
subagent({ action: "stop", id })              // ends the run; not resumable
subagent({ action: "interrupt", id })         // pauses the child's current turn
subagent({ action: "list" })  ·  subagent({ action: "models" })
subagent({ action: "guide", options: { topic: "<section address>" } })
```

Launches are async by default. Set `async: false` only when the parent must
block; final reviews and gates stay async. After launching, keep doing safe
independent work, or yield: native completion wakes this session. Do not sleep,
poll, or call `bg_wait` for ordinary children. Use `bg_wait` only for provider
or detached work that has no native notification and whose result this turn
needs.

## Workflow scripts

Use a script when later steps depend on earlier results, or for keyed,
retried, aggregated, or resumed children. Write one ```` ```js workflow ````
block in the reply and call `subagent({ workflow: true })` in the same reply.
For a long script, write it to a file and pass `workflow: "./path.js"`; calls in
one reply run at the same time, so write the file in one reply and `validate` or
launch it in the next. When a `workflow: true` call reports the block missing,
pass the source as `options: { script: "..." }` in place of `workflow: true` for
the rest of the turn: on some hosts, text after a tool call reaches the session
as a summary without the block.

```js workflow
const scan = await runs.run("scan", { label: "Map auth flow", agent: "scout", task: "..." });
const reviews = await runs.all([
  { key: "correctness", label: "Review auth correctness", agent: "reviewer", task: "... " + scan.output },
  { key: "tests", label: "Review auth tests", agent: "reviewer", task: "..." },
]);
return reviews.map((review) => review.output);
```

- Scripts are statement bodies with an explicit `return`, top-level `await`,
  and plain helpers. Nested async functions, arrows, and methods are rejected.
- Every `runs.run` / `runs.all` item needs a stable `key`. Add a short
  verb + behavior `label` unless the user gave one.
- Bind files with `output: "plans/x.md"` (relative paths land in run
  artifacts) and return `outputReference` or `artifactPaths`. A filename in
  task text does not route output. Never send reports to the repo root.
- `runs.lanes([{ key, stages: [...] }])` runs a predeclared plan: first stages
  together, later stages in order per lane.

Resuming a retained child:

```js workflow
let child = await runs.run("fix-1", { agent: "worker", task: "..." });
child = await runs.run("fix-2", { resume: child.runId, task: "Apply these accepted findings: ..." });
return child.output;
```

- Always resume the latest returned run id; every resume returns a new one.
- Use a new stable key for every resume pass.
- `resume` excludes `agent` and `gate`; the child keeps its agent, model, and tools.
- Resume a completed child; steer a live one. Top-level `{ action: "resume" }` is detached.

## Briefs

Every child starts cold. Its task states: goal; repo, explicit `cwd`, and
ref; authority and edit boundary; relevant files, decisions, and evidence;
success criteria; validation; expected output; and when to stop or ask.
Make parallel briefs differ by seam, evidence, and decision, not just an item
number.

## Rules

- One writer per cwd or worktree. Parallelize reading, review, and
  validation. `worktree: true` needs a clean checkout (untracked files count;
  `.pi/subagents/` does not). For Pi extension repos, put lane worktrees
  outside `~/.pi/agent/extensions`, for example `~/.pi/agent/worktrees`.
- Reviewers use fresh context. Use `context: "fork"` only when the child needs
  the parent's history; it requires a persisted parent session.
- Children do not spawn subagents unless the parent delegated fanout and their
  resolved `tools` include `subagent`.
- A failed workflow, launch, prompt runtime, extension load, or child tool
  setup blocks the lane. Stop, report the exact failure and run/worktree state,
  verify a clean worktree or capture the partial diff, then retry the same way
  once. Switching to `interactive_shell`, `pi -ne`, or another CLI needs owner
  approval.
- As a conservative orchestration policy, do not pass a hard `toolBudget` or tight `usageBudget` to mutation-capable workers. The default tool budget blocks read/search tools rather than mutation tools. If interrupted after a tool call starts, checkpoint after the current tool returns with changed files, build/test state, and commit or PR state.
- Route workers and scouts to a fast capable tier, serious reviews to a strong
  tier, and top reasoning only to bounded read-only critique. Exact model names
  belong in user or project settings, not here.
- `subagent`, `subagents_enable`, `subagent_supervisor`, `contact_supervisor`, and `structured_output` are model-only: call them as ordinary model tool calls. Codemode scripts cannot reach them through `tools.*`, `ALL_TOOLS`, or `searchTools`.
- Receipts, CI, and review bots are evidence, not authority. Backlog, release,
  and merge policy belong to the user's or project's own skill.

## Look up the rest

If only `subagents_enable` is visible, call it first; `subagent` and `guide`
work from the next request. Read one section, not a whole topic:

| Need | Guide section |
| --- | --- |
| Script API: `runs.*`, `state`, limits | `workflows/scripted-workflows` |
| Typed gates, host commands, rolling fanout | `workflows/typed-post-run-checks-and-typed-steps`, `workflows/host-command-steps`, `workflows/advanced-rolling-child-runs` |
| Budgets, timeouts, `baseRef`, `gate`, `output` | `tool-reference/execution-parameters`, `tool-reference/output-mode-details` |
| Fresh or forked context | `tool-reference/fork-context-details` |
| Resume, steer modes, stop, status | `tool-reference/retained-children`, `tool-reference/resume`, `tool-reference/steer`, `tool-reference/stop`, `tool-reference/status` |
| Acceptance and review gates | `tool-reference/acceptance-gates` |
| Worktrees and handoffs | `workflows/worktree-isolation` |
| Child asks the parent (`contact_supervisor`) | `workflows/supervisor-coordination-child-asks-parent` |
| Agent create, update, eject, disable, refine | `tool-reference/management-actions`, `agents/frontmatter-reference` |
| Missions and schedules | `missions/missions`, `missions/schedules` |
| Watchdog | `watchdog/when-it-runs`, `watchdog/choosing-a-model` |
| Model overrides and profiles | `models/setting-defaults-and-overrides` |
| Other projects in panes | `tool-reference/herdr-project-panes` |
| Setup looks wrong | `subagent({ action: "doctor" })` |

## References

- Choosing roles, writing prompts, review/research/cleanup techniques, oracle → [prompting-and-roles.md](references/prompting-and-roles.md)
- Several lanes, worktrees, repositories, staged fixes, review loops, finding and gate triage → [orchestration.md](references/orchestration.md)
- Advisor council → [../council-mode/SKILL.md](../council-mode/SKILL.md)

content.text:
# Orchestration

Use this when several tasks need coordinated children, worktrees, or
repositories, or when a change goes through write, review, and fix rounds.
Create lanes only after delegation is operator-authorized and each lane
materially improves evidence, independent review, specialization, useful
parallelism, or isolated execution. Keep dependent work serial.

## Recipes

Recipes select a shape; they do not authorize delegation. Pick the smallest:

- **Recon then implement:** one focused `scout`, then one `worker` that gets its findings.
- **Implementation:** settle scope and acceptance first, then use a scout, writer, or fresh reviewer only where that stage earns its overhead. Split large work into serial milestones, not a writer swarm.
- **Parallel analysis:** fan out only independent read, review, or validation work, or give each writer its own worktree.

## Seams before writers

Before launching a writer for substantial mutation work, classify it as
**single-seam** or **multi-seam**. Two or more independently testable
contracts or source boundaries make it multi-seam. One PR does not imply one
writer.

- **Multi-seam:** give each component writer exclusive file or contract
  ownership, a focused gate, and a committed or otherwise durable handoff.
  Start one integration-only owner after those handoffs are ready. Repartition
  any writer brief that owns all major outcomes across independent boundaries.
- **Single-seam:** one writer is right when the work is one coupled seam, or
  when splitting would create overlapping ownership or artificial handoffs.
  Record that evidence. Do not split coupled work to raise the lane count.

## Lane board

Before more than one mutation-capable lane starts, record in the parent:

`Lane | repo/cwd | decision | owned files or contract | isolation path | authority | next gate | handoff | why independent`

One source seam or decision is one lane. Record each lane's delivery target,
allowed actions, validation, and review rigor. For cross-repository work,
name the shared contract and which repository changes first. A blocked
decision is a lane state: owner, options, recommended default, and the
evidence needed to continue.

Mutation lanes need distinct isolation paths and explicit `cwd` values.
`worktree: true` branches from `HEAD` (or `baseRef`) and refuses a dirty
checkout; in a shared or dirty checkout, commit first or give each lane a
worktree you created. Use one async workflow for a coordinated wave:
`runs.all` for independent lanes, `runs.run` for dependent stages, repo slug
or lane key in every child key and output path.

While one lane waits, run safe independent preparation, validation, or
read-only review. When only async lanes remain, record what reopens work and
yield; completion wakes the parent.

## Review loop

1. Inspect the source, diff, issue, or plan directly.
2. One writer implements inside its boundary and runs focused validation that can fail for the changed behavior.
3. When the delegation contract calls for independent review, fresh-context read-only reviewers inspect the actual worktree. Otherwise parent inspection is enough; skip review for trivial wording, renames, or local probes.
4. The parent classifies findings (below) and sends accepted fixes to one writer: resume the original worker with its latest run id, or launch one forked `worker` as `/review-loop` does.
5. Re-run affected validation and review only the changed blast radius.
6. Stop when no blocker or fix worth doing now remains, an unapproved product, scope, or architecture decision appears, or the round cap is reached (default 3). Do not loop for polish. Children never decide the loop outcome.

An async writer's handoff is an intermediate state, not completion, unless the
user asked for writer-only work.

| Situation | Review shape |
| --- | --- |
| One coherent diff or risk | one reviewer |
| Independent risks (correctness, tests, security, UI) | parallel reviewers with distinct contracts |
| Possible over-scope | same-writer challenge before fresh review |
| Material design tradeoff | council mode |

### Staged fixes

When reviews have produced findings across several clusters:

1. Run a read-only planning fanout, one reviewer per cluster or angle, each returning exact files, lines, fixes, and validation.
2. Classify the accepted fixes as single-seam or multi-seam (above) on the lane board before any writer starts.
3. Give a writer only its assigned stage. Pass each earlier result into the later task by variable or by its declared `output` path, not as a whole aggregate blob. With `runs.lanes`, keep stages narrow: red test, helper change, one render seam, validation, review.
4. Validate the integrated result with fresh read-only reviewers on distinct angles.

When a child returns a target list, validate it in JavaScript and map bounded
entries into `runs.all`.

## Finding disposition

Classify each finding against the current head:

- **Valid blocker:** concrete failure, repro, security issue, contract mismatch, or source-proven regression. Fix now.
- **Valid non-blocker:** real but outside the slice. Record or defer.
- **Stale:** already fixed or absent. Cite current evidence.
- **Invalid:** contradicted by source, tests, docs, or approved scope. Cite it.
- **Out of scope or policy:** needs an unapproved product, architecture, authority, or release decision. Escalate.
- **Speculative:** no contract, repro, or reachable failure. Do not block.

Classify bot comments the same way before assigning severity.

## Gate failures

1. Confirm the run belongs to the exact head under judgment.
2. Read the focused failing log; name the failing test, assertion, or contract.
3. Classify: current diff, stale test, environment, or existing flake.
4. Reproduce with the narrowest command when practical.
5. Patch forward when the diff caused it. For a stale or flaky failure, collect proof before one rerun.
6. Re-run the affected command or exact-head gate after every fix.

## Handoff and cleanup

A handoff states lane status, repository and worktree, changed files,
validation, open decisions, next action, and artifact or receipt paths. Copy
only final evidence to memory, a mission, a PR, or an approved docs path, then
remove scratch reports from the worktree.

Keep a worktree until its handoff is durable, no run owns it, and no later
gate needs it. If a run stops or needs attention, preserve its worktree and
artifacts, then resume that run or start one replacement lane from the
handoff. Never start a second writer while worktree ownership is unclear.

Before reporting done, check the board: every lane terminal or blocked with a
named next action; one writer per worktree; required validation and fresh
review done; accepted findings fixed and revalidated; publication authority
present before any push, comment, merge, or release; residual risks and
skipped checks stated.

sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- subagent: Delegate focused work to child agents; compose multi-child work in one workflow call.
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- bg_start: Run a long-lived shell command in the background (dev servers, builds, watchers); output is captured and you're notified on exit
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use bg_start for commands expected to run long or indefinitely (servers, watch modes, long builds); use the regular bash tool for quick commands.
- bg_start processes receive no stdin — never start a command that requires interactive input.
- After bg_start, keep working; the exit result arrives automatically. Use bg_status only when you need current output before continuing.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>
