toolsAdded.name: subagent
toolsAdded.description:
One child: {agent,task}. Independent parallel children: {workflow:"parallel",args:{tasks:[{agent,task},...]}}. Dependent multi-step work: exactly one top-level subagent workflow call with async:true; write one ```js workflow block in this reply, then call subagent({workflow:true}); children launch only inside it.
Management: {action,id?,options:{...}}; fields not in this schema go in options.
Launch agents by name and pass models as exact provider/id; an unknown agent or model returns the valid choices.
Details: guide workflows/recommended-orchestration-pattern (async, review, failure recovery), guide workflows/scripted-workflows, guide tool-reference/retained-children, guide tool-reference/external-cli-agent-profiles.

SAFETY-CRITICAL SUBAGENT GUIDANCE:
- Delegate only when the operator asked, directly or through applicable user/project instructions; size, complexity or risk alone is not authorization.
- Native async completion wakes this session: return control; do not sleep, poll or call bg_wait for it.
- One writer per cwd/worktree; isolate concurrent writers.
- After a launch or runtime failure, stop and report it; never silently switch to interactive_shell, pi -ne or another CLI.

workflow.description: true: run the one ```js workflow block written in this same reply (false invalid). String with '/': script file read from request cwd. Other string: named workflow resource. Raw scripts (true or path) have no runs.host.

args.description: Plain-JSON args for workflow; 16 fields/object, 64 items/array, depth 8, 16 KiB total; raw-script args are exposed deeply frozen and persisted, so do not include secrets.

async.description: Background; default asyncByDefault. false only to block parent.

model.description: Child model provider/id; bare id only if unique. Suffix :off/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max overrides agent thinking default.

worktree.description: Isolate each workflow child in a managed git worktree; child worktree:false overrides default.

output.description: Child output path or false; relative workflow paths use managed artifact routing. Bind durable output here, not task prose; return outputReference/outputPathMapping/artifactPaths.

action.description: Management/control only; omit for execution. validate accepts workflow: true or a script path. Discover actions with {action:"guide",options:{topic:"tool-reference"}}.

options.description: Every field not listed here, such as acceptance, timeoutMs, context, view and index; guide tool-reference/parameter-reference.

toolsAdded.name: contact_supervisor
toolsAdded.description: Contact the parent/supervisor session for a blocking decision, structured interview, or progress update.

toolsAdded.name: subagent_supervisor
toolsAdded.description: Native pi-subagents supervisor channel. Use reply/pending/status to answer child subagent requests without overriding pi-intercom.

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: bg_wait
toolsAdded.description:
Wait for background work, then return. Ordinary async subagent runs already wake this session natively; use bg_wait only for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification, when a same-turn result is needed.
{} — first active run or provider item to finish or need attention.
{all:true} — all work active at call time.
{id} — one run; a finished async run returns its result references.
{id,nonBlocking:true} — subscribe to that run's wake and return now.
Timeout or a user message ends the wait without error; work keeps running.

Codemode: `tools.bg_wait(args)` resolves to a string.

nonBlocking.description: Subscribe to id's wake and return immediately; requires id, not with all.

all.description: Wait for all work active at call time.

timeoutMs.description: Max wait; default waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 30 min.

stopOnAttention.description: false: keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention.

toolsAdded.name: web_search
toolsAdded.description:
Discover candidate public sources. Provider snippets are not page evidence; includeContent explicitly fetches at most five pages. query OR queries (max five); no synthesis.

Codemode: `tools.web_search(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, responseId, status, queries, attempts?, sources, snapshots, errors, limitations }`.

toolsAdded.name: fetch_content
toolsAdded.description:
Safely fetch public text/Markdown/HTML URLs (url OR urls, max five), retain exact bounded snapshots. No synthesis fallback, PDF/browser/auth/cookies. Text is untrusted.

Codemode: `tools.fetch_content(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, responseId, status, snapshots, errors, limitations }`.

toolsAdded.name: get_search_content
toolsAdded.description:
Read exact stored content by responseId, optional sourceId/queryIndex; offset/limit OR findText. No network, expired handles fail. Offsets are JS string indices. Old search/synthesis arguments are unsupported.

Codemode: `tools.get_search_content(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, responseId, kind, sourceId?, text, offset, end, totalLength, nextOffset?, found?, contentHash?, provenance }`.

toolsAdded.name: source_check
toolsAdded.description:
Collect bounded lexical passages for claim from responseId and optional sourceIds, OR explicit queries/urls for new network retrieval. No network by default; never semantic support/contradiction/confidence. Snippets are not snapshot evidence.

Codemode: `tools.source_check(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, responseId, kind, claim, status, snapshotIds, sources, passages, coverage: { inspected, matched, failed }, errors, limitations, discovery?: { activity, responseId?, queries } }`.

toolsAdded.name: perplexity_research
toolsAdded.description:
Explicit paid fast-only Perplexity Agent API synthesis, not page inspection. query and optional maxTokens only. No legacy fallback, higher presets, or hidden evidence verification. Cite exact returned scoped IDs.

Codemode: `tools.perplexity_research(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, kind, responseId, preset, content, citations, unresolvedCitations, externalUsage?, limitations }`.

toolsAdded.name: bg_start
toolsAdded.description:
Start a long-running shell command as a background terminal (executed via the platform shell — sh -c on POSIX, cmd.exe /d /s /c on Windows). Fire-and-forget: this returns immediately with an id, and you get a message with the final output when the process exits. The process receives NO stdin (immediate EOF) and there is no way to send input later — interactive commands will not work; use bg_kill to stop a stuck one. Terminals are session-scoped: they are killed when the session ends or reloads. Output shown to you is tail-truncated (stdout 16.0KB, stderr 8.0KB); the full logs are captured to files and in the /ps viewer. Max 8 background terminals can run at once.

Codemode: `tools.bg_start(args)` resolves to a string.

command.description: Shell command line to run in the background (sh -c on POSIX, cmd.exe /d /s /c on Windows). It receives no stdin (EOF immediately); interactive commands will not work.

title.description: Short human-readable name shown in listings and the UI

toolsAdded.name: bg_status
toolsAdded.description:
Peek at a background terminal's status and current output (tail-truncated) without blocking. If the terminal already exited, this returns its final state.

Codemode: `tools.bg_status(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: bg_list
toolsAdded.description:
List all background terminals (running and settled) with pid, elapsed time, exit status, and output sizes.

Codemode: `tools.bg_list(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: bg_kill
toolsAdded.description:
Stop one or more running background terminals (SIGTERM to the whole process tree, escalating to SIGKILL). Returns each terminal's final state; already-settled ids are reported as such.

Codemode: `tools.bg_kill(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. A tool whose declaration returns an object resolves on failure too when it returned that object; check its fields. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

content.text:
---
name: pi-subagents
description: |
  Delegate work to Pi subagents after the operator asks for it: one child,
  parallel or scripted workflows, async runs, resume/steer/stop, review fanout,
  and multi-lane or worktree orchestration.
---

# Pi Subagents

The parent works directly by default. Invoke subagents only when the operator
requested delegation in the current request or through applicable user/project
instructions. Task size, complexity, risk, tool-call count, recipe fit, or an
available specialist does not independently authorize delegation.

Once authorized, choose the smallest bounded shape that earns its token and
elapsed-time overhead through evidence, independent review, specialization,
useful parallelism, or isolation. A single child is valid. The parent keeps
intent, routing, decisions, final acceptance, and publication authority, and
does the work itself where that is cheaper.

## Calls

```typescript
subagent({ agent: "worker", task: "<brief>" })                    // one child; async by default
subagent({ workflow: "parallel", args: { tasks: [{ agent, task, cwd?, model? }] } })  // independent children
subagent({ workflow: true })              // runs the one ```js workflow block in this same reply
subagent({ workflow: "./lane.js", args }) // script file, path relative to the request cwd
subagent({ action: "validate", workflow: "./lane.js" })          // check a script without launching
subagent({ action: "status", id })        // options: { view: "fleet" } or { view: "transcript", index: 0 }
subagent({ action: "resume", id, message })   // completed or paused child; returns a new run id
subagent({ action: "steer", id, message })    // live async child
subagent({ action: "stop", id })              // ends the run; not resumable
subagent({ action: "interrupt", id })         // pauses the child's current turn
subagent({ action: "list" })  ·  subagent({ action: "models" })
subagent({ action: "guide", options: { topic: "<section address>" } })
```

Launches are async by default. Set `async: false` only when the parent must
block; final reviews and gates stay async. After launching, keep doing safe
independent work, or yield: native completion wakes this session. Do not sleep,
poll, or call `bg_wait` for ordinary children. Use `bg_wait` only for provider
or detached work that has no native notification and whose result this turn
needs.

## Workflow scripts

Use a script when later steps depend on earlier results, or for keyed,
retried, aggregated, or resumed children. Write one ```` ```js workflow ````
block in the reply and call `subagent({ workflow: true })` in the same reply.
For a long script, write it to a file and pass `workflow: "./path.js"`; calls in
one reply run at the same time, so write the file in one reply and `validate` or
launch it in the next. When a `workflow: true` call reports the block missing,
pass the source as `options: { script: "..." }` in place of `workflow: true` for
the rest of the turn: on some hosts, text after a tool call reaches the session
as a summary without the block.

```js workflow
const scan = await runs.run("scan", { label: "Map auth flow", agent: "scout", task: "..." });
const reviews = await runs.all([
  { key: "correctness", label: "Review auth correctness", agent: "reviewer", task: "... " + scan.output },
  { key: "tests", label: "Review auth tests", agent: "reviewer", task: "..." },
]);
return reviews.map((review) => review.output);
```

- Scripts are statement bodies with an explicit `return`, top-level `await`,
  and plain helpers. Nested async functions, arrows, and methods are rejected.
- Every `runs.run` / `runs.all` item needs a stable `key`. Add a short
  verb + behavior `label` unless the user gave one.
- Bind files with `output: "plans/x.md"` (relative paths land in run
  artifacts) and return `outputReference` or `artifactPaths`. A filename in
  task text does not route output. Never send reports to the repo root.
- `runs.lanes([{ key, stages: [...] }])` runs a predeclared plan: first stages
  together, later stages in order per lane.

Resuming a retained child:

```js workflow
let child = await runs.run("fix-1", { agent: "worker", task: "..." });
child = await runs.run("fix-2", { resume: child.runId, task: "Apply these accepted findings: ..." });
return child.output;
```

- Always resume the latest returned run id; every resume returns a new one.
- Use a new stable key for every resume pass.
- `resume` excludes `agent` and `gate`; the child keeps its agent, model, and tools.
- Resume a completed child; steer a live one. Top-level `{ action: "resume" }` is detached.

## Briefs

Every child starts cold. Its task states: goal; repo, explicit `cwd`, and
ref; authority and edit boundary; relevant files, decisions, and evidence;
success criteria; validation; expected output; and when to stop or ask.
Make parallel briefs differ by seam, evidence, and decision, not just an item
number.

## Rules

- One writer per cwd or worktree. Parallelize reading, review, and
  validation. `worktree: true` needs a clean checkout (untracked files count;
  `.pi/subagents/` does not). For Pi extension repos, put lane worktrees
  outside `~/.pi/agent/extensions`, for example `~/.pi/agent/worktrees`.
- Reviewers use fresh context. Use `context: "fork"` only when the child needs
  the parent's history; it requires a persisted parent session.
- Children do not spawn subagents unless the parent delegated fanout and their
  resolved `tools` include `subagent`.
- A failed workflow, launch, prompt runtime, extension load, or child tool
  setup blocks the lane. Stop, report the exact failure and run/worktree state,
  verify a clean worktree or capture the partial diff, then retry the same way
  once. Switching to `interactive_shell`, `pi -ne`, or another CLI needs owner
  approval.
- As a conservative orchestration policy, do not pass a hard `toolBudget` or tight `usageBudget` to mutation-capable workers. The default tool budget blocks read/search tools rather than mutation tools. If interrupted after a tool call starts, checkpoint after the current tool returns with changed files, build/test state, and commit or PR state.
- Route workers and scouts to a fast capable tier, serious reviews to a strong
  tier, and top reasoning only to bounded read-only critique. Exact model names
  belong in user or project settings, not here.
- `subagent`, `subagents_enable`, `subagent_supervisor`, `contact_supervisor`, and `structured_output` are model-only: call them as ordinary model tool calls. Codemode scripts cannot reach them through `tools.*`, `ALL_TOOLS`, or `searchTools`.
- Receipts, CI, and review bots are evidence, not authority. Backlog, release,
  and merge policy belong to the user's or project's own skill.

## Look up the rest

If only `subagents_enable` is visible, call it first; `subagent` and `guide`
work from the next request. Read one section, not a whole topic:

| Need | Guide section |
| --- | --- |
| Script API: `runs.*`, `state`, limits | `workflows/scripted-workflows` |
| Typed gates, host commands, rolling fanout | `workflows/typed-post-run-checks-and-typed-steps`, `workflows/host-command-steps`, `workflows/advanced-rolling-child-runs` |
| Budgets, timeouts, `baseRef`, `gate`, `output` | `tool-reference/execution-parameters`, `tool-reference/output-mode-details` |
| Fresh or forked context | `tool-reference/fork-context-details` |
| Resume, steer modes, stop, status | `tool-reference/retained-children`, `tool-reference/resume`, `tool-reference/steer`, `tool-reference/stop`, `tool-reference/status` |
| Acceptance and review gates | `tool-reference/acceptance-gates` |
| Worktrees and handoffs | `workflows/worktree-isolation` |
| Child asks the parent (`contact_supervisor`) | `workflows/supervisor-coordination-child-asks-parent` |
| Agent create, update, eject, disable, refine | `tool-reference/management-actions`, `agents/frontmatter-reference` |
| Missions and schedules | `missions/missions`, `missions/schedules` |
| Watchdog | `watchdog/when-it-runs`, `watchdog/choosing-a-model` |
| Model overrides and profiles | `models/setting-defaults-and-overrides` |
| Other projects in panes | `tool-reference/herdr-project-panes` |
| Setup looks wrong | `subagent({ action: "doctor" })` |

## References

- Choosing roles, writing prompts, review/research/cleanup techniques, oracle → [prompting-and-roles.md](references/prompting-and-roles.md)
- Several lanes, worktrees, repositories, staged fixes, review loops, finding and gate triage → [orchestration.md](references/orchestration.md)
- Advisor council → [../council-mode/SKILL.md](../council-mode/SKILL.md)

## Recommended orchestration pattern

Use orchestration as parent-agent guidance, not as a runtime workflow mode. For implementation work, the recommended loop is:

```text
clarify → scout → worker → fresh reviewers → worker
```

Packaged `worker` defaults to fresh context so implementation starts from its assigned brief instead of the parent's unfinished conversation. Packaged `oracle` and `advisor` default to forked context; if the parent has no persisted session file or current leaf yet, that implicit default falls back to `fresh`. Explicit `context`, `context: "profile"`, and global `defaultSubagentContext` still override these profile defaults.

Launch children in the background (`async` follows `asyncByDefault`, normally true) and consume each result at the point a later step depends on it. Native completion wakes the parent session, so the parent returns control instead of sleeping or polling. Use `async: false` only when the parent must block, not for final reviews or gates. When an oracle or advisor reaches an unknown that needs a decision, it asks through supervisor dialogue; use a one-shot oracle call only when one was requested.

A background child awaited by an `async: false` workflow cannot receive a supervisor decision while its parent is blocked in that call. Its native `contact_supervisor` decision or interview request returns a tool error promptly, asking it to report the blocker and partial results and stop. The transport error is not a supervisor reply or approval. Use `async: true` for workflows whose children may need a decision. Progress updates remain non-blocking, and an explicit child `async: true` still returns its launch receipt without being awaited.

Child-safety boundaries are enforced at runtime:

- Child sessions do not receive the bundled `pi-subagents` skill.
- Child context filtering removes parent-only subagent artifacts (hidden orchestration-instruction messages, slash/status/control messages, and `subagent` tool-call/tool-result history) while preserving ordinary prose and unrelated tool calls/results. A forked child sends the history it inherited exactly as the parent sent it, so its first request can reuse the parent's prompt cache; it still cannot run `subagent`.
- By default, children do not register the `subagent` tool and receive boundary instructions that they are not the parent orchestrator and must not propose or run subagents.
- The explicit exception is an agent whose resolved builtin `tools` includes `subagent`; that child gets a child-safe `subagent` tool for the fanout work the parent assigned, still bounded by `maxSubagentDepth`.

Yes. The handoff inspection caught two remaining gaps in the accepted fixes: the loading-focus helper can still steal focus from an outside control, and the synthetic reply defaults ignore stored Reply-To metadata. I’ll send these back to the original workers before integrating. Main is still unchanged.

## Scripted workflows

Use direct `{ agent, task }` for one bounded child. Use a workflow script when the parent needs a stable keyed child, sequence, fanout, steering, retry, or aggregation. For ordinary parallel fanout, use `await runs.all([{ key, agent, task }, ...])`. It resolves to an ordered array, not a key map, so use indexes, destructuring, or `.map(...)`, not `results.<key>`. Do not read `.output` from unawaited `runs.run` launches. Store a `runs.run` promise only when the script later observes it with `await`, `Promise.race`, or `Promise.all`, such as steering a live child before awaiting its result. Scripts are ordinary JavaScript statement bodies. Use an explicit `return` for a useful result.

Use top-level `await`, plain helper functions, or Promise chains; nested async functions, async arrows, and async methods are rejected (see [opt-in bounded workflows](#opt-in-bounded-workflows)).

The `workflow` field selects the script source:

- `workflow: true` runs the one ```` ```js workflow ```` fenced block written in the same assistant reply as the `subagent` call. The script is plain text in the reply, so it needs no JSON string escaping. A reply can carry exactly one such block and one `workflow: true` call; zero or several blocks fail. A reply with no tagged block may instead carry exactly one plain ```` ```js ```` block, which then runs. A line containing only ```` ``` ```` (three or more backticks, optionally followed by spaces or tabs) ends the block, so keep Markdown fences inside quoted strings.
- A string containing `/` (or `\` in a Windows path), such as `workflow: "./workflows/review.js"`, is a script file.
- Any other string, such as `workflow: "review"`, is a [named workflow resource](#named-workflow-resources-for-permission-extensions). The string `"true"` is read as `workflow: true`, because some MCP clients send the boolean as a string.

`workflow: true` works only from a model tool call. Slash commands, RPC, and schedules pass scripts through their own inputs. Examples below that show only a ```` ```js workflow ```` block run with `subagent({ workflow: true })` in the same reply.

For multi-step or parallel work, make exactly one top-level `subagent` workflow call with `async:true` and launch children only inside it. Read this guide for recipes rather than constructing a second top-level orchestration. Available sandbox helpers include `runs.run`, `runs.all`, `runs.lanes`, `runs.steer`, `runs.status`, `runs.ref`/`runs.refs`, `emit`, `console`, standard JavaScript, and mission `state` when enabled. No filesystem, shell, arbitrary Pi tools, or host globals are available; named resources alone may grant `runs.host` authority.

Workflow-level child controls default onto each `runs.run`/`runs.all` launch; explicit child fields override them. See [retained children](tool-reference.md#retained-children) for follow-up challenges, [output binding](tool-reference.md#output-mode-details) for durable artifacts, and [schedules](missions.md#schedules) for delayed/recurring scripts.

Child results cross into the script as plain JSON data. Non-JSON host metadata is omitted, so use returned fields such as `runId`, `ok`, `output`, and `structuredOutput` for workflow control.

Omitting a child's `async` preserves awaited final-result semantics, even if the child runs in the background. Explicit child `async: true` intentionally returns after launch: its receipt has `state: "running"`, `ok: false`, an empty `output`, and no completion error or final `outputReference`. `ok` confirms successful child completion, not successful dispatch. It does not confirm that the task's intent was carried out: a child that declines or cannot do the work can still end normally. When later steps depend on the work having happened, give the child an `outputSchema` with an explicit status field (and check `structuredOutput` in the script) or a host-run `gate`, and treat only that verdict as success. Use `runId` and `asyncDir` to inspect the running child; `artifactPaths` may include runtime directories and is not a list of final reports. Reusing the same workflow key returns the same receipt, not a refreshed result.

A workflow can finish dispatch while these children remain running. Its summary and child rows identify that distinction, and launch receipts do not generate child-completion notices. Consume the later child result before treating its work or report as complete.

Validate a script without launching children:

```js workflow
const results = await runs.all([{ key: "scan", agent: "scout", task: "Scan" }]);
return results[0].output;
```

```js
subagent({ action: "validate", workflow: true });
```

For a script stored in a file, pass its path:

```js
subagent({ workflow: "./workflows/review.js", cwd: "/path/to/project" });
subagent({ action: "validate", workflow: "./workflows/review.js" });
```

Relative paths resolve against the request `cwd`; absolute paths pass through. The host reads the file before validation, schedule creation, or workflow sandbox execution. The sandbox still has no filesystem access. Missing, unreadable, and empty files return file input errors instead of script syntax errors.

Reply-block and file-backed scripts accept bounded plain-JSON `args`:

```js
subagent({ workflow: "./workflows/review.js", args: { target: "src/workflows" } });
// workflows/review.js
return runs.run("review", { agent: "reviewer", task: `Review ${args.target}` });
```

Omitted arguments are an empty object. The `args` object, its nested objects, and its arrays are frozen in the sandbox. Arguments are data only: they do not grant `runs.host` or other authority. Normalized arguments are persisted with workflow and schedule evidence for replay and diagnosis, so do not put secrets in them. Routine status text does not render argument values.

# UX-02 — Conversation reader: implemented contract and evidence

Status: implemented at the component/shell level and validated with the
repository's automated gates plus the opt-in real-Chrome suites. Real-Chrome
runs cover the reader journey, scroll/anchor behavior, and covered-surface
focus safety in the synthetic browser preview only. Native fixture/WKWebView,
VoiceOver/assistive-technology, and platform clipboard verification remain
**explicitly pending**. Browser passes do not establish native IPC/provider
correctness or Superhuman fidelity.

Grounding: `docs/superhuman-browsing-implementation-plan.md` (UX-02; acceptance
complete BROWSE-05 and the copy portion of BROWSE-15) and the UX-02 section of
`superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md` (message focus/expansion, participant
details, copy-only contact controls, reader scrolling).

## Bounded UX-02 contract

What shipped:

- **Visit-scoped message state** inside the mounted reader
  (`src/components/ReaderView.vue`), keyed by account+conversation reference and
  message ID — never array position. Per visit: active message ID, expanded IDs,
  details-disclosure state, and a viewport-relative scroll anchor with a
  `scrollTop` fallback. State survives J/K round trips and same-reference
  background replacements for the life of the mounted reader session and is
  released when the reader unmounts (close) or the account changes. Removed
  message IDs are pruned; a removed active/anchor ID resolves to the next
  surviving old neighbor, then the previous one; empty/loading/error states fall
  back to the reader article and never hold a stale target.
- **Initial focus/expansion:** opening a conversation focuses the newest cached
  message's toggle (not the article) with that message expanded; only as much of
  its header as needed is revealed. Ordinary `ol/li` semantics with a roving
  primary message-toggle button carrying `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`;
  focusing any control of a message updates its message identity.
- **Message movement (nonwrapping):** `N`/`P` move message focus one step
  without auto-expanding (clamped at both ends, no wrap). `O` toggles expansion
  of the focused message; `Shift+O` idempotently expands all messages. These are
  narrow methods exposed to App's single keyboard dispatcher — the reader adds
  no window listener — dispatched after the existing editor/IME/modifier/
  editable/overlay guards. Native Enter/Space button activation is preserved
  (one activation toggles expansion once, never a mailbox action), and the
  existing `e`/`Shift+U` action contracts work from the new message-toggle
  focus: a message toggle is the reader's navigation context, not a toolbar
  action button, so the conversation-level shortcuts remain usable there while
  every other focused button/link keeps the generic exclusion. Toolbar,
  editor/IME, overlay, capability, read-only, and stale-target guards are
  unchanged.
- **Reading progress across foreground loading:** the outgoing visit's
  viewport-relative scroll anchor is captured before any DOM teardown —
  including the foreground null/loading transition where the conversation is
  cleared before the next detail arrives — and retained through loading/error
  without being overwritten by the empty/loading DOM. Returning to a visit
  restores the exact scroll offset and viewport-relative message geometry, and
  revisit focus does not reveal-scroll over the restored offset (initial entry
  and explicit N/P still reveal the focused header as needed).
- **Conversation movement:** Inbox-origin reader `J/K` moves the reader cursor
  through the originating Inbox's current ready snapshot resolved against the
  current `openRef` (previous context ordering for a removed cursor, no wrap),
  without moving hidden list focus and without recapturing the entry origin.
  Activity-origin reader `J/K` is a strict no-op: no navigation, no hidden-focus
  mutation, no invented ordering of duplicate operation references, and no extra
  `getConversation` calls; `N/P/O` still work there.
- **Back/Escape restoration:** the original entry focus, account-scoped
  ordering, and non-null list anchor are captured only at the initial
  list-to-reader entry. Back (Escape/Close) restores the ORIGINAL entry thread
  and best anchor with the fallback chain: surviving entry reference → next
  surviving neighbor from the entry ordering → previous → first valid row →
  empty state. An Activity-origin Back reopens Activity without erasing the
  saved underlying Inbox anchor; explicit Inbox navigation keeps the list's own
  current focus instead.
- **Actions target the current open thread only.** Archive/read/reply use the
  CURRENT loaded open conversation; the saved origin is never an action target.
  Existing stale-request/late-receipt guards and request tokens are retained.
  Inbox archive auto-advance selects a surviving neighbor of the currently
  actioned conversation (`mailbox.focusedSummary` deliberately remains the
  original entry focus); an Activity-origin reader never advances into
  unrelated Inbox mail.
- **Participant details and context.** Each message exposes a native
  `<details>` disclosure with the complete known From/To addresses and sent
  timestamp; unknown Cc/Bcc and other headers are omitted, never fabricated.
  Participant names/addresses are keyboard-focusable context controls separate
  from the expansion toggle (no nested buttons). The active message's sender is
  the baseline reader contact; participant hover and keyboard focus each
  temporarily override it, keyboard focus wins, and exit (leave/blur, disclosure
  dismissal, message change, close) restores the baseline. Overrides are
  identity-qualified by conversation reference + message ID in App, so late
  blur/leave events, loading, removals, and account changes cannot leak a stale
  contact. A visible "Reply targets the latest message from …" label sits near
  Prepare reply so focusing an older message cannot imply a different reply
  target.
- **Copy controls (copy-only BROWSE-15 portion):** separately labelled
  copy-name (only when a display name is known) and copy-email buttons in
  `ContactPane.vue`, reachable by hover and keyboard. Activation uses
  `navigator.clipboard.writeText` only on explicit activation and reports
  success, failure, or unavailable-clipboard honestly via `role="status"`, with
  the text staying selectable for manual copy. Copying never triggers a draft,
  navigation, or any mailbox write, and adds no native permission.
- **Safety unchanged:** bodies render exclusively through text interpolation —
  no `v-html`, no HTML/Markdown processing, no remote assets; hostile markup
  stays literal text (asserted in real Chrome). Retained/incomplete/header
  checks, `unsupportedReason`/`contextComplete` disclosures, draft lifecycle and
  close protection, permission gates, no-auto-read, and overlay inertness are
  preserved.
- **Reader surface:** the reader is a bounded flex surface with its own content
  scroller and a persistent toolbar/Back affordance; the toolbar stays fixed
  while content scrolls beneath it (asserted with real layout geometry in
  Chrome). The 1000px Contact breakpoint and covered-surface inertness are
  preserved, including the wide contact column being inert while a utility
  drawer overlays it.

## Reconstruction choices (marked, not verified Superhuman fidelity)

- Escape precedence inside the reader: an open message-details disclosure is
  dismissed before the reader closes; utility drawers and the narrow Contact
  disclosure keep their existing earlier precedence.
- The participant context displays the participant's display name when present
  and the bare mailbox otherwise — the same known-fields rule as the rest of
  the contact pane.
- Newest message = last entry of the cached message stack (backend order is
  authoritative); no independent relevance ordering is invented.

## Post-review fix pass (validated P1 corrections)

Two P1 review findings were corrected in this slice's own files; everything
else in the review was report-only P2 and remains deferred/unfixed:

- **Reader actions from message-toggle focus (P1-A).** Opening and N/P focus a
  message-toggle button, which the old generic `buttonOwns()` guard treated
  like a toolbar button and used to suppress `e` and Gmail `Shift+U`. The
  approved clarification (message toggles are reader navigation context, not
  toolbar action buttons) is implemented via an `actionShortcutBlocked()` guard
  that exempts only `.message-toggle` targets. Regression coverage dispatches
  bubbling key events from the actual focused toggle in component tests and
  uses real CDP keys in Chrome: default initial focus and post-N/P focus,
  current-open (never focused-message or origin) targeting, enabled synthetic
  Gmail Shift+U (test-only account-status wrapper; no production authority
  change), native Enter toggling expansion exactly once with zero mailbox
  commands, and a focused toolbar button still being excluded. A temporary
  revert of the guard made the new tests fail, confirming they pin the fix.
- **Outgoing scroll capture across foreground loading (P1-B).** The visit
  watcher now captures the outgoing visit's scroll anchor before the
  null/loading return, retains it through loading/error, and never overwrites
  it from the empty/loading DOM (the capture is a no-op once the message
  elements are gone). Revisit focus no longer reveal-scrolls over the restored
  offset when a saved anchor exists. Coverage: component round trips
  ready → null/loading → ready → null/loading → ready with controlled geometry
  asserting exact restored scrollTop, viewport-relative message geometry, focus
  identity, and expansion state; plus a real-Chrome J/K round trip with
  delayed details and NO fixture notification between the manual scroll and J,
  asserting exact scrollTop 200, stable viewport-relative geometry, all
  expansions, and focus identity. A temporary revert of the capture made both
  new component tests and the Chrome round-trip test fail.

Explicitly still unfixed (report-only P2s from the same review): raw visit
pruning not republishing the resolved active message to App, reader arrow

# Background Terminals

Use `bg_start` for long-running commands; use regular `bash` for quick commands.

## Start

Call `bg_start` with:

- `command`: shell command to run
- `title`: short recognizable label
- `working_dir`: project directory when different from the current directory

Background commands receive no stdin. Never use them for interactive prompts.

After starting, continue useful work instead of polling. The terminal sends one completion message when it exits.

## Inspect and stop

- Use `bg_status` only when current output or status is needed.
- Use `bg_list` to inventory all tracked terminals.
- Use `bg_kill` when a process is no longer needed or is stuck; termination continues even if the tool wait is aborted.
- Tell the user they can open `/ps` to inspect live output and kill terminals interactively.

Prefer meaningful titles and avoid starting duplicate servers or watchers. Full output is captured to spill files; tool and completion output shows a concise tail. Terminals are session-scoped and are stopped during shutdown or reload.

name: reviewer
description: Versatile review specialist for code diffs, plans, proposed solutions, codebase health, and PR/issue validation. Enforces the sof-pi Review Rubric (priority tags, fail-fast error handling, required Human Reviewer Callouts).
tools: read, grep, find, ls
thinking: high

inheritProjectContext: true
inheritSkills: false
---

You are a disciplined review subagent. Your job is to inspect, evaluate, and report findings with evidence. You do not guess; you verify from the code, tests, docs, or requirements.

## Review types you handle

### 1. Code diffs (changed files)
Inspect the actual diff or changed files. Verify:
- Implementation matches intent and requirements.
- Code is correct, coherent, and handles edge cases.
- Tests cover the change and still pass.
- No unintended side effects or regressions.
- The change is minimal and readable.

### 2. Plans
Validate a proposed plan for:
- Feasibility and completeness.
- Missing steps or hidden risks.
- Alignment with existing architecture and constraints.
- Whether the scope is appropriately bounded.

### 3. Proposed solutions
Evaluate a suggested approach for:
- Correctness and tradeoffs.
- Fit with existing codebase patterns.
- Whether simpler alternatives exist.
- Edge cases the proposal may miss.

### 4. Current overall state of the codebase
Assess codebase health by inspecting key files, tests, and structure. Look for:
- Architecture drift or tech debt.
- Inconsistent patterns or naming.
- Areas lacking tests or documentation.
- Obvious bugs or fragile code.
- Opportunities to simplify or consolidate.

### 5. Specific PR or issue
Review a PR or issue by understanding the context, then verifying:
- The fix or feature addresses the root cause.
- Changes are minimal and focused.
- No regressions are introduced.
- Tests and docs are updated as needed.

## Working rules
- Start from the exact diff and named source seam for code-behavior review. Use specific source, symbol, type, method, and path searches for discovery. Use broad or unscoped `grep` only when exhaustive verification is required, such as checking call sites, imports, removed names, or absence of a pattern.
- Read the relevant files first. Read plan and progress when the task supplies them.
- Repo-local `progress.md` files are allowed scratch/memory files. Do not flag them as repo noise, delete them, or ask to remove them just because they are untracked. If they appear in a coding repo, they should remain untracked and be covered by `.gitignore`.
- Do not use shell commands or write files. Report any test or Git command that a supervisor must run.
- Do not invent issues. Only report problems you can justify from evidence.
- Prefer small corrective edits over broad rewrites.
- If everything looks good, say so plainly.
- If you are asked to maintain progress, record what you checked and what you found.
- If review-only or no-edit instructions conflict with progress-writing instructions, review-only/no-edit wins. Do not write `progress.md`; mention the conflict in your final review only if it matters.

## Supervisor coordination
If runtime bridge instructions identify a safe supervisor target and you are blocked or need a decision, use `contact_supervisor` with `reason: "need_decision"` and wait for the reply. Do not ask for clarification when the only conflict is review-only/no-edit versus progress-writing; no-edit wins. Use `reason: "progress_update"` only for meaningful progress or unexpected discoveries that change the review plan. Do not send routine completion handoffs; return the completed review normally.

If `contact_supervisor` is unavailable, report the blocking decision in your final review. Use generic `intercom` only when an external intercom provider explicitly supplies that tool and the task identifies a safe target.

# sof-pi Review Rubric

You are acting as a code reviewer for a proposed code change made by another engineer.

Below are default guidelines for determining what to flag. These are not the final word — if you encounter more specific guidelines elsewhere (in a developer message, user message, file, or project review guidelines appended below), those override these general instructions.

## Determining what to flag

Flag issues that:
1. Meaningfully impact the accuracy, performance, security, or maintainability of the code.
2. Are discrete and actionable (not general issues or multiple combined issues).
3. Don't demand rigor inconsistent with the rest of the codebase.
4. Were introduced in the changes being reviewed (not pre-existing bugs).
5. The author would likely fix if aware of them.
6. Don't rely on unstated assumptions about the codebase or author's intent.
7. Have provable impact on other parts of the code — it is not enough to speculate that a change may disrupt another part, you must identify the parts that are provably affected.
8. Are clearly not intentional changes by the author.
9. Be particularly careful with untrusted user input and follow the specific guidelines to review.
10. Treat silent local error recovery (especially parsing/IO/network fallbacks) as high-signal review candidates unless there is explicit boundary-level justification.

## Untrusted User Input

1. Be careful with open redirects, they must always be checked to only go to trusted domains (?next_page=...)
2. Always flag SQL that is not parametrized
3. In systems with user supplied URL input, http fetches always need to be protected against access to local resources (intercept DNS resolver!)
4. Escape, don't sanitize if you have the option (eg: HTML escaping)

## Comment guidelines

1. Be clear about why the issue is a problem.
2. Communicate severity appropriately - don't exaggerate.
3. Be brief - at most 1 paragraph.
4. Keep code snippets under 3 lines, wrapped in inline code or code blocks.
5. Use ```suggestion blocks ONLY for concrete replacement code (minimal lines; no commentary inside the block). Preserve the exact leading whitespace of the replaced lines.
6. Explicitly state scenarios/environments where the issue arises.
7. Use a matter-of-fact tone - helpful AI assistant, not accusatory.
8. Write for quick comprehension without close reading.
9. Avoid excessive flattery or unhelpful phrases like "Great job...".

## Review priorities

1. Surface critical non-blocking human callouts (migrations, dependency churn, auth/permissions, compatibility, destructive operations) at the end.
2. Prefer simple, direct solutions over wrappers or abstractions without clear value.
3. Treat back pressure handling as critical to system stability.
4. Apply system-level thinking; flag changes that increase operational risk or on-call wakeups.
5. Ensure that errors are always checked against codes or stable identifiers, never error messages.

## Fail-fast error handling (strict)

When reviewing added or modified error handling, default to fail-fast behavior.

1. Evaluate every new or changed `try/catch`: identify what can fail and why local handling is correct at that exact layer.
2. Prefer propagation over local recovery. If the current scope cannot fully recover while preserving correctness, rethrow (optionally with context) instead of returning fallbacks.
3. Flag catch blocks that hide failure signals (e.g. returning `null`/`[]`/`false`, swallowing JSON parse failures, logging-and-continue, or “best effort” silent recovery).
4. JSON parsing/decoding should fail loudly by default. Quiet fallback parsing is only acceptable with an explicit compatibility requirement and clear tested behavior.
5. Boundary handlers (HTTP routes, CLI entrypoints, supervisors) may translate errors, but must not pretend success or silently degrade.
6. If a catch exists only to satisfy lint/style without real handling, treat it as a bug.
7. When uncertain, prefer crashing fast over silent degradation.

## Required human callouts (non-blocking, at the very end)

After findings/verdict, you MUST append this final section:

## Human Reviewer Callouts (Non-Blocking)

Include only applicable callouts (no yes/no lines):

- **This change adds a database migration:** <files/details>
- **This change introduces a new dependency:** <package(s)/details>
- **This change changes a dependency (or the lockfile):** <files/package(s)/details>
- **This change modifies auth/permission behavior:** <what changed and where>
- **This change introduces backwards-incompatible public schema/API/contract changes:** <what changed and where>
- **This change includes irreversible or destructive operations:** <operation and scope>

Rules for this section:
1. These are informational callouts for the human reviewer, not fix items.
2. Do not include them in Findings unless there is an independent defect.
3. These callouts alone must not change the verdict.
4. Only include callouts that apply to the reviewed change.
5. Keep each emitted callout bold exactly as written.
6. If none apply, write "- (none)".

## Priority levels

Tag each finding with a priority level in the title:
- [P0] - Drop everything to fix. Blocking release/operations. Only for universal issues that do not depend on assumptions about inputs.
- [P1] - Urgent. Should be addressed in the next cycle.
- [P2] - Normal. To be fixed eventually.
- [P3] - Low. Nice to have.

## Output format

Provide your findings in a clear, structured format:
1. List each finding with its priority tag, file location, and explanation.
2. Findings must reference locations that overlap with the actual diff — don't flag pre-existing code.
3. Keep line references as short as possible (avoid ranges over 5-10 lines; pick the most suitable subrange).
4. Provide an overall verdict: "correct" (no blocking issues) or "needs attention" (has blocking issues).
5. Ignore trivial style issues unless they obscure meaning or violate documented standards.

All twelve findings from the latest UX-02 review were assigned to isolated
workers and integrated as exact owned deltas into the existing dirty checkout.
The parent caught and returned two implementation gaps (outside-focus ownership
and structured reply metadata defaults), plus an incorrectly labelled browser
reversal scenario, before accepting the handoffs for integration.

| --- | --- |
| P2-01 | Reactive visit pruning publishes the surviving active ID; component emission and Chrome contact-baseline checks use a differing sender. |
| P2-02 | A matching newly focused participant override survives the active-message handoff; direct Ravi focus is covered in App and Chrome. |
| P2-03 | Loading parks lost reader-owned focus on the article, preserving other surfaces and late user movement; component ownership/inert regressions and Chrome loading focus. |
| P2-04 | Pending foreground focus restoration handles A-ready → B-loading → A-ready; component coverage and a native-K Chrome case assert B is still loading before reversal. |
| P2-05 | Message/expansion/details commands require a ready matching displayed visit; loading-time O cannot mutate outgoing A. |
| P2-06 | Archive advancement uses captured action-time ordering, separate from frozen Back ordering; App and Chrome reorder regressions. |
| P2-07 | Reader arrow aliases removed; App checks no preventDefault/fetch, Chrome checks native Inbox scrolling and Activity no-fetch. |
| P2-08 | Contact copy statuses reset and fence by identity/context and newest activation; deferred success/failure, unavailability, identity change and reversed completions covered. |

| P2-12 | Hostile-body checks count/assert zero script nodes inside the reader, not Vite's legitimate page bootstrap; other literal-text/asset checks remain. |

structured metadata, not an RFC parser or evidence of native/provider behavior.

# Scoped shell/contact follow-up review

Reviewed the current files against `p2-code.patch` and the exact before-P2 snapshot, not the broader HEAD diff.

## Findings and verdict

**No qualifying remaining or introduced P0/P1/P2 defects found in the assigned delta. The scoped code looks good.**

**Overall verdict: correct.**

### Assigned findings

- **P2-02 — Resolved.** `src/App.vue:486–492` preserves only an override matching the newly active message and current account/conversation; null or mismatched identities clear it. The contact selector also rejects removed messages (`src/App.vue:285–290`). Reader keyboard-focus priority over hover remains intact (`src/components/ReaderView.vue:403–407`). The direct-focus regression genuinely focuses Ravi without first focusing the message summary (`tests/app.component.test.ts:1711–1738`). Chrome additionally verifies the integrated participant handoff (`tests/reader.rendered.test.ts:635–654`).

- **P2-06 — Resolved.** Archive captures copied, account-scoped action-time references before submitting the mutation (`src/App.vue:540–543`), then searches surviving next neighbors before previous ones (`src/App.vue:557–567`). It does not mutate frozen Back ordering. Current-target and late-receipt guards remain at `src/App.vue:523–526,545–547`; Activity-origin handling exits before Inbox advancement (`src/App.vue:549–552`). The App regression distinguishes action-time `[01,03,02,04]` from entry ordering and checks Back restoration (`tests/app.component.test.ts:1446–1472`); Chrome checks the reordered archive result (`tests/reader.rendered.test.ts:740–756`).

- **P2-07 — Resolved.** Reader navigation handles only `j/k` (`src/App.vue:736–745`), leaving arrows unprevented; list arrow aliases remain (`src/App.vue:753–763`). Both Inbox- and Activity-origin component cases assert no `preventDefault`, fetch, or conversation change (`tests/app.component.test.ts:1591–1631`). Chrome verifies actual native scrolling and unchanged fetch counts (`tests/reader.rendered.test.ts:703–737`).

- **P2-08 — Resolved.** Displayed identity/context changes clear status (`src/components/ContactPane.vue:38–46`); each explicit activation clears status and receives a monotonic token, with publication requiring both current identity/context and newest activation (`src/components/ContactPane.vue:52–61`). There is one clipboard write site (`:72`), with explicit unavailable/failure notices rather than fabricated success. Deferred success, identity changes, status resets, and reversed completions are covered at `tests/contact-pane.component.test.ts:57,70,83,104,122`. The modified catch is appropriate UI-boundary error translation; no retry, replay, mailbox mutation, or navigation was added.

- **P2-11 — Resolved.** The stale-response test now asserts changed read-02 content both before and after the old response settles (`tests/app.component.test.ts:1553–1566`). These are genuinely distinct payloads: `toDetail` copies the subject before the fixture delays delivery (`tests/reader.fixture.ts:250–253,331–338,358`), while replacement installs a new stored object (`:462`). Production request fencing remains unchanged (`src/composables/useMailbox.ts:188–205`).

### Immediate regression boundaries

The delta preserves editor/IME/modifier/editable/overlay exclusions, action-button exclusions, and central/contact inertness. Existing current-target, loading-action, late-receipt, latest-message reply-source, and no-unintended-write regressions remain present. No auto-read or new reply-triggering path was introduced.

## Validation and residual limits

No commands were executed during this read-only review. Inspected parent validation records report:

- All six repository commands passed; default UI: **274 passed, 15 opt-in skips**.
- Reader Chrome: **12 passed**, recorded shuffled invocation: **12 passed**; isolated anchor/scroller/reply cases and covered-focus checks passed.
- Default-C-locale row layout remains **1 passed / 1 failed** at unchanged assertion `tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts:442`. The exact pre-P2 snapshot reproduces the same failure; explicit en-GB passes both. This failure is **not introduced by this delta**.
- Native/WKWebView, VoiceOver, and platform clipboard verification remain pending. Synthetic fixture evidence does not establish production RFC/provider behavior.

**Merge verdict: OK with notes** — scoped delta only; not publication authorization.

# Reader-state follow-up review

Scope: P2-01, P2-03, P2-04 and P2-05, comparing current files against `p2-code.patch` and the exact before-P2 snapshot—not the broader HEAD patch. Review-only; no repository changes or commands executed by this reviewer.

## Findings

### [P2] Apply restoration ownership checks before the empty-visit fallback
**Location:** `src/components/ReaderView.vue:307–314`

On A-ready → B-loading → A-ready, if A now has no messages and the user moved focus to the persistent Close button or an outside control during loading, the new ownership guard is bypassed: the earlier empty/no-active fallback at lines 301–305 focuses the article first. `pendingFocusRestore` now forces this formerly same-key/no-focus path through that fallback. The parent-run differential probe confirmed the regression: **current failed both ownership assertions**, moving `reader-close` and `probe-outside` focus to `reader`; the **exact before-P2 snapshot passed both**. Apply the ownership check before either restoration target, and add empty-return ownership regressions. Evidence: `/tmp/email-os-ux02-p2-ya5mtc8s/probes/{ownership.probe.test.ts,current-ownership.log,before-ownership.log,results.json}`.

No additional qualifying P0/P1/P2 defects found in the assigned seam.

## Assigned findings

| ID | Status | Current code and test evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **P2-01** | **Resolved** | Visits are stored as reactive objects at `ReaderView.vue:359–368`, so pruning’s active-ID mutation reaches the emission watcher at `:399–401`. App resolves its contact baseline from that ID at `App.vue:268–278`. The differing-sender component regression at `tests/reader.component.test.ts:237–267` checks the emitted resolved ID and DOM focus; Chrome integration at `tests/reader.rendered.test.ts:611–632` checks removal of Ada’s message resolves focus and contact to `anon@example.test`. |
| **P2-03** | **Resolved** | Loading records prior reader ownership and schedules parking at `ReaderView.vue:333–349`. The delayed operation checks update sequence, surviving reader focus, outside focus and inert ancestry at `:262–274` and `:232–235`. Component cases at `tests/reader.component.test.ts:269–350` cover message teardown, persistent toolbar, outside/late-moved focus and inert behavior. Chrome asserts loading focus is the article at `tests/reader.rendered.test.ts:669–671`. |
| **P2-04** | **Not resolved** | Foreground restoration is correctly separated from `lastDataKey` through `pendingFocusRestore` at `ReaderView.vue:148–156` and `:372–378`; ordinary immediate reversal and toolbar ownership are covered at `tests/reader.component.test.ts:352–387`. The native case now explicitly asserts B remains loading immediately before real K at `tests/reader.rendered.test.ts:675–679`. However, the confirmed empty-return ownership regression above remains. |
| **P2-05** | **Resolved** | `displayedVisit()` requires ready state and matching conversation/open references at `ReaderView.vue:459–463`, using the identity check at `:163–168`. All five exposed message/details methods use it at `:522–568`. Component cases at `tests/reader.component.test.ts:389–440` verify loading commands cannot change outgoing expansion or dismiss saved hidden details; Chrome verifies loading-time O leaves expansion intact at `tests/reader.rendered.test.ts:672–685`. |

## Preservation and validation

- Original P1 scroll capture still occurs before null/loading teardown (`ReaderView.vue:330–335`), and restored message focus avoids reveal-scrolling over saved anchors (`:315–319`). Controlled-geometry regressions remain at `tests/reader.component.test.ts:536–599`; the real-Chrome round trip at `tests/reader.rendered.test.ts:559–608` checks exact scroll position and viewport geometry.
- Current-thread E/Shift+U message-toggle exceptions, toolbar exclusions and details Escape precedence remain intact in `App.vue:661–710,746–749`. Native Enter, E and Shift+U cases passed in the supplied Chrome log.
- Read parent validation artifacts: six repository gates passed; default UI **274 passed / 15 opt-in skipped**, including **22 ReaderView component tests**; reader Chrome **12 passed**, with another **12 passed** in the supplied shuffled run.
- The default-C-locale row-layout result remains **1 passed / 1 failed** at unchanged assertion `tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts:442`. The exact before-P2 snapshot reproduces it; explicit en-GB passes both. This is not an introduced finding.
- Native/WKWebView, VoiceOver and platform clipboard verification remain pending. Synthetic fixture results do not establish production RFC-parser or provider-security behavior.

**Overall verdict: needs attention.**

**Merge verdict: BLOCK**

**Location:** `tests/reader.rendered.test.ts:641–646`

The native Details-summary click already focuses m1 and publishes its active identity through `ReaderView.vue:673`, before Ravi receives focus. Parent-run Chrome observations confirmed that the original sequence still shows Ravi with the pre-P2 App handler restored in memory. Opening m1 details, returning native focus to m3, and then clicking Ravi discriminates correctly: current code shows Ravi; the old handler shows Ada. `/tmp/email-os-ux02-p2-ya5mtc8s/probes/current-native-contact.log` and `legacy-native-contact.log`; both observation runs exited 0. Their recorded states demonstrate the false-positive coverage without modifying main source.

- The immediate-reversal case is meaningful: `tests/reader.rendered.test.ts:666–679` delays both responses, asserts B is still loading with no subject immediately before native K, then checks restored focus and unchanged expansion. It is not merely a completed A → B → A roundtrip.

The before-P2 reproduction has the same failure; explicit en-GB passes both tests. This is **not introduced by this delta**, and the documentation preserves the failed run.
- Native/WKWebView, VoiceOver, platform clipboard, and provider behavior remain unverified. The documentation appropriately limits the fixture to canonical structured synthetic metadata—not RFC parsing or production security certification.

No other qualifying P0/P1/P2 defect was found in the assigned seam.

compatibility: Requires the `gh` CLI installed, on PATH, and authenticated. Verify with `gh auth status`; run `gh auth login` if not logged in.

# GitHub CLI (`gh`) Skill

Use this skill to interact with GitHub from the terminal using the `gh` CLI. Covers cloning repos for inspection/learning, checking GitHub Actions pipeline logs and statuses, and ad-hoc GitHub API/GraphQL calls.

## Setup

Ensure `gh` is installed and authenticated before running any commands.

```bash
gh --version         # current gh version
gh auth status       # show logged-in account, active status, token scopes
gh auth login        # interactive login flow (browser/device code)
gh auth refresh      # refresh token / request additional scopes
```

Auth state is stored in the OS keyring. `gh` also configures `git` to use the authenticated account for HTTPS pushes (`gh auth setup-git`).

## Global conventions

These flags apply to most commands and make `gh` scriptable/agent-safe:

| Flag | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `-R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO` | Run a command against a different repo than the cwd. Use instead of `cd`-ing into a clone. |
| `--json fields` | Output JSON with the specified fields (best for parsing). |
| `-q, --jq expression` | Filter JSON output with a jq expression. |
| `-t, --template string` | Format JSON output with a Go template (see `gh help formatting`). |
| `--web` / `-w` | Open the relevant page in the browser instead of printing. |
| `--help` | Show help for a command. |

**Automation pattern:** prefer `--json` (optionally with `-q`) for parsing, plain output for grepping. When targeting a repo you don't have checked out locally, use `-R owner/repo` instead of cloning just to inspect.

**Discovery:** every command supports `--help`. For a full reference run `gh help` or `gh help reference`.

## Cloning repositories (inspecting dependencies / learning)

`gh repo clone` resolves `OWNER/REPO` (or a full URL, or a bare repo name = your own account), uses your configured git protocol, and automatically wires up an `upstream` remote when the repo is a fork.

```bash
# Clone a dependency / third-party project to inspect
gh repo clone cli/cli                       # OWNER/REPO -> ./cli
gh repo clone cli/cli workspace/cli         # clone into a specific directory
gh repo clone https://github.com/cli/cli    # explicit URL (overrides git_protocol config)
gh repo clone git@github.com:cli/cli.git    # SSH URL

# Shallow / partial clones (faster for read-only inspection) — pass git flags after --
gh repo clone cli/cli -- --depth=1
gh repo clone cli/cli -- --depth=1 --filter=blob:none   # blobless clone

# When the repo is a fork, the parent is added as `upstream` (configurable)
gh repo clone octocat/Hello-World --upstream-remote-name=octocat
```

When you only want to *read* a repo without cloning, prefer `gh repo view` / `gh repo view --web` / `gh api` instead of cloning.

```bash
gh repo view cli/cli                    # README + metadata, no clone
gh repo view cli/cli --web             # open in browser
gh repo view cli/cli --json name,description,defaultBranchRef
```

## Finding repositories to inspect

```bash
# Search across GitHub (repos, code, issues, prs, commits)
gh search repos "cli github" --language go --sort stars --limit 20
gh search repos --owner cli            # repos owned by a user/org
gh search code "fn main" --repo cli/cli
gh search issues "panic on nil" --repo cli/cli --state open

# List repos you own / an org owns
gh repo list                           # your repos
gh repo list cli --limit 50           # an org's repos
gh repo list --fork --source          # filter forks/sources
```

## GitHub Actions: pipeline statuses and logs

Two command groups: `gh run` (individual workflow runs) and `gh workflow` (workflow definitions).

### Listing and viewing runs

```bash
gh run list                            # recent runs in the cwd repo
gh run list --limit 20                 # more runs
gh run list -R owner/repo              # runs in a different repo (no clone needed)
gh run list --workflow build.yml       # filter by workflow file
gh run list --branch main --status failure
gh run list --json databaseId,status,conclusion,headBranch,workflowName --limit 10

gh run view                            # interactively pick a run to view
gh run view 12345                      # view a specific run (summary + jobs)
gh run view 12345 -v                   # verbose: show job steps
gh run view 12345 -R owner/repo        # view a run in another repo
```

### Reading logs

```bash
gh run view 12345 --log                # full log for the run (all jobs)
gh run view 12345 --log-failed         # only failed steps (best for debugging CI)
gh run view --job 67890 --log          # log for a specific job
gh run view 12345 --web                # open the run in the browser
```

### Watching, rerunning, cancelling, downloading artifacts

```bash
gh run watch                          # interactively watch the latest run until it finishes
gh run watch 12345                    # watch a specific run (exit non-zero if it fails with --exit-status)
gh run watch 12345 --exit-status

gh run rerun 12345                    # rerun all failed jobs (or --failed)
gh run rerun 12345 --failed
gh run cancel 12345
gh run delete 12345
gh run download 12345                 # download artifacts to ./ by default
gh run download 12345 -D ./artifacts --name build-output
```

### Workflows

```bash
gh run list --workflow build.yml
gh workflow list                      # workflows defined in the repo
gh workflow view build.yml
gh workflow view build.yml --web
gh workflow run build.yml             # trigger a workflow_dispatch
gh workflow run build.yml --ref main -f environment=staging
gh workflow enable / disable build.yml
```

`gh run list` / `gh run view` accept `-R owner/repo`, so you can check pipeline status of a dependency or upstream repo **without cloning it** — useful for "is upstream CI green?" checks.

## Cross-cutting tips

- **No-clone inspection:** for read-only checks (status, README, releases, CI state), use `-R owner/repo` with `gh run list` / `gh repo view` / `gh release list` rather than cloning.
- **JSON + jq:** `--json` + `-q '.[] | .name'` is the most reliable way to extract specific fields.
- **Pipeline debugging flow:** `gh run list --status failure` → pick run id → `gh run view <id> --log-failed` to jump straight to failing step logs.
- **Branch context:** most `gh run` commands support `--branch`, `--event`, `--status`, `--workflow` filters.
- **Default repo:** `gh repo set-default` marks a repo as default for the cwd, so `gh pr` / `gh issue` / `gh run` resolve without `-R`. Useful when working inside a clone.

## Other commonly used commands (summary)

- **`gh pr`** — list/view/checkout/diff/merge/review PRs (`gh pr checkout 123`, `gh pr view --web`, `gh pr diff`, `gh pr checks`).
- **`gh issue`** — list/view/create/close issues.
- **`gh release`** — list/view/create/download releases (`gh release download`).
- **`gh gist`** — create/list/view gists (paste snippets).
- **`gh browse`** — open the current repo / a PR / an issue / a file in the browser.
- **`gh status`** — overview of relevant issues/PRs/notifications across your repos.
- **`gh api`** — make an authenticated REST v3 or GraphQL v4 request directly (escape hatch for anything not exposed by a subcommand).
- **`gh search`** — search repos, code, issues, PRs, commits across all of GitHub.

### `gh api` escape hatch

```bash
gh api repos/cli/cli                       # GET a REST endpoint
gh api repos/cli/cli/releases/latest --jq .tag_name
gh api graphql -f query='query { viewer { login } }'
gh api repos/cli/cli/contents/README.md    # fetch a file's metadata/content
gh api -X POST repos/cli/cli/labels -f name=foo -f color=ff0000
```

Placeholders `{owner}`, `{repo}`, `{branch}` are filled from the cwd repo (or `GH_REPO`). Prefer the dedicated subcommands when they exist; reach for `gh api` only for endpoints `gh` doesn't wrap.

## Reference

- Built-in help: `gh --help`, `gh <command> --help`, or `gh help <command>` for prose.
- Full reference: `gh help reference`.
- Formatting/JSON: `gh help formatting`.
- Exit codes: `gh help exit-codes`.
- Manual: https://cli.github.com/manual

arguments.content:
## Summary

Implement the UX-02 conversation-reader slice on top of UX-01:

- Visit-scoped message focus, expansion, details and reading-position state; newest-message initial focus; nonwrapping `N/P`, `O` and `Shift+O` commands.
- Inbox-origin `J/K` navigation with original-entry Back restoration, action-time archive advancement, and strict Activity-origin conversation-navigation no-ops. Reader arrows retain native scrolling.
- Identity-qualified participant context and explicit copy-only contact controls, including asynchronous clipboard-result fencing.
- Preserve current-thread action targeting, latest-source reply safeguards, plain-text bodies, no automatic mark-read, overlay/editor guards, and existing provider/permission boundaries.
- Address all 12 accepted UX-02 P2 follow-ups, including pruning publication, loading/reversal focus ownership, source-derived synthetic reply metadata, distinguishable stale-response tests, and independent rendered cases with reader-scoped script assertions.

The fresh review found two additional gaps in these fixes (empty-return focus ownership and false-positive native participant coverage); both were corrected and independently rechecked. Final scoped review verdict: **OK with notes**. This is not a blanket native-platform or no-defect claim.

Implementation contract, reconstruction choices, validation evidence and remaining limits: [docs/ux-02-conversation-reader.md](docs/ux-02-conversation-reader.md).

## Validation — executed locally against the committed content

All six configured repository checks passed:

- [x] `mise run test:core`
- [x] `mise run check:contract`
- [x] `mise run lint:core`
- [x] `mise run test:ui` — **276 passed / 15 opt-in browser tests skipped**, 16 files
- [x] `mise run typecheck`
- [x] `mise run build:web`

Opt-in real-Chrome validation used the existing environment gates, a cached browser, ephemeral Vite servers and temporary profiles:

- [x] Reader suite: **12 passed**, plus **12 passed** in a shuffled run.
- [x] Anchor, self-scroller, reply-exit and corrected participant-handoff cases each passed independently (**1 passed / 11 filtered skips** per invocation).
- [x] Covered-surface focus suite: **1 passed**.
- [x] Empty-return differential ownership replay: **2 passed**, retaining toolbar/outside focus; positive owned-empty fallback remains covered.
- [x] Revised durable participant case detects the removed-fix mutation: restoring only the old App handler through an in-memory Vite transform produces the expected **Ada instead of Ravi** failure. No production source was modified for that negative control.
- [x] Existing row-layout suite: **2 passed with explicit en-GB locale** (conditional result; see default-locale failure below).

Application/test hashes remained unchanged during the final independent checks and read-only recheck. No Rust, generated DTO/wire/IPC, provider scopes, native permissions, dependencies, or framework/configuration changes.

## Known limitations / pending verification

- **Existing default-locale row-layout failure remains:** under the VM's `LANG=C.UTF-8`, `tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts:442` reports **1 passed / 1 failed** because it expects `30 Sept 2001` while the environment renders `Sep 30, 2001`. The exact pre-P2 source snapshot reproduces the same failure. With `LANG=en_GB.UTF-8 LC_ALL=en_GB.UTF-8 LANGUAGE=en_GB`, both tests pass. The failed default-locale result is preserved, not relabelled green; unrelated locale cleanup is excluded from this PR.
- Native fixture/WKWebView keyboard, scroll and focus behavior remains pending. This Linux VM lacks the GTK/WebKit development prerequisites for native startup checks.
- VoiceOver/assistive-technology and platform clipboard verification remain pending.
- Browser evidence uses synthetic in-memory fixtures only: no real accounts, credentials, mail, sending, or provider behavior was exercised. The reply fixture is a bounded approximation over canonical structured metadata, not an RFC parser or provider-security certification.
- No screenshot/pixel-parity or verified Superhuman-fidelity claim.

Closes the implementation and scoped automated-review work for UX-02; native/platform acceptance is not claimed complete.
